NEGATIVO sense(b): headline result IS that dedicated memory systems underperform naive full-context ICL -- systematic negative evidence about current memory-management mechanisms. F confirms F_screening (NEGATIVO) + adds RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO (gain metric), FIDELIDAD (concept-drift/staleness design), COSTO (explicit $/rollout table).

title: Manufactured Confidence: How Memory Consolidation Turns Hearsay into Confident Facts
benchmarks: own constructed diagnostic harness (running-total computation + budget-approval agent + access-control agent); tested against mem0, LangMem, and a verbatim VectorStoreRetrieverMemory control
fallos_mitigaciones: 'Manufactured confidence': fact-extraction consolidation (mem0, LangMem) rewrites a casual, hedged remark into a confident, dated assertion that later agent steps obey like a verified fact. TWO sources: (1) natural staleness -- a once-true hedge goes stale and its correction is never stored (no attacker needed), producing confident-wrong grants on 0.69 (mem0)/0.75 (LangMem) of requests (Table3); (2) adversarial injection -- one planted sentence is laundered into an authoritative dated fact by BOTH real products (100% laundering rate) vs 0% on the verbatim control (Table7), yielding 0.72 unauthorized-grant with no defense (Table6). 'The obvious fixes fail': a passive 'unverified' tag is leaky and provider-dependent (0.00-0.81, Table5/6); an active 'do not trust this' instruction (distrust) stops the cascade everywhere (0.00 wrong-decision) but by ABDICATION not discrimination -- it escalates 100% of requests even on CORRECT memory (Table8). The fix that actually works: preserve tentative phrasing AT THE STORE (do not de-hedge; hygiene, not an adversarial defense) PLUS add a redundant/second source (authoritative directory) to verify against, which restores correct discrimination (wrong-grant 0.00, zero escalation, Table2) even under an assertive poisoned memory.
cita: Kwon (2026). Manufactured Confidence: How Memory Consolidation Turns Hearsay into Confident Facts.
notes: S1/Fig1: memory products (mem0, LangMem) extract conversation into stored 'facts' retrieved by later steps -> representacion=DOCS-ARCHIVOS (extracted text facts), retrieval=EMBEDDINGS (paper explicitly probes the underlying BGE-small vector: hedge IS linearly recoverable there, balanced accuracy 1.00, so the loss happens at the LLM-rewrite/consolidation step, not the embedding -- CONSOLIDACION is the operation under study, title-level). S3 cross of 7 framings (bare/attributed/forged-authority all confident vs 4 hedge types) isolates that the agent obeys CONFIDENCE not SOURCE (Table1: confident framings grant 0.81 regardless of attribution/forged 'system of record'; hedges collapse grants near 0.00). Table3: with an in-context correction present, memory reconciles/downgrades (ACTUALIZACION, grants 0/16); without one, staleness persists (grants 0.69-0.75) -- direct fidelidad_procedencia=SI evidence (this IS the paper's core axis: staleness + provenance-blindness). Table2: redundant authoritative-directory source restores discrimination (wrong-grant 0.00). 5 models tested (Claude Sonnet/Haiku, Llama-70B, GPT-4o-mini, Qwen-72B), all deterministic at temp=0 -- systematic controlled manipulation of framing/defense/source = ABLATION per calibration vara E (not a standard task BENCHMARK-E2E). handoff=CONTENIDO: 'LLM agents carry conclusions across steps AND SESSIONS in compressed memory' -- the manufactured-confident fact IS the content that travels. NEGATIVO sense(b) + SEGURIDAD (cs.CR; explicit memory-poisoning/injection attack, 'PoisonedRAG corrupts what is retrieved; we study a memory-store variant that corrupts what is recorded'). F confirms F_screening (FIDELIDAD;NEGATIVO) + adds CONSOLIDACION, SEGURIDAD, WRITE.

title: ManimAgent: Self-Evolving Multimodal Agents for Visual Education
benchmarks: own paper-section Manim-animation dataset (memory-building 39 tasks / fixed-probe 33 / cross-test 40); baselines: Manim-code RAG, Random EMB, VLM-reflection-only
fallos_mitigaciones: 'Cross-task forgetting' (S1, Fig.1): a reflection pipeline closes the INTRA-task loop (observe error, revise, retry) but every lesson paid for in tokens is thrown away before the next task starts, so a structurally similar future task repeats the same layout/formula mistake and pays the full reflection cost again. Mitigated by the dual-channel Episodic Memory Bank: positive channel M+ = soft Reference Examples (success rationale, write-gated at score>=85), negative channel M- = hard Known Pitfalls (validated failure->success transitions, causal-attribution gated, requires score delta>=5 for visual transitions) injected into the Coder prompt on retrieval. Table1/Fig3: EMB@200 improves blind-human Pass@1 to 84.9% (vs 68.5% VLM-reflection-only, 69.6% Random-EMB, and even 83.3% for a strong matched-budget static Manim-code RAG baseline) while cutting reflection rounds to 6.5 (vs 12.2 baseline).
cita: Jiang et al. (2026). ManimAgent: Self-Evolving Multimodal Agents for Visual Education.
notes: S3.1-3.3: dual-channel Episodic Memory Bank M=M+ union M-, backed by 1 SQLite table + 2 per-polarity Faiss IndexFlatIP vector indices (representacion=HIBRIDA); M+ records a success rationale (soft prior, PROCEDIMENTAL template) per high-scoring scene (u*>=theta_high=85, ADMISION); M- records a structured 'validated failure pattern' (EPISODICA, causal-attribution-gated: crash->success text transitions accepted unconditionally, visual transitions require delta_fail>=5 score-margin, ADMISION) via LLM-distilled lessons (NOT literal diffs -- explicit CONSOLIDACION step). Retrieval by task-embedding cosine similarity (all-MiniLM-L6-v2, EMBEDDINGS), disjoint per-polarity indices (a query on M+ never returns M- records). Explicit six named agents (Storyboarder, Coder, text Reviewer, VLM Reviewer, Visual Reviser, Lesson Distiller/Rationale Writer) sharing the single EMB -> multiagente=SI (paper self-describes as 'self-evolving multi-agent system'). S3.3 'Provenance, deduplication, and embedder pinning': provenance block (run id, scene id, extraction source, transition ordinal, before/after scores) for write-time dedup; embedder identity PINNED at first creation, 'refused on reopen if a different encoder is requested' preventing silent re-embedding drift between writes/reads -> fidelidad_procedencia=SI. 'No capacity, no eviction... grow monotonically' -- explicitly NO OLVIDO mechanism. Table1 ablations (channel isolation No-M+/No-M-/No-memory, gate stringency, Top-1 retrieval depth, Weak-VLM reviewer) directly measure read-side utility -> mide_lectura=SI/RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO. NEGATIVO sense(a): M- is explicitly a negative/failure channel storing 'Known Pitfalls' (validated failures) as first-class memory content. F confirms F_screening (NEGATIVO;RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO) + adds CONSOLIDACION (LLM-distilled lessons), FIDELIDAD (provenance/embedder-pinning), MULTIAGENTE, WRITE.

title: MemDelta: Controlled Baselines and Hidden Confounds in Agent Memory Evaluation
benchmarks: LongMemEval-S (500 questions, 50+ sessions/user, 3 model families); strategies compared: S0-no-memory, S_rand-random-RAG, S1-full-context, S4-RAG-MiniLM, S4b-RAG-cloud-embedding, S2-agent-scratchpad self-memory, S3-Mem0
fallos_mitigaciones: Agent self-memory (scratchpad) failure: the 4,096-token scratchpad 'collapses on multi-session questions (3.3%), where it cannot retain enough detail across 50+ sessions' -- 'compression is a wager: each write decides what future questions will not need' (S4.1); self-memory (42%) underperforms basic retrieval (47%). No mitigation for this is implemented; the paper's own contribution is methodological, not architectural: fix the embedding model across comparisons, stratify by model family, and report write-path cost before attributing gains to memory architecture (S1/S6).
cita: Wang (2026). MemDelta: Controlled Baselines and Hidden Confounds in Agent Memory Evaluation.
notes: Pure measurement/methodology paper (Table1: 7 strategies S0/Srand/S1/S4/S4b/S2/S3, no own memory architecture) -> mem_tipos/representacion/operaciones/trigger/retrieval=NA. S3 protocol: 6 controlled pairwise comparisons each varying EXACTLY one factor (Table2): S4 vs S4b isolates embedding choice ONLY (+6.2pp, p=0.004, identical code/chunking/top-k/model/judge) -> this IS a direct retrieval-quality measurement -> mide_lectura=SI/RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO. Headline finding (S4.1, matches abstract): Mem0 beats MiniLM-RAG by +11pp but LOSES to cloud-embedding RAG by -1.2pp -- 'one variable flips the conclusion' (Fig1 case study) -> NEGATIVO sense(b), core architectural-memory-gain claims are often embedding confounds not real memory-method wins. S4.2: same S1-vs-S4 comparison gives 3 DIFFERENT conclusions across GPT-4o-mini/Sonnet/Gemini (Sonnet refuses 63% of full-context queries) -> model-behavior confound. S4.5 knowledge-update question type requires 'identify which of several conflicting facts is the most recent' -- a direct staleness-resolution axis where full-context (72%) beats retrieval (62-63%) -> fidelidad_procedencia=SI. Table6/7: write-path cost audited as first-class metric (S0 $0/0s -> S4b $0.01/60s -> S2 $0.34/90min/~250 LLM calls -> S3(Mem0) $0.50+/120min/1000+ calls) -> COSTO-TOKENS+LATENCIA; on 88 matched instances Mem0(72.7%) does NOT beat cloud-RAG(73.9%, p=1.0) at 50x the cost. F confirms F_screening (FIDELIDAD;NEGATIVO) + adds RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO, COSTO.

title: MemSyco-Bench: Benchmarking Sycophancy in Agent Memory
benchmarks: MemSyco-Bench (own, 5 task categories); systems evaluated: No-Memory, Full-Dialog, NaiveRAG, Mem0, A-Mem, LightMem, MemGPT, MemoryBank, SuperMemory (2 backbones: Qwen3-8B, DeepSeek-V4-Flash)
fallos_mitigaciones: 'Memory-induced sycophancy' (S3.1): retrieved historical user beliefs/preferences/statements can be outdated, out-of-scope, or contradicted by objective evidence, yet the agent treats them as evidentiary signal and shifts its answer toward the remembered claim instead of following current evidence -- distinct from ordinary sycophancy because the source is retrieved MEMORY (possibly absent from the current query), the failure extends to scope-violation/evidence-override (not just agreement), and it persists/repeats across sessions. No mitigation is proposed by this benchmark (diagnostic only): S2.1 preliminary study shows adding a memory snippet drops factual accuracy (largest drop DeepSeek-V4-Flash 56.1%->40.2%) while sycophancy rate rises (24.3%->52.3%); Table1 main results show EVERY evaluated memory system (Mem0/A-Mem/LightMem/MemGPT/MemoryBank/SuperMemory) INCREASES sycophancy rate on Objective-Fact-Judgment relative to a No-Memory floor and DECREASES accuracy relative to No-Memory on both backbones.
cita: Xiang et al. (2026). MemSyco-Bench: Benchmarking Sycophancy in Agent Memory.
notes: Pure diagnostic benchmark (no own memory mechanism, evaluates 8 systems + No-Memory/Full-Dialog controls) -> mem_tipos/representacion/operaciones/trigger/retrieval=NA. S1/S3.2: explicit design intent 'shifting the evaluation focus from RETRIEVAL SUCCESS to POST-RETRIEVAL memory use' -- S2.2 preliminary error-cause analysis on LongMemEval/LoCoMo/STALE/PersonaMem shows their errors are 47.4-66.1% retrieval-failure(R-/A-) vs only 5.8-13.7% post-retrieval-failure(R+/A-), motivating this benchmark's post-retrieval focus -> mide_lectura=SI/RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO (measures what happens AFTER successful retrieval). 5 task categories (S3.2): Objective-Fact-Judgment, Contextual-Scope-Control, Memory-Evidence-Conflict (suppress inapplicable memory); Valid-Memory-Selection ('identify the currently valid preference when a user's preference has been updated, reversed, or replaced' -- direct staleness-tracking), Personalized-Memory-Use (valid personalization) -> fidelidad_procedencia=SI (Valid-Memory-Selection is exactly a staleness/update-tracking axis). Metrics (S3.4): Generation Accuracy (all tasks) + Sycophancy Rate (first 3 tasks) + Memory-Use Metrics (Correct-Mem-Use / Outdated-Mem for last 2 tasks) -> bespoke OTRA metrics alongside EXITO. Table1 (Qwen3-8B): Objective-Fact-Judgment Sycophancy Rate jumps from an effective ~0.67(no-memory floor) to 69-99% with ANY memory system present; accuracy drops from 49.12%(No-Memory) to 26-36% across all 7 memory conditions -- systematic degradation from adding memory. F confirms F_screening (FIDELIDAD;NEGATIVO) + adds RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO (post-retrieval-use focus).

title: When Not to Write Memory: Governing False Promotion from Correlated Agent Traces
benchmarks: GovMem-Bench (own controlled synthetic); project-internal real-trace subset (120 human-gold candidates / 79 recorded traces + project reports); external SWE-agent/OpenHands trajectory stress tests (2x50-trajectory pilots + a 361-candidate V2 pool + a 133-row human-adjudicated high-impact packet)
fallos_mitigaciones: 'False promotion from correlated agent traces': repeated observations across agents are NOT necessarily independent evidence -- the same claim may be copied from a shared source, induced by a shared prompt/tool, stale under a new environment, adversarial, or valid only in a narrower scope (S1). Naive promotion turns 'long-term memory into a persistence layer for correlated errors.' Mitigated by GovMem: (1) dependency-aware support estimation (groups observations by dependency structure -- copied/shared-prompt/shared-tool observations do NOT count as independent votes), (2) counterevidence retrieval + scope-compatibility check, (3) promote/reject/needs-review triage. Controlled GovMem-Bench: reduces false promotion 0.597(raw)->0.040 preserving 0.960 recall. Project-internal real traces: reduces false promotion 0.371(source+scope)->0.032 but held-out FP remains 0.111, recall drops to 0.448, review burden 0.692 -- i.e. the safety gain is largely reviewer-routing, not automatic promotion. CRITICALLY, final human adjudication of a 133-row high-impact external packet found ZERO safe automatic promotions and REJECTED ALL 11 of GovMem's own local verification-gate positives (mistaken pytest boilerplate/file-dumps/non-reusable-debugging-traces for verified evidence) -- so even GovMem's own output does not survive independent human review, a genuinely negative finding about the method's own limits, not just naive baselines.
cita: Qi et al. (2026). When Not to Write Memory: Governing False Promotion from Correlated Agent Traces.
notes: S3 GovMem = a conservative write-path AUDITOR side-agent, task-independent from the agents that write traces: task agents emit traces -> a memory proposer normalizes candidate memories (aggregated similar observations + provenance metadata: source, prompt family, parent event, environment, trust) -> GovMem's 4-step audit (form candidate -> estimate dependency-aware support via a PROVENANCE/DEPENDENCY GRAPH among observations, NOT sample-similarity -> retrieve+classify counterevidence & check scope -> output promote/reject/needs-review) BEFORE the write reaches long-term storage -> operaciones=WRITE;ADMISION (this IS the paper's central operation), retrieval=GRAFO (dependency lineage graph traversal for counterevidence), mem_tipos=PROCEDIMENTAL(reusable lessons)+EPISODICA(trace-derived observations), consistent with related-work framing (ExpeL/LEGOMem-style reusable memories). Index Terms explicitly list 'multi-agent systems' + repeated-multi-agent-observation framing throughout ('Multi-agent traces: A observes X, B repeats X, C: stale X', Fig1) -> multiagente=SI. Table III (GovMem-Bench, controlled synthetic mechanism experiments: true-independent/true-copied/false-copied/false-correlated/stale/adversarial/out-of-scope candidate types) is the ABLATION evidence; Table IV/VIII (real-trace + 133-row external human-adjudication) is BENCHMARK-E2E. GovMem-verified is NOT strictly dominant: 'review-all-correlated' baseline nearly matches its internal false-promotion (0.033 vs 0.032) with HIGHER recall (0.881 vs 0.448) and LOWER review burden (0.492 vs 0.692) -- 'GovMem should be read as one point in a risk-control design space,' explicitly NOT claiming universal dominance. NEGATIVO sense(b): the paper's OWN headline external result is that surface verification and repeated trace evidence are insufficient for safe automatic promotion, even under the proposed governance mechanism. F confirms F_screening (WRITE;FIDELIDAD;NEGATIVO) + adds MULTIAGENTE, SEGURIDAD (adversarial candidate type tested; evidence-governance/provenance framing explicitly parallels memory-poisoning defense literature, cites A-MemGuard).

title: Experience to Competence Without Weight Updates: Pre-Registered Falsifiable Gates for Agent Memory
benchmarks: own pre-registered gate suite M0-M4: synthetic-facts recall (M0/M1), consolidation stress test (M2), brain-vs-RAG controlled comparison (M3), hidden-rule-discovery agentic task (M4, 60 episodes)
fallos_mitigaciones: TWO mechanisms explicitly KILLED by pre-registered gates, not salvaged: (1) Repetition-weighted ranking VIOLATES cue-specificity -- 'a distractor at sim=0.87 with strength 4 outranks the correct singleton at 0.95' (10/10 first failures inspected); loses to vanilla cosine RAG by -0.440 (multiplicative scoring) and -0.180 (cue-gated tie-breaking, delta=0.07 band); 'as pre-declared, strength ranking was removed from the default system' -- no fix attempted, the mechanism was simply killed. (2) Cosine-only deduplication is 'structurally unsound': validated same-fact paraphrase similarities (median 0.83) completely overlap same-template-distractor similarities (median 0.87) -- 'no threshold exists.' Mitigated by adding an LLM same-fact judge (12/12 on a probe set) instead of relying on embedding threshold alone, and by BANNING LLM-paraphrase summarization during consolidation (observed 'inventing field contents' / corrupting exact values) in favor of verbatim-text retention -- 'verbatim beats gist, twice' (both M2 consolidation and M4 lesson-writing).
cita: Raviotta (2026). Experience to Competence Without Weight Updates: Pre-Registered Falsifiable Gates for Agent Memory.
notes: S3: memory = SQLite graph over a plain-text vault; nodes are episodic/semantic memories (mem_tipos) with embedding+strength-counter+archived-flag; edges reinforced on co-recall, decay over time, dropped below threshold (OLVIDO) -> representacion=HIBRIDA (graph+embeddings). Same-fact judge gates writes (ADMISION); re-exposures bump strength / create edge instead of duplicate (ACTUALIZACION); nightly selective-consolidation cycle fuses re-exposure-connected clusters into ONE semantic node keeping verbatim text of the strongest member (CONSOLIDACION, explicit CHECKPOINT trigger); episodics archived not deleted. 5 pre-registered falsifiable gates (floor=no-memory arm, ceiling=oracle arm, bootstrap 95% CIs, PASS/PARTIAL/KILL fixed BEFORE runs) -- M0 establishes recall utility (naked 0.00 -> memory 0.98), M1 finds a repetition-learning-curve LATER shown (M3) to be self-inflicted interference -> mide_lectura=SI/RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO is the paper's entire methodological core. M4 (main result, matches abstract): frozen 9B agent + memory converts verbatim API-error lessons into procedural competence, first-try success 0.45->1.00 over 2 blocks of 20 unseen episodes vs memoryless control flat at 0.00 for all 60, oracle 0.95; seed replication 3/3 on the categorical transfer effect (memory>>control), 1/3 on within-run curve significance at n=20/block -- reported HONESTLY as PARTIAL where applicable. NEGATIVO BOTH senses: (a) 'we report everything: two clean passes, two kills of mechanisms we had previously celebrated' (explicit negative-results publication, rare in the field per abstract); (b) systematic negative evidence that popular mechanisms (strength-weighted ranking, embedding-only dedup) actively HURT vs a trivial baseline. F confirms F_screening (CONSOLIDACION;NEGATIVO) + adds FIDELIDAD (verbatim-vs-gist corruption findings), PROCEDIMENTAL, RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO, WRITE.

title: R2D2: Remembering, Replaying and Dynamic Decision Making with a Reflective Agentic Memory
benchmarks: WebArena
fallos_mitigaciones: 'Rapid forgetting of potentially valuable experiences': prior web-agent methods 'discard incoming trajectories immediately after a single episode,' impeding future decision-making (S1). Navigation failures account for ~60% of web-agent errors (Fig.6) because agents operate under an 'Unknown MDP' with limited visibility into action outcomes before acting. Mitigated by the Remember paradigm: a replay-buffer directed graph G=(O,E) of visited webpages/actions transforms the task into a 'Known MDP,' and A* search (LLM-provided heuristic h(o)) over this cached graph 'substantially reduces navigation failures' (Fig.6 error analysis: R2D2 vs vanilla ReACT trajectory inspection on 60 queries). The Reflect paradigm then addresses the remaining execution failures once navigation is no longer the bottleneck, storing corrective rationale + truncated-to-error trajectory in the reflective memory.
cita: Huang et al. (2025). R2D2: Remembering, Replaying and Dynamic Decision Making with a Reflective Agentic Memory.
notes: S3.2 Remember paradigm: replay-buffer graph (nodes=webpage observations incl. root o0, edges=(action, transition); stores DIFFS between consecutive observations, not full state) -> GRAFO; A* search (Algorithm1) with LLM-derived heuristic estimating subtree relevance selects candidate trajectories, LLM ranks final P*. S3.3 Reflect paradigm: for execution failures, LLM identifies the first erroneous action, truncates trajectory to correct prefix, generates a rationale, stores both in reflective memory. S3.4 Reflective Memory = key-value store, query encoded via dense embedding (MiniLM, retriv framework) as key (EMBEDDINGS), corrected/truncated trajectory+insight as value; TWO explicit ops: Lookup (nearest-key retrieval) and 'Update: if a newly truncated trajectory provides a more accurate or enriched reflection for an existing query, the memory updates the current value... R2D2 uses an LLM to make such decision' (ACTUALIZACION, DISCRECIONAL-LLM trigger for the update DECISION itself, layered on an EVENTO-DETERMINISTA pipeline stage). Results (Table1, matches abstract): R2D2 27.3% overall SR on WebArena vs ReACT 13.1%/Tree-Search 19.0%/LATS 22.5%/AR 23.4%/BrowserGym 23.5% (best baseline); ~50% navigation-error reduction + 3x task-completion increase claimed in abstract. S4.3 ablation studies remove Remember/Reflect paradigms individually (Fig.5) -> mide_lectura=SI/RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO. S4.4/Limitations: Table2 average-steps-per-task (ITERACION) explicit; full WebArena pass costs ~$200 GPT-4o usage (COSTO-TOKENS); step-count used as inference-latency proxy (LATENCIA). No multi-agent sharing (single ReACT-based agent) -> multiagente=NO. NEGATIVO sense(a)-adjacent: Reflect paradigm explicitly analyzes and stores insight distilled FROM failed/erroneous trajectories. F confirms F_screening (NEGATIVO;RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO) + adds COSTO (explicit $200/pass + step/latency accounting), PROCEDIMENTAL, WRITE.

title: SWE-Exp: Experience-Driven Software Issue Resolution
benchmarks: SWE-Bench Verified (500 human-verified GitHub issues)
fallos_mitigaciones: Memoryless agents suffer three inefficiencies (S1): (1) redundant exploration (retry ineffective trajectories across similar issues), (2) inability of knowledge transfer (discard successful insights -- workflows, code patterns, contextual factors -- after each session), (3) lack of strategic evolution (no compounding expertise over time). Mitigated by the multi-facet Experience Bank distilled from BOTH successful AND failed trajectories: failure trajectories carry explicit failure-cause metadata (incorrect localization / flawed modification strategy / insufficient problem comprehension, S3.2) enabling targeted extraction of negative patterns alongside positive ones. RQ2 ablation (Table2, DeepSeek-V3-0324) confirms both facets independently help and combine: full SWE-Exp 42.0% vs w/o-Comprehension-Experience 38.8% vs w/o-Modification-Experience 39.4% vs w/o-Dual-Agent 39.8%.
cita: Chen et al. (2026). SWE-Exp: Experience-Driven Software Issue Resolution.
notes: S3.1-3.3 four-stage OFFLINE pipeline: (1) collect repair trajectories (success+failure) from diverse repos, each tuple <directive,action,state,feedback>, annotated success/failure + failure-cause metadata; (2) Experiencer agent DISTILLS raw (lengthy/noisy/problem-specific) trajectories into 2 facets -- Comprehension Experience (perspective: how the issue was understood) + Modification Experience (generalized repair strategy) -- explicit CONSOLIDACION/abstraction step; (3) offline embedding+storage in a vector-database Experience Bank, indexed by issue_type+description (representacion=VECTOR). S3.4 online reuse: dual-agent architecture (Instructor=high-level strategy, Assistant=low-level execution) sharing retrieved experience -> multiagente=SI; before each MCTS decision node, top-N retrieved by vector similarity (EMBEDDINGS) then a RerankerAgent selects top-K (RANKING) -- integrated as contextual guidance at MCTS decision points, not a one-shot injection. Results (matches abstract): Pass@1 73.0% on SWE-Bench Verified w/ Claude 4 Sonnet, SOTA among open-source agent frameworks. Table3 Cost Analysis (S6.3): token cost 203.3K vs 189.1K baseline(SWE-Search), API cost $0.13 vs $0.12, wall time 15min49s vs 12min37s, retrieval+rerank overhead ~37.5s/instance -> COSTO-TOKENS+LATENCIA, explicit conclusion 'substantial performance gains achieved with minimal additional cost.' RQ2 ablation (Table2) isolates read-side utility of each experience facet -> mide_lectura=SI/RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO. NEGATIVO sense(a): failure trajectories explicitly annotated+stored with failure-cause metadata as first-class content for targeted extraction. F confirms F_screening (NEGATIVO;WRITE;RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO) + adds CONSOLIDACION, COSTO, MULTIAGENTE, PROCEDIMENTAL.

title: ReasoningBank: Scaling Agent Self-Evolving with Reasoning Memory
benchmarks: WebArena, Mind2Web, SWE-Bench-Verified
fallos_mitigaciones: LLM-as-a-judge correctness signal used to label success/failure is potentially noisy/unreliable when tasks are ambiguous or the judge errs (Limitations S.E); no correction mechanism beyond claimed empirical robustness -- paper suggests (not implements) stronger verifiers/human-in-the-loop/ensemble judgment as future mitigation.
cita: Ouyang et al. (2025). ReasoningBank: Scaling Agent Self-Evolving with Reasoning Memory.
notes: S3.2 memory items = title+description+content distilled via LLM-as-judge from BOTH successful and failed trajectories (Fig2); retrieval=EMBEDDINGS (gemini-embedding-001, top-k cosine, default k=1); operaciones=WRITE(extraction)+CONSOLIDACION('simple addition operation' into RB, S3.2/AppA.2) -> representacion=VECTOR (embedding-indexed structured items). Table1: RB beats No-Memory/Synapse/AWM on WebArena (+8.3/+7.2/+4.6 SR by backbone) + fewer steps (up to -1.6 vs baselines); Table3 Mind2Web cross-task/website/domain gains largest in cross-domain; Table2 SWE-Bench-Verified +4.6/+3.4pp resolve rate. AppC.1 Fig13 ablates number-of-retrieved-experiences (k) -> mide_lectura=SI/RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO. AppC.2 Table5 token-consumption breakdown (+~4.3% vs No-Memory) -> COSTO-TOKENS; Step metric=ITERACION. Fig7 ablates removing failure trajectories from induction -> NEGATIVO sense(a) (paper's OWN contribution is learning from BOTH success+failure, contrasted with prior success-only baselines). Limitations S.E: LLM-as-judge correctness signal is noisy/unverified, no ground-truth mitigation beyond claimed robustness -> fallos_mitigaciones. Single-agent (BrowserGym/bash-only ReAct loop) -> multiagente=NO. F confirms F_screening (NEGATIVO;WRITE;RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO;CONSOLIDACION), no change.

title: From Knowledge to Noise: CTIM-Rover and the Pitfalls of Episodic Memory in Software Engineering Agents
benchmarks: SWE-bench Verified (45-sample stratified test subset)
fallos_mitigaciones: Noisy/irrelevant CTIM items injected without relevance filtering bias the agent toward wrong actions (Fig3 'clean'-item case; an arbitrary 'GRANDMA LIKES PASTA' item also alters an unrelated outcome) -- an over-retention/noise failure mode. Mitigation proposed but NOT implemented: embedding-based retrieval of only highly-relevant CTIM items per turn instead of full-context injection, and removing the fixed max-size sqrt(n) constraint (Conclusion, Limitations).
cita: Lindenbauer et al. (2025). From Knowledge to Noise: CTIM-Rover and the Pitfalls of Episodic Memory in Software Engineering Agents.
notes: S4.1 KD reuses ExpeL ops (add/edit/upvote/downvote) on Cross-Task-Instance-Memory items distilled from successful trajectory pairs + success-failure self-reflection tuples (Fig2) -> operaciones=WRITE;ADMISION;ACTUALIZACION;OLVIDO(importance<0 removes item, footnote4). representacion=HIBRIDA: CTIM itself = plain-text importance-scored items injected wholesale (no retrieval filter, a stated limitation) + separate Milvus/Code-T5 embedding index for exemplar-trajectory retrieval (cosine, 90pct threshold, S4.2) -> retrieval=EMBEDDINGS. Table1 (45-sample SWE-bench-Verified test subset): CTIM-Rover 40% vs AutoCodeRover baseline 42% (WORSE in every configuration); 'CTIM only' 31% (-11pp), 'Repo-level CTIM only' 31% -> ABLATION across 5 configurations = mide_lectura=SI/RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO (measures utility of what's injected). S5.1 qualitative case studies (CUALITATIVA): removing one biasing 'clean'-mentioning CTIM item fixes django-13933; adding an arbitrary capitalized item also fixes django-15987 -> demonstrates the failure is noise/bias not content quality, core NEGATIVO finding ('does not outperform...in any configuration', concludes ExpeL/DoT-Bank do NOT scale to SE). Repository-level scope (cross-task-instance within same repo, S4.1) -> alcance=PROYECTO. Single agent -> multiagente=NO. F confirms F_screening (NEGATIVO;RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO) + adds WRITE (central KD write-path mechanism, S4.1).

title: Agentic Learner with Grow-and-Refine Multimodal Semantic Memory
benchmarks: HallusionBench, RealWorldQA, MathVista (mini), MathVision (mini), MMMU (val), MMStar
fallos_mitigaciones: Brevity bias and catastrophic forgetting from naive iterative memory rewriting (cited vs Dynamic-Cheatsheet/ACE baselines) mitigated by the grow-and-refine merge/create rule (Eq5,7) instead of rewriting. Manual inspection (S4.2) finds a residual 'textual bias' bottleneck: solver over-relies on logical memory and under-attends visual cues even when visual guidance is retrieved -- no explicit fix reported for this residual bottleneck beyond attention-map augmentation.
cita: Bo et al. (2025). ViLoMem: Agentic Learner with Grow-and-Refine Multimodal Semantic Memory.
notes: S3 dual-stream memory: logic bank ML (text guidelines) + visual bank MV (guideline+source-image pairs), structured JSON schema -> mem_tipos=SEMANTICA;MULTIMODAL, representacion=HIBRIDA (schema-based text+paired-images + dual embedding retrieval). Memory Generation (S3.1) ONLY activates on verifier-detected error (y-tilde_i != y_i) -> operaciones=WRITE;ADMISION; similarity-threshold Merge/Create (Eq5,7, 'grow-and-refine' avoiding 'detail erosion') -> CONSOLIDACION; trigger=EVENTO-DETERMINISTA (deterministic verifier mismatch). Table1 (6 benchmarks x 3 MLLMs): consistent pass@1 gains, e.g. GPT-4.1 MathVision +6.48pp. S4.7/Table5 memory-scalability stress test: progressive pool from 4 math benchmarks to 150k memory tokens, WeMath acc rises monotonically 72.53->74.58pct (no catastrophic forgetting) -> COSTO-TOKENS. Only failure-triggered writes -> NEGATIVO sense(a). Single MLLM solver, no agent sharing -> multiagente=NO. F confirms F_screening (NEGATIVO;CONSOLIDACION) + adds RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO, WRITE, COSTO (Table5 token-scale tracking).

title: Learning Hierarchical Procedural Memory for LLM Agents through Bayesian Selection and Contrastive Refinement
benchmarks: ALFWorld, WebShop, TravelPlanner, InterCodeSQL
fallos_mitigaciones: Unbounded procedural-memory growth / over-retention of obsolete or redundant procedures mitigated by (1) duplicate-merge at write time (theta_dup=0.85 cosine) and (2) periodic multi-factor utility pruning (Eq8: reliability+frequency+recency) that explicitly favors NOT over-retaining 'obsolete frequently-used skills'; failure index per procedure capped at K_fail=15 entries via success-based removal + redundancy-aware eviction + temporal decay.
cita: Forouzandeh et al. (2025). Learning Hierarchical Procedural Memory for LLM Agents through Bayesian Selection and Contrastive Refinement.
notes: S4.1-4.6: LLM segments trajectories into structured Proc=<goal,precondition,action,postcondition> tuples embedded for ANN retrieval (semantic vector space, S4.1) -> mem_tipos=PROCEDIMENTAL, representacion=VECTOR, retrieval=EMBEDDINGS;RANKING (Bayesian expected-utility Eq3-5 reranks ANN candidates). operaciones: WRITE(extraction, Eq1) + ADMISION(dup-check theta_dup=0.85 merge-vs-new, S4.1) + ACTUALIZACION(contrastive refinement edits Psi/pi/Phi, Eq6, S4.3) + CONSOLIDACION(merge dup + meta-procedural composition S4.4) + OLVIDO(multi-factor utility pruning Eq8, bounded Kfail=15/Nproc=200, S4.6). trigger=EVENTO-DETERMINISTA(episode-end construction, refine when >=3 successes+3 failures per Algorithm1 line23);PRESUPUESTO(bounded capacity forces pruning);CHECKPOINT(periodic pruning). Table2 ablation on ALFWorld: removing Bayesian selection -7.7/-9.1pp (largest), meta-procedural -11.9pp unseen, contrastive/ontological -3.5/-4.6 and -4.3/-6.2pp -> mide_lectura=SI/RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO (ablates the selection/scoring READ-path directly). Table1: 78.1pct avg across ALFWorld/WebShop/TravelPlanner/InterCodeSQL, ALFWorld-unseen 90.3pct (+3.1pp positive generalization gap). Table3/S5.3: memory built in 56s vs IPR's 44.8 GPU-hrs (2800x faster) -> LATENCIA/OTRA cost metric; memory footprint <4MB. Eq8 explicit recency-decay term 'avoiding over-retention of obsolete...skills' -> fidelidad_procedencia=SI (staleness-aware pruning). Contrastive refinement built entirely from paired failure contexts F_i -> NEGATIVO sense(a). Single agent (frozen LLM + external memory) -> multiagente=NO. F confirms F_screening (NEGATIVO;PROCEDIMENTAL) + adds RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO, WRITE, CONSOLIDACION, COSTO.

title: Learning from Mistakes via Cooperative Study Assistant for Large Language Models
benchmarks: BBH (16 tasks), BBQ (9 tasks)
fallos_mitigaciones: Prior self-reflection/self-refine methods are unreliable because they lack ground-truth to decide when to stop revising (cited Huang et al. 2023) -- Self-Refine baseline empirically 'repeatedly revise correct answers' without a stopping signal (AppA.4), even underperforming direct prompting M. SALAM mitigates by restricting ground-truth USE to the offline gathering phase only (T sees the label there) and reusing the resulting static mistake-memory entries at examination time without needing live ground truth or a learned stopping criterion.
cita: Wang and Li (2023). Learning from Mistakes via Cooperative Study Assistant for Large Language Models.
notes: S3: two cooperating agents -- main LLM M + study assistant T -- sharing a global mistake memory Oerr (key=query, value=list of (wrong_answer,feedback)) -> multiagente=SI, mem_tipos=EPISODICA. Gathering phase: T writes an entry ONLY when R(st,at)=0 (incorrect) -> operaciones=WRITE;ADMISION;ACTUALIZACION('updates the entry with the current response yt if it is incorrect', S3.2), trigger=EVENTO-DETERMINISTA. Examination phase retrieval: SentenceTransformer cosine similarity, top-k=1, threshold=0.9 -> retrieval=EMBEDDINGS, representacion=VECTOR. Table2 (BBH/BBQ, 3 backbones): SALAM beats M/Self-refine/M-w-Ocorr baselines (e.g. Flan-T5 BBH avg 42.4->48.6, BBQ 62->80); ablation M-w-Oerr (retrieval WITHOUT T's feedback policy) vs M-w-Ocorr (successes-only memory) directly isolates read-path value of failure-vs-success content -> mide_lectura=SI/RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO. S4.4-equivalent 'Failure can sometimes be more valuable than success': Oerr(mistakes) consistently outperforms Ocorr(successes) -- explicit NEGATIVO finding that failure-content is the more useful memory type (sense b), on top of the core design of gathering ONLY mistakes (sense a). Table3: SALAM w/10pct training data matches/beats baselines w/100pct -> data-efficiency result folded into EXITO reporting. Persists across the WHOLE task/benchmark stream (train split -> test split reuse), not per-session -> alcance=PROYECTO. F confirms F_screening (WRITE;RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO;NEGATIVO) + adds MULTIAGENTE (2-agent cooperative architecture sharing Oerr).

title: Failures Pave the Way: Enhancing Large Language Models through Tuning-free Rule Accumulation
benchmarks: BBQ-Lite (7 tasks), TweetEval, AGNews, DBPedia, Dyck Language (BIG-Bench Hard)
fallos_mitigaciones: Rule collection growing excessively under streaming mistakes is mitigated by an explicit LRU eviction strategy once size exceeds a fixed threshold (100 rules) -- ablation (Table4 '-LRU') shows removing this cap HURTS performance (e.g. Disability -4.5pp, matching the count of evicted rules). Separately, incoming rules can be redundant or contradictory as 'user requirements evolve' -- mitigated by fcheck, an LLM pass that detects identical/contradictory rule pairs via semantic-similarity lookup and retains only the new rule (S2.4); ablating fcheck ('-fcheck' in Table4) also degrades performance.
cita: Yang et al. (2023). Failures Pave the Way: Enhancing Large Language Models through Tuning-free Rule Accumulation.
notes: S2.3-2.4 Fig2: rule collection Theta built ONLY from mistakes f(xt)!=yt (process a-f) -> operaciones=WRITE(fgen, Eq1);ADMISION(retest, keep only rules that fix the mistake, discard failed ones into a separate mistake collection Phi);CONSOLIDACION(fsum summarizes rules from MULTIPLE related mistakes retrieved from Phi, Eq2; fcheck merges/dedupes identical-or-contradictory incoming rules, S2.4);OLVIDO(explicit LRU eviction when collection exceeds size threshold=100, S2.4). trigger=EVENTO-DETERMINISTA(mistake-triggered)+PRESUPUESTO(size-threshold-triggered LRU). retrieval=RANKING (BM25 explicitly, S3.1 Setup, top-3 rules) -> representacion=DOCS-ARCHIVOS (plain-text 'if...then...' rule collection). mem_tipos=SEMANTICA (declarative generalizable rules, not raw episodic trajectories). Table4 ablation (-LRU,-fsum,-fcheck) on 3 BBQ-Lite tasks: removing fsum hurts most; -LRU drops Disability -4.5pp; Fig3c ablates rule-collection SIZE directly showing performance scales with the amount of rule content available to read -> mide_lectura=SI/RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO. Tables1/2/3/5/6/8: TRAN beats Zero-Shot/CoT/SALAM/Auto-CoT across BBQ-Lite(7 tasks)+TweetEval+AGNews+DBPedia+Dyck-Language, zero-shot BBQ-Lite avg 91.6% vs SALAM 82.8% (+8.8pp). fcheck explicitly resolves identical/contradictory rules as 'incoming rules are dynamic and can be contradictory, reflecting evolving user requirements' -> fidelidad_procedencia=SI (consistency-check between memory entries, rule7 FIDELIDAD-costuras). Title itself + core design = NEGATIVO sense(a) (memory IS built exclusively from failures). Single frozen LLM plays all roles (fgen/fsum/fcheck) -> multiagente=NO. F confirms F_screening (NEGATIVO;WRITE) + adds CONSOLIDACION, RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO, FIDELIDAD.

title: A Dual-Helix Governance Approach Towards Reliable Agentic AI for WebGIS Development
benchmarks: own case studies (FutureShorelines WebGIS legacy-code refactor; COVID-19 infodemic-mapping cartographic-reliability rubric per Mooney & Juhasz 2020); no standard public benchmark
fallos_mitigaciones: The paper's premise IS 5 LLM failure modes (C1 long-context degradation, C2 cross-session forgetting, C3 stochasticity, C4 instruction-following failure, C5 adaptation rigidity via costly fine-tuning). Mitigated by the dual-helix's two axes: Knowledge Externalization persists facts outside the ephemeral attention window and restores project context via a standardized initialization protocol (fixes C1/C2); Behavioral Enforcement makes protocol compliance mandatory rather than advisory (fixes C4), unlike RAG whose 'retrieved text serves merely as context that the model may probabilistically ignore as task complexity grows'; the self-learning cycle persists newly discovered patterns as auditable graph nodes without retraining (fixes C5).
cita: Guan et al. (2026). A Dual-Helix Governance Approach Towards Reliable Agentic AI for WebGIS Development.
notes: S3.2 3-track KG substrate: Track1(Knowledge)=facts/patterns nodes (mem_tipos=SEMANTICA), Track3(Skills)=validated reproducible workflows (PROCEDIMENTAL); every node is a version-controlled JSON document with parent links -> representacion=GRAFO, retrieval=GRAFO (agent 'traverses the hierarchical relationships', queries KG for 'step-specific constraints'). S3.4 5-step self-learning cycle (Discovery->Structuring->Linking->Validation->Persistence, Fig4) -> operaciones=WRITE;ADMISION(schema-check+human Agent-Builder review before persisting); trigger=DISCRECIONAL-LLM(agent decides when it 'discovers' a concept)+CHECKPOINT(persistence at session/step boundaries). S4.4 Table4: KG grew 28->126 nodes (+350%) during FutureShorelines refactor, 98 nodes created autonomously and human-reviewed -> fidelidad_procedencia=SI (auditable/version-controlled/reversible, reviewed to avoid 'redundancy or hallucinations'). S4.5 controlled 3-condition experiment (Fig7/8): dynamic KG-retrieval (Condition C, dual-helix) vs static full-prompt (B) vs unguided (A), same info/model(gpt-5.2), 5 trials each -> directly measures retrieval-STRUCTURE utility: C halves variance (sigma=0.36 vs 0.79) and wins Rule-Compliance E5 by +27.7pp (1.66 vs 1.30) despite a SMALLER per-step prompt (~1400 vs ~4000 tokens) -> mide_lectura=SI/RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO. S5 5-condition COVID-19 cartographic ablation (Table5/Fig10): Full Dual-Helix 8.33 best; removing Skills(E)->6.33 (largest drop, near-baseline 6.22), Behaviors(D)->7.22, Knowledge(C)->8.00 (smallest) -> ABLATION ranks Skills>Behaviors>Knowledge for this task. S3.3 role separation: Agent Builder(meta-level, can itself be an LLM agent per COVID case study)+Domain Expert(task-level) SHARE the KG substrate -> multiagente=SI. S3.4/S4.5 'phase memory' + session-specific KG-State track step-by-step plan/discovery progress explicitly INJECTED forward into subsequent steps (Fig9b: 4->17 entries) -> plan_estado=SI. Table3: SLOC -49%, cyclomatic complexity -51%, maintainability +7pts, JSHint warnings -98% (code-quality OTRA metrics) -> metricas=EXITO(compliance scores)+OTRA(code-quality). Cross-session persistence (addressing C2) + mandatory behavioral protocols = literally what travels between sessions -> handoff=CONTENIDO;CONTRATO. F confirms F_screening (WRITE;PROCEDIMENTAL) + adds RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO, FIDELIDAD, MULTIAGENTE, DOCS-VERSIONADO (version-controlled/auditable/reversible framing throughout).

title: EffiSkill: Agent Skill Based Automated Code Efficiency Optimization
benchmarks: EffiBench-X (623 code-efficiency tasks, Python+C++ subsets)
fallos_mitigaciones: Prior LLM-based code-optimization approaches operate purely at the instance level (one-shot rewriting or retrieved exemplars) and 'do not explicitly distill reusable optimization knowledge', repeatedly re-deriving the same fixes -- mitigated by mining mechanism-level Operator/Meta Skills instead of instance pairs. Skill-library fragmentation/redundancy from clustering is mitigated by merging highly similar skill summaries at a TF-IDF cosine threshold of 0.8 followed by a conservative LLM merge pass, keeping the final library compact.
cita: Wang et al. (2026). EffiSkill: Agent Skill Based Automated Code Efficiency Optimization.
notes: S3.2 Stage I (offline): trace extraction (ProblemBrief/SlowAudit/FastAudit/DeltaSummary) from 900+900 paired slow/fast programs -> signature abstraction -> hybrid TF-IDF+dense-embedding (all-MiniLM-L6-v2) clustering -> Operator Skills distilled per cluster + Meta Skills as procedural controllers; merge threshold 0.8 cosine + LLM merge pass -> operaciones=WRITE;CONSOLIDACION, representacion=DOCS-ARCHIVOS (skill cards, Fig2: metadata+body fields), retrieval=EMBEDDINGS. Stage II (S3.3, execution-free): Diagnose->RetrieveSkills(3 candidate sets)->ComposePlans(2-3 plans)->GenerateCandidates, NO runtime execution feedback in the loop. Table2 RQ2 ablation (S5.2): 'w/o Retrieval' (generate directly from diagnosis, skip skill retrieval) vs 'w/ Random Skills' (uniformly-sampled skills replace retrieved ones) vs 'w/o Multi Plans' -> Random-Skills ablation is a textbook retrieval-precision test -> mide_lectura=SI/RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO; paper concludes 'relevant skill retrieval improves alignment with optimization bottlenecks'. Table1 (RQ1/RQ3): EffiSkill beats Instruction/CoT/RAG/FasterPy/SBLLM/EffiCoder baselines by 3.69-12.52pp OPT@k across GPT-5-mini/Qwen3-Coder-30B, Python+C++ (cross-language RQ3 consistency). Single offline-mined static library reused at inference, no online agent-to-agent sharing studied -> multiagente=NO. F confirms F_screening (PROCEDIMENTAL;WRITE) + adds RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO, CONSOLIDACION (merge-threshold dedup).

title: Mem$^2$Evolve: Towards Self-Evolving Agents via Co-Evolutionary Capability Expansion and Experience Distillation
benchmarks: GAIA, ALFWorld, WebShop, TravelPlanner, HotpotQA, 2WikiMultihopQA, AIME24, AIME25 (8 benchmarks, 6 task categories)
fallos_mitigaciones: Creating new tools/agents from scratch without experience guidance causes 'non-replicable success and repeated errors' (motivating gap vs pure capability-centric baselines like Alita/AutoAgents) -- mitigated by conditioning asset creation on retrieved Experience Memory (Eq6). Also, 'a correct answer does not guarantee robust underlying assets' -- mitigated by a Self-Correction Loop: newly created assets must pass an LLM-synthesized unit-test Valid() gate (Eq8) before persisting to Asset Memory; failed validation triggers Improve() revision + regenerated tests until it passes (Eq8-9).
cita: Cheng et al. (2026). Mem2Evolve: Towards Self-Evolving Agents via Co-Evolutionary Capability Expansion and Experience Distillation.
notes: S3.1 Dual-Memory: Asset Memory MA=Bagt(cup;Btool (expert-agent specs <role,expertise,suggestions,tools> + MCP tool records <name,func-desc,code,docs>, PROCEDIMENTAL) + Experience Memory ME=Eagt(cup;Etool (lessons <title,desc,use-cases,content> distilled from success/failure trajectories, EPISODICA) -> representacion=HIBRIDA (structured records+code+text). S3.2 forward inference: Recruitment Function Gamma(si) via sim(si,MA)>=delta (EMBEDDINGS retrieval) picks reuse-vs-create; Creation conditions on Retrieve(si,Etool)+web search (Eq6) -> retrieval=EMBEDDINGS. S3.3 backward evolution: Judge()=LLM-as-judge produces (rt,ct) (trigger=DISCRECIONAL-LLM) after each task (trigger=EVENTO-DETERMINISTA pipeline stage); Asset Memory Evolution gates new assets through Valid(mnew,ct) unit-test verification before MA<-MA U {mfinal} (Eq8-9, operaciones=ADMISION;ACTUALIZACION) -> fidelidad_procedencia=SI (explicit pre-persistence correctness verification). Experience Memory Evolution: Reflection(tau_t,rt,ct) distills BOTH Success-Generalization and Failure-Diagnosis lessons, merged via ME<-ME U {enew} (Eq10-11, CONSOLIDACION). Table3 RQ1 ablation: w/o Tool Creation -10.28pp (largest), w/o Expert-Agent-Creation -1.72pp, w/o Agent-Memory -4.73pp, w/o Tool-Memory -3.13pp. Table4 RQ2 (S5.2): Experience-Guided vs w/o-Exp.-Guide asset creation directly measured -> First-Pass-Validity +56.0% relative on GAIA, Avg.Improve.Iter down to -68.4% on AIME -> mide_lectura=SI/RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO (explicit read-utility measurement). Table2: Mem2Evolve avg Pass@1 70.24% vs strongest capability-baseline Alita+6.46%, experience-baseline AFLOW+11.80%, naive-LLM+18.53%; RQ4 explicitly claims 'effective memory reuse in cross-task settings' -> alcance=PROYECTO. Experience Memory guides MULTIPLE recruited expert agents ('guiding specific expert agents in handling complex tasks') sharing the same pool -> multiagente=SI. F confirms F_screening (CONSOLIDACION;PROCEDIMENTAL) + adds WRITE, RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO, MULTIAGENTE, FIDELIDAD.

title: Skill Drift Is Contract Violation: Proactive Maintenance for LLM Agent Skill Libraries
benchmarks: DriftBench (own, 880 pairs: 174 controlled drifts + 107 real-world drifts + 599 negative controls, from 49 SWE-Skills-Bench source skills)
fallos_mitigaciones: The entire paper addresses skill staleness: 'skills silently decay as the external services, packages, APIs, and configurations they reference evolve' (APIs migrate, packages deprecate, URLs move, auth mechanisms change, 8 drift types S3). Naive contract-free monitoring over-alerts (40% FPR from probing every changed value, including incidental mentions like documentation links). Mitigated by SKILLGUARD's role-bearing contract extraction: only OPERATIONAL-role assumptions are validated (raises ZERO false alarms over 599 no-drift/hard-negative cases, Wilson 95% CI [0,0.6]%), and violated contracts localize repair (one-round success 10%->78% vs unlocalized 'the skill is stale' prompting).
cita: Fan et al. (2026). Skill Drift Is Contract Violation: Proactive Maintenance for LLM Agent Skill Libraries.
notes: S4: skill document S -> deterministic regex pass across 15 pattern families (URLs/versions/imports/API-paths/auth/Docker/env-vars/etc, retrieval=GREP-ARCHIVOS) finds candidate mentions; a semantic pass labels each as OPERATIONAL vs INCIDENTAL (role decision) forming contract records C(S)={(type,role,value,evidence)} -> operaciones=ACTUALIZACION (repair rewrites stale skill content once a contract is violated; no new-skill creation/write pipeline is studied here, skills pre-exist from SWE-Skills-Bench). S4.2 contract-drift matching predicate is type-gated+token-overlap based, applied ONLY to OPERATIONAL-labeled records -> this precision-first ordering (role-filter BEFORE probing) is the paper's central mechanism, distinct from a retrieval-utility axis, so mide_lectura=NO (the axis measured is content VALIDITY/staleness, not read-precision for a downstream task) -> fidelidad_procedencia=SI is the dominant facet instead. S5.1 Table2: 100% precision / up to 76% recall (best backbone) on known-drift verification across 5 LLM backbones; ZERO false positives over 599 negative controls (vs CI-probes 40% FPR, Dependabot-style 10% FPR). S5.2 pre-registered LIVE study over 49 real skills: 86% conservative precision, 55% recall, 7% FPR (2 apparent FPs later confirmed genuine drift). S5.3 repair: contract-localized repair 78% one-round success (p<1e-5 vs no-localization's 10%) using ~10K tokens/skill vs ~18K for 3-round Self-refine (COSTO-TOKENS;ITERACION=round count). S6 sensitivity ablation: expanding regex families 7->15 raises real-world recall 45%->78% at 0% FPR. F confirms F_screening (FIDELIDAD;PROCEDIMENTAL) + adds DOCS-VERSIONADO (drift = pinned-dependency/version staleness in skill documents, the paper's core framing).

title: SkillOps: Managing LLM Agent Skill Libraries as Self-Maintaining Software Ecosystems
benchmarks: ALFWorld (229 curated SkillsBench skills + synthetic degraded variants, 9 library scales 200-2000 skills)
fallos_mitigaciones: 'Skill technical debt': persistent library-level defects (redundancy, missing validation, interface drift, stale implementations) that don't break a single skill locally but harm future retrieval/composition/execution as the library grows -- task-time repair fixes one episode while the underlying defect remains. Mitigated by a 5-dimension health diagnosis (Utility/Redundancy/Compatibility/Failure-Risk/Validation-Gap, Eq4) feeding typed maintenance actions: merge (collapses redundancy-edge duplicates), repair (rewrites failing operations from execution feedback), retire (removes obsolete/failing skills), add_validator (fills validation gaps), add_adapter (fixes type-incompatible dependency edges).
cita: Song et al. (2026). SkillOps: Managing LLM Agent Skill Libraries as Self-Maintaining Software Ecosystems.
notes: S2-3: each skill = typed Skill Contract (P,O,A,V,F); library=Hierarchical Skill Ecosystem Graph (HSEG) with dep/comp/red/alt typed edges -> representacion=GRAFO, mem_tipos=PROCEDIMENTAL. Task-Time Loop (Alg.1): skill matching r(s,tau)=lambda*BM25+(1-lambda)*semantic (Eq1, retrieval=RANKING;EMBEDDINGS), then dependency+compatibility-constrained graph stitching (retrieval=GRAFO also), validator/adapter insertion, local repair on failure. Library-Time Loop (Alg.2, Fig1 orange): 'mines skill contracts from execution logs' (WRITE) -> 5-dim health diagnosis + optional CGPD risk-propagation over dep edges (Eq5) -> typed actions merge(CONSOLIDACION)/repair(ACTUALIZACION)/retire(OLVIDO)/add_validator(ADMISION, fills Validation-Gap G(s)=1[Vs=empty])/add_adapter; trigger gated by DeltaH<Theta_maint threshold (PRESUPUESTO) after each task (EVENTO-DETERMINISTA). H3 ablation (Table5): removing Task-Time Loop drops SR 79.5%->15.7% (largest), removing Library-Time Loop drops to 71.9%, graph-level ablations to 64.6%/72.2% -> mide_lectura=SI/RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO (isolates retrieval/graph-stitching value directly). H1 (Table1): SkillOps_Full 79.5% SR on ALFWorld vs strongest baseline LLM_Skill_Planner 70.6% (+8.9pp), zero std across seeds. V4 plug-in (Table2): consistently helps retrieval-heavy baselines (+2.90pp Hybrid, +1.00pp BM25, +1.12pp Dense) when swapped into their unchanged code -- direct evidence maintenance improves READ quality. H2 (Table4): SkillOps stays ~79-80% SR as library scales 200->2000 with rising synthetic degradation density (15%->90%), while task-time-only baselines degrade sharply -> fidelidad_procedencia=SI. V2 (Table3, S6.4): nearly-zero library-time LLM cost (rule-based), task-time tokens mostly neutral/negative (24/35 cells decrease) -> COSTO-TOKENS. F confirms F_screening (PROCEDIMENTAL;FIDELIDAD) + adds WRITE, RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO, CONSOLIDACION, COSTO.

title: Library Drift: Diagnosing and Fixing a Silent Failure Mode in Self-Evolving LLM Skill Libraries
benchmarks: MBPP+ hard-100 (Claude Opus 4.7, 100 rounds x 3 seeds, own reproducible-trigger + 8-ablation protocol)
fallos_mitigaciones: The paper's entire subject IS a memory failure mode it names 'library drift': unbounded skill accumulation without outcome-driven lifecycle management causes retrieval degradation, false-positive/stale injections, and performance stagnation-or-collapse below the no-skill baseline (silent: 'end-task metrics decline gradually with no explicit error signal'). Mitigated by the Ratchet recipe: outcome-driven retirement (Nmin=100 trials + contribution threshold tau=0.10, formal non-divergence guarantee Prop.1), a bounded active-cap (C=50, forces eviction of lowest-contribution skill), and a meta-skill authoring prior (reduces harmful/redundant skill births at the source, -43% of Default's gain when ablated, the single most valuable component). Critically documents a NEGATIVE result: harsh/premature retirement (A4, Nmin=20) is WORSE than no governance at all (-0.019, below the no-skill floor) -- governance itself can actively harm when calibrated on insufficient evidence (Hoeffding epsilon~0.44 at Nmin=20).
cita: Zhang et al. (2026). Library Drift: Diagnosing and Fixing a Silent Failure Mode in Self-Evolving LLM Skill Libraries.
notes: S3-5, Fig1 'Ratchet' loop: persistent append-only Skill Bank(ACTIVE+DEPRECATED, never deletes raw log)+Meta-Skill Bank(one ACTIVE authoring prior)+Evidence Log(capsules+verdicts) -> representacion=DOCS-ARCHIVOS, mem_tipos=PROCEDIMENTAL. Router picks skill via tf-idf-union-embed similarity (S6.3 A2 ablation description) -> retrieval=RANKING;EMBEDDINGS. Synthesizer clusters>=3 failures sharing a canonical pattern into ONE new skill (operaciones=WRITE;CONSOLIDACION); Curator retires if per-skill contribution ĉ(s)=(succ-fail)/trials < -tau after Nmin trials (OLVIDO, EVENTO-DETERMINISTA-gated) and enforces the bounded cap C=50 (PRESUPUESTO); Meta-Synth rewrites the meta-skill every N rounds (ACTUALIZACION, CHECKPOINT-triggered, A8 ablation). S4 trace-level diagnostics (per-skill contribution score Eq2, HELPED/HURT/NEUTRAL/INAPPLICABLE attribution verdicts, router-engagement%) are explicitly designed to measure retrieval/injection utility BEFORE it reaches aggregate pass@1 -> mide_lectura=SI/RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO is the paper's central diagnostic axis. Table1/Fig2 (8 ablations, 3 seeds): Default lifts pass@1 0.258->0.584 late-window (+0.328); A1(no injection, floor)+0.002; A4(harsh retirement)-0.019 BELOW floor (explicit NEGATIVO governance-harm finding, consistent across all 3 seeds -0.005/-0.027/-0.025); A5/A6(no dedup) slightly EXCEED Default, showing the meta-skill subsumes explicit deduplication. S6.4: Default uses ~14.5k LLM calls/100 rounds (COSTO-TOKENS, +43% vs no-skill A1) and 6.5h wall time vs A1's 2.3h (LATENCIA). Explicit staleness framing throughout ('stale skill injected into the solver prompt actively misleads', 'silent injection harm') -> fidelidad_procedencia=SI. Single frozen LLM plays ALL pipeline roles (Router/Solver/Grader/Critic/Synthesizer/Curator/Meta-Synth), not separate persistent cooperating agents -> multiagente=NO. F confirms F_screening (CONSOLIDACION;PROCEDIMENTAL) + adds NEGATIVO (A4 governance-harm), WRITE, RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO, FIDELIDAD, COSTO.

title: More Skills, Worse Agents? Skill Shadowing Degrades Performance When Expanding Skill Libraries
benchmarks: SkillsBench (88 tasks; 38 filtered task-model pairs with oracle skills; library sizes |S| in {S*,52,102,202})
fallos_mitigaciones: 'Skill shadowing': as a skill library grows, distractor skills with superficially-matching descriptions displace the correct oracle skill during selection (up to 68% of the pass-rate drop, the only statistically-significant component, CI excludes zero at |S|=202); a smaller, statistically-indistinguishable-from-zero 'context overhead' effect also exists (enlarged context degrades execution even when selection is correct). No mitigation is implemented (pure diagnostic paper); Discussion proposes retrieval-based pre-filtering, description disambiguation, and learned routing as future fixes.
cita: Song and Wei (2026). More Skills, Worse Agents? Skill Shadowing Degrades Performance When Expanding Skill Libraries.
notes: Pure diagnostic/measurement paper over EXISTING full-context skill libraries (industry Agent-Skills convention, Anthropic/OpenAI SKILL.md): the agent context is simply q+D(S) = the FULL set of all skill (name,description) pairs injected at once, no retrieval/write/consolidation mechanism of its own is proposed -> mem_tipos/representacion/operaciones/trigger/retrieval=NA (mirrors the pure-measurement precedent: paper studies an existing paradigm, not its own architecture). S3 exact decomposition (Eq.10): library-induced pass-rate drop Delta(q,S)=p(q,S*(q))-p(q,S) splits into Delta_ctx(context overhead, event-probabilities fixed, only conditional pass-rates vary) + Delta_shd(skill shadowing, conditional pass-rates fixed, only selection-event probabilities vary), with derived upper bounds (Lemma1/2). This decomposition IS a precision/utility measurement of skill SELECTION (reading) as scale grows -> mide_lectura=SI/RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO (rule3). Table1 (38 task-model pairs, 2545 trajectories, 95% two-stage clustered-bootstrap CI): at |S|=202, Delta_shd=.14[.06,.26] (CI excludes zero, dominant) vs Delta_ctx=.07[-.13,.25] (never separates from zero at any scale). Table2: event-o ('oracle only') trajectory share collapses from 88.0%(S*) to 52.6%(|S|=202), mass migrating into n('no skill', 12.0%->38.5%) and m('mixed/wrong skill', 0%->8.9%) -- two distinguishable failure sub-modes: abandonment and wrong selection. Table3 (mario-coin-counting example, Intro+AppendixA.4): a distractor 'video-frame-extraction' skill (superficially better textual match) shadows the correct oracle skill in ALL 26/26 trajectories -> CUALITATIVA anchor. Overall pass rate drops up to 21% (avg both models) at |S|=202; skill shadowing is the primary bottleneck, NOT the enlarged context -> NEGATIVO sense(b) (negative evidence against the assumed 'more skills=better' premise of skill-library scaling). F confirms F_screening (PROCEDIMENTAL) + adds RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO, NEGATIVO.

title: Managing Procedural Memory in LLM Agents: Control, Adaptation, and Evaluation
benchmarks: AFTER (own, 382 tasks, 6 professional roles, 22 procedural skills)
fallos_mitigaciones: Skills evolved from NARROW experience (single source context) exhibit 'source-context overfitting': specificity (train gain) improves while generality (test gain) degrades (Fig1 landscape). Mitigated by evolving from DIVERSE multi-task/role/model trace pools, which moves skills toward the desired high-specificity+high-generality regime (Table3: diverse evolution reaches +7.3 test-gain on pdf/xlsx/pptx vs narrow's often-negative test deltas). Separately, cross-role transfer is an unmitigated limitation: skills specialized to one role's workflow LOSE effectiveness (-4.8 to -7.5pp) when applied to a different role's use of the same nominal skill (Fig5, pdf skill PM<->DS).
cita: Belikova et al. (2026). Managing Procedural Memory in LLM Agents: Control, Adaptation, and Evaluation.
notes: S2/S3: 22 skills as versioned SKILL.md artifacts (YAML+markdown, Agent-Skills format) -> representacion=DOCS-ARCHIVOS, mem_tipos=PROCEDIMENTAL; 'skill annotations are fixed at task definition rather than retrieved at solve time, separating skill quality from retrieval quality' -> retrieval=NA (retrieval explicitly out of scope by design). EVOLUTION harness: full-skill updates via COLLECT-DIAGNOSE-REVISE-PROMOTE cycle, s(v+1)=U_rho(s(v),Dsrc); rho='reflector' (model/procedure that inspects traces and PROPOSES revision, trigger=DISCRECIONAL-LLM) fires after each refinement round (trigger=EVENTO-DETERMINISTA pipeline stage) -> operaciones=WRITE;ACTUALIZACION; PROMOTE step + 'validation, promotion, rollback, and lineage tracking' -> ADMISION + fidelidad_procedencia=SI (explicit lineage/rollback/validation infrastructure). Diverse-trace evolution (n=5) aggregates multi-model/task traces into ONE updated skill -> CONSOLIDACION. S4.1 static valuation (Table2): comparing no-skill(NA) vs handcrafted(H) vs LLM-generated(G) skill CONTENT injected in-prompt directly measures content-utility (no retrieval step, since skills are fixed by design) -> mide_lectura=SI/RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO (the facet covers read-utility broadly, not only vector retrieval). Skills improve M2 by +2.8pts avg; single refinement round adds +5.2pts (S4.2, Fig3: +3.7 to +6.7 aggregate across model scales). S4.4 cross-model transfer (Fig4): diverse-source-evolved skills reach 73.1% test accuracy vs best single-source 59.4% (+13.7pp) -- weaker source models give BETTER transfer signal, a genuinely negative/counterintuitive finding (NEGATIVO sense b). Token efficiency (Fig6): evolved skills cut total tokens by 326k(62%, Claude)/48k(16%, Hermes) on Kafka-Lag-Anomaly-Detection -> COSTO-TOKENS. Spans SIX professional organizational roles (DE/DS/GenAI/Infra/PM/SWE) with explicit cross-ROLE transfer as a primary evaluation axis -> alcance=ORGANIZACION. F confirms F_screening (PROCEDIMENTAL) + adds WRITE, RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO, NEGATIVO, FIDELIDAD, CONSOLIDACION, COSTO.

title: RESOURCE2SKILL: Distilling Executable Agent Skills from Human-Created Multimodal Resources
benchmarks: own 7 authoring-domain benchmark suites (Web, Excel, Reaper, PPT, Blender, CAD, UE5; 80 task briefs/domain)
fallos_mitigaciones: 'Directly placing raw videos into an agent's memory is expensive, redundant, and often impractical... compressing video into a plain text summary discards precisely the information that makes video useful: dynamic operations, before-after visual changes, animation quality, spatial layout, timing, tool interaction order.' Mitigated by the multimodal distiller fθ that extracts modality-specific evidence (key frames, code regions, prose passages, rendered exemplars) via a vision-capable LM and normalizes it into a structured (text,visual,code,metadata) entry instead of raw video or lossy text-only summarization, gated by a 5-check admission predicate (completeness, traceable provenance, deduplication, modality consistency, structural executability).
cita: Fan et al. (2026). Resource2Skills: Distilling Executable Skills from Human-Created Resources for Software Agents.
notes: S3.1 skill tuple s=(p,xtext,xvisual,xcode,m), p=taxonomy path, m=metadata for filtering/auditing/provenance -> mem_tipos=PROCEDIMENTAL;MULTIMODAL, representacion=HIBRIDA (structured multimodal entries + hierarchical Skill Wiki). S3.2 construction operator fθ distills 4 resource families (video/code/article/artifact) into candidates, domain predicate A_D enforces 5 checks incl. 'traceable provenance' before acceptance (operaciones=WRITE;ADMISION) -> fidelidad_procedencia=SI. S3.3 MetaBrowse: 2-stage selection, BM25 lexical scorer over name+tags+applicability+TAXONOMY-PATH narrows candidates (retrieval=RANKING;GRAFO, hierarchy directly favors topically-relevant subtrees), then an LM selects a SUBSET (can pick zero) to compose. S3.4 online acquisition reuses the SAME (fθ,A_D) operator when offline coverage is insufficient -> trigger=EVENTO-DETERMINISTA (coverage-gap condition). Table1 main comparison (4 backends x 4 systems x 7 domains, N=80/domain): w-Skills beats w/o-Skills in ALL 28 cells (56.8% vs 45.0%, +11.9pp) and beats the stronger off-the-shelf harness in 26/28 cells (paired Wilcoxon p<1e-3 in every GPT-5.4/5.5 cell); largest gains on UE5 (+30 to +40pp). Table2: offline-only vs offline+online acquisition: on Tstandard online adds only +0.7pp(noise), but on Tnovel(capability-gap stress test) online lifts 41.2%->62.8% (+21.6pp) -> pure gap-filler, not a booster. S4.4.1 panel-b ablation: Flat(pure-text list) vs Our-Wiki(hierarchical+multimodal) -- Wiki beats Flat by 2.5-8.2pp -> mide_lectura=SI/RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO. Table3 source-ablation: holding Video out drops avg 68.9%->59.4% (video is the non-substitutable source, Excel -12.1pp/Web -9.8pp). Table4 matched-budget representation ablation isolates content-type value: Text-only=65.0%, +Visual=+1.9pp, +Code=+2.0pp, Full=68.9% (multimodal content itself adds gain beyond curated-text-memory alone). Blinded human A/B (200 paired ratings, 5 raters, 40 pairs x 7 domains, AppendixK, CUALITATIVA): w-Skills wins 83.3% of non-tied pairs. F confirms F_screening (WRITE;PROCEDIMENTAL) + adds RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO, FIDELIDAD.

title: AgentSM: Semantic Memory for Agentic Text-to-SQL
benchmarks: Spider 2.0 / Spider 2.0 Lite (547 enterprise Text-to-SQL tasks)
fallos_mitigaciones: Three explicit failure modes of memoryless agentic Text-to-SQL: (1) 'Repeated exploration' -- agents retrace identical schema-exploration steps across queries on the same database (fewer than 10-20% of trajectories are distinct per cited prior work), inflating cost/latency; mitigated by trajectory reuse via the Trajectory Store. (2) 'Strategy selection' -- a single rigid pipeline strategy fails on out-of-distribution queries (e.g. vector search invoked in only 30% of firebase questions when unnecessary, Fig2); mitigated by per-query dynamic trajectory retrieval instead of a fixed one-size-fits-all routine. (3) 'Reducing variance' -- small syntax deviations derail reasoning and cause inconsistent results even at temperature=0; mitigated by composite tools shortening trajectories. A further explicit negative finding (Table1): reading RAW/unstructured ('Naive') trajectories yields NO improvement over no trajectory at all (both 25% accuracy) -- structured Markdown/JSON representation is required to realize any gain (50% accuracy).
cita: Biswal et al. (2026). AgentSM: Semantic Memory for Agentic Text-to-SQL.
notes: S3.2 offline Trajectory Synthesis (Algorithm1): LLM-generated synthetic exploration-rich questions per database schema -> agent executes them -> raw trajectories are STEP-CLASSIFIED (regex-based intent matching into exploration/execution/validation phases, not position-based) and restructured into markdown with LLM-generated semantic headers (operaciones=WRITE;CONSOLIDACION, mem_tipos=EPISODICA(trace-derived)+PROCEDIMENTAL(structured reusable 'programs')). Trajectory selection (Eq1-3): filter to same-database trajectories, then pick highest-semantic-similarity match to the current question -> retrieval=EMBEDDINGS, representacion=DOCS-ARCHIVOS (markdown/JSON trajectory files in a Trajectory Store). Table1 (20-question sample): 'No trajectory'/'Naive'(raw unstructured) BOTH give 25% accuracy/22.62 avg-steps identically -- raw-trajectory reading is USELESS; 'Markdown'/'JSON'(structured) reach 50% accuracy at 15-16.5 avg-steps -> mide_lectura=SI/RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO (direct precision test of representation format on read-utility). Table2 main results (547-task Spider2.0-Lite): AgentSM reaches SOTA 44.8% overall accuracy, +14.1% over agentic baseline SpiderAgent, +20% over a plain CodingAgent. Table3 ablation (75-question sample): removing trajectory reading OR composite tools each sharply cuts accuracy while INCREASING token usage and latency; full method reduces avg trajectory length 25% and improves accuracy 35% vs no-trajectory-reading -> COSTO-TOKENS;ITERACION;LATENCIA. Two agents (planner + schema-linking) exist but explicitly do NOT share the trajectory-memory system: 'introducing additional agents would necessitate a shared memory... which we leave as future work' -> multiagente=NO; design DELIBERATELY avoids inter-agent handoff/control-transfer to prevent 'context loss commonly observed when control is handed off to specialized sub-agents' -> handoff=NO. F confirms F_screening (PROCEDIMENTAL;RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO) + adds WRITE, COSTO.

title: ProcMEM: Learning Reusable Procedural Memory from Experience via Non-Parametric PPO for LLM Agents
benchmarks: ALFWorld, TextArena (Mastermind-v0); BFCL v4 (appendix)
fallos_mitigaciones: Three fundamental obstacles to reusable procedural memory motivate the design: C1 Executability (episodic narratives are passive, not directly-instantiable procedures) -- addressed by the Skill-MDP's explicit <Activation,Procedure,Termination> structure; C2 Reusability (stored procedures must reliably transfer) and C3 Non-Parametric Optimization (must improve without weight updates while avoiding catastrophic forgetting/over-specialization) -- addressed jointly by the PPO Gate, which explicitly guards against candidates that 'extrapolate beyond the observed interaction data and introduce hallucinated or behaviorally unstable Skills' via trust-region verification (only admits ω' if J(ω')>0). Unbounded pool growth/redundancy is mitigated by online-score-based pruning: skills with non-positive score or duplicate/redundant skills are removed, 'phasing out obsolete Skills while retaining those with consistently positive gains.'
cita: Mi et al. (2026). Skill-Pro: Learning Reusable Skills from Experience via Non-Parametric PPO for LLM Agents.
notes: S3.2 Skill omega=<I_omega,pi_omega,beta_omega> (activation/execution/termination), explicit natural-language readable form (representacion=DOCS-ARCHIVOS, mem_tipos=PROCEDIMENTAL, contrasted throughout vs EPISODIC memory as the paper's central framing, Fig1). S4.1 Semantic Gradients: per-trajectory hindsight attribution -> batch-aggregated update direction -> candidate omega'=omega XOR g_omega (WRITE). S4.2 PPO Gate: importance-ratio+clipped-advantage verification (Eq6, LCLIP) admits only J(omega')>0 candidates (ADMISION;ACTUALIZACION). S4.3 online score+pruning removes non-positive-score/duplicate skills under fixed capacity K (OLVIDO, trigger=PRESUPUESTO); evolution operator E applied per-trajectory-batch (trigger=EVENTO-DETERMINISTA). Skill selection: Sim(st,I_omega) via cosine-embeddings-or-LLM-judge (retrieval=EMBEDDINGS) then top-k re-ranked by estimated Q-value (retrieval=RANKING). Table1 headline metric IS 'Experience Reuse Rate' (in-domain/cross-task/cross-agent) -> mide_lectura=SI/RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO directly measures read-precision. Cross-agent: skills LEARNED on Gemma-2-9B are REUSED by Gemma-3-4B/Qwen3-32B/LLaMA-3.3-70B, a headline result -> multiagente=SI, handoff=CONTENIDO (the natural-language skill content itself travels between different agent backbones). Table1 efficiency: Skill-Pro stores only 816 tokens total vs baselines' 40510-391706 tokens (RAG/Expel/A-MEM/AWM/G-Memory) -> extreme memory compression -> COSTO-TOKENS; 'Retrieval Ratio' = probability of retrieving memory per step -> OTRA. Ablation (Table3/Fig3): Semantic-Gradients and PPO-Gate both indispensable; online-scoring preserves long-term evolutionary gains. F confirms F_screening (PROCEDIMENTAL;MULTIAGENTE) + adds RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO, FIDELIDAD, WRITE, COSTO.

title: TextBFGS: A Case-Based Reasoning Approach to Code Optimization via Error-Operator Retrieval
benchmarks: HumanEval-Hard (45 tasks), MBPP-Hard (117 tasks), via EvalPlus
fallos_mitigaciones: Existing first-order textual optimizers (TextGrad) are stateless: 'each optimization run begins tabula rasa,' causing inefficient zig-zagging/oscillation and excessive token consumption -- mitigated by the Hessian-Proxy Case Base of historical error-operator pairs. Separately, existing memory-augmented optimizers (REMO) retrieve by INPUT/problem similarity, which causes 'surface-level case overfitting' and fails to transfer across domains: Table3 shows MBPP-with-HumanEval-CB Plus-pass-rate COLLAPSES to 58.12%, barely above the 48.72% no-CB floor (a -20.51pp degradation vs in-domain retrieval) -- mitigated by TextBFGS's gradient/error-based retrieval instead, which maintains 74.36% Plus-pass-rate cross-domain (+16.24pp over REMO, Table4).
cita: Zhang et al. (2026). TextBFGS: A Case-Based Reasoning Approach to Code Optimization via Error-Operator Retrieval.
notes: S3.3 Hessian-Proxy Case Base M={(g_i,O_i)}: g_i=textual error/gradient (episodic, trace-derived), O_i=abstract adaptation operator (procedural rule) -> mem_tipos=EPISODICA;PROCEDIMENTAL; stored in ChromaDB indexed by Qwen3-Embedding-8B embeddings, top-k cosine retrieval on the QUERY gradient g_t^query=g_{t-1} ('Semantic Momentum', Eq6) -> representacion=VECTOR, retrieval=EMBEDDINGS. S3.5 Case Retention (operaciones=WRITE;ADMISION): only upon f(x_{t+1})>f(x_t) is the tuple (g_t,O_t) injected back into M (trigger=EVENTO-DETERMINISTA), enabling self-evolution. Case Base bootstrapped via TextBFGS(w/o CB) over 3 epochs -> 39 cases(HumanEval)/245 cases(MBPP), k=3 retrieved per query (matched to TextGrad-Momentum's 3-record window for fair comparison). S4.2 ablation (Table1/2): TextGrad(91.11/82.22% HumanEval Base/Plus) -> +Momentum(86.67% Plus) -> +CaseBase(TextBFGS-REMO 91.11%, TextBFGS 93.33% Plus) -- Case-Base integration is the single largest lever (+6.66pp over Momentum on HumanEval, +20.51pp on MBPP-Plus). S4.3 (Table3/4, the paper's central experiment) directly compares problem-based(REMO) vs error/gradient-based(TextBFGS) retrieval strategies IN-domain vs CROSS-domain -> this IS a rigorous mide_lectura=SI/RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO test: TextBFGS-REMO overfits to surface content (near-identical In-Domain 97.56% but collapses Cross-Domain to 58.12%), while TextBFGS's error-dynamics retrieval transfers robustly (96.34% In vs 93.33%/74.36% Cross) -- proves 'optimization logic...is more transferable than specific code instances.' S4.4: One-Pass fusion (gradient+operator+update in ONE LLM call) cuts token counts by -50.6%(HumanEval) with fewer model calls vs multi-step TextGrad pipelines -> COSTO-TOKENS;ITERACION. F confirms F_screening (WRITE;RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO;PROCEDIMENTAL) + adds COSTO.

title: Mind-Tool: Domain Memory Architecture for AI Agents
benchmarks: NINGUNO
fallos_mitigaciones: NINGUNO
cita: Chrysochos (2026). Mind-Tool: Domain Memory Architecture for AI Agents.
notes: Single-author production case study (90-day home-lab+VPS infra deployment), not a controlled experiment vs an academic benchmark. Memory Folder = versioned markdown files in Git (infra state, operational history/incidents, decision records, procedural runbooks) -> representacion=DOCS-ARCHIVOS, mem_tipos spans episodic(incidents)/semantic(infra state,decisions)/procedural(runbooks). Fig.3 caption explicitly names 'consolidation' of accumulated knowledge -> CONSOLIDACION. Table1: 147 files/8437 lines, 68% tasks automated, 2.3min(automated) vs 8.7min(human-assisted), 62% time reduction (15h/week), 94% success, 6% error(non-reasoning/network), 91% escalation accuracy, 34 reused workflows (5.8 avg reuse), 18 troubleshooting patterns. Fig.4: 85% time reduction vs manual, 73% vs stateless AI. No controlled ablation isolating memory presence (comparison to 'stateless AI'/manual baselines is informal/anecdotal, not measured on the same tasks) -> evidencia_tipo=MEDICION-COSTO;CUALITATIVA not ABLATION/BENCHMARK-E2E. Desired-State component = persisted conversational goal-tracking -> plan_estado=SI. Git version-control provides change-tracking but no explicit content verification/staleness-resolution mechanism -> fidelidad_procedencia=NO. Single-agent pattern (explicit contrast to Anthropic's two-agent pattern) -> multiagente=NO. F differs from F_screening (PROCEDIMENTAL only): added WRITE, DOCS-VERSIONADO (git-versioned md files central to the architecture), COSTO (62%/94% quantified efficiency), CONSOLIDACION.

title: LongMemEval-V2: Evaluating Long-Term Agent Memory Toward Experienced Colleagues
benchmarks: LongMemEval-V2 (own; built from WebArena OneStopShop/CMS/Reddit + WorkArena/WorkArena++ ServiceNow trajectories)
fallos_mitigaciones: NINGUNO
cita: Wu et al. (2026). LongMemEval-V2: Evaluating Long-Term Agent Memory Toward Experienced Colleagues.
notes: Sec.3.3 formal Insert/Query context-gathering formulation is the core RQ3 measurement (mide_lectura=SI -> RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO required in F). 451 curated Qs over 5 abilities (static/dynamic/workflow/gotchas/premise) paired w/ 100-500-trajectory haystacks (25M/115M tokens). Two own baselines: AgentRunbook-R (S4.1, RAG: raw-state-slice pool + state-transition-event pool + procedure/hint-note pool, dense retrieval per pool -> VECTOR+EMBEDDINGS) and AgentRunbook-C (S4.2, stores trajectories as files, coding-agent harness searches/inspects at query time -> DOCS-ARCHIVOS+GREP-ARCHIVOS-like file exploration). Note pool explicitly 'consolidate[s] trajectory experience into compact reusable knowledge' -> CONSOLIDACION. Main results (S5, abstract): simple RAG state-slice 40.1%; AgentRunbook-R 57.8%; off-the-shelf Codex 69.3% at ~182s/query (6.9x slower than AgentRunbook-R); AgentRunbook-C best at 72.5% accuracy, 32% faster than Codex -> LATENCIA explicitly reported alongside accuracy (accuracy-latency Pareto frontier). Pilot studies (Fig.4): frontier LLMs w/o trajectory history top out at 14.1% (parametric knowledge insufficient); oracle-trajectory/oracle-slices+notes ablation isolates retrieval-vs-grounding difficulty -> ABLATION. F_screening confirmed (RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO;PROCEDIMENTAL) + added WRITE(Insert API), CONSOLIDACION, COSTO(latency/query-cost central finding).

title: PREPING: Building Agent Memory without Tasks
benchmarks: AppWorld, BFCL v3, MCP-Universe
fallos_mitigaciones: Uncontrolled synthetic practice yields redundant/infeasible/uninformative tasks and can contaminate memory with misleading guidance from unfiltered trajectories; mitigated via Validator feasibility-gated admission (score=5/5 required before solver-memory insertion, Sec.3.4) plus proposer-memory practice-history tracking of over/under-used tools to avoid redundancy (Sec.3.3). Table2 component ablation: removing the Validator raises Infeasible-Task% and lowers Unique-Tools/Weighted-Recall (e.g. AppWorld all-disabled=Naive Task Generation drops to 47.8/26.8 TGC/SGC vs full PREPING 83.7/70.2).
cita: Choi et al. (2026). PREPING: Building Agent Memory without Tasks.
