notes: Pre-task (cold-start) procedural memory construction w/o any target-environment task data: Proposer/Solver/Validator loop (Sec.3.2) builds proposer memory Mprop (construction-time control state: practice history + grounded-environment view) and solver memory Msol (deployment-facing playbook, distilled into 'compact procedural bullets' -> CONSOLIDACION per reflector-curator style of ACE). Validator gates admission (feasibility score must be 5) -> ADMISION + FIDELIDAD (grounding/feasibility verification before write). Table1 main results: PREPING improves over no-memory Base by +17.1pp AppWorld, +19.3pp BFCL v3, +5.4pp MCP-Universe avg; exceeds ACE-Offline on AppWorld, competitive w/ ACE-Online. Deployment cost 2.99x lower (AppWorld) / 2.23x lower (BFCL v3) than ACE-Online when frozen (no online memory-update calls) -> COSTO. Table2 ablates Validator/Env.Info/Practice-History components on AppWorld+BFCL v3. Table3/Fig.3: PREPING+ACE warm-start improves AppWorld 71.3->76.3 and mitigates online cold-start. Retrieval mechanism at deployment not specified (solver memory supplied wholesale to agent, no ranking/embedding/graph retrieval described) -> retrieval=NA. Solver/proposer memory scoped per target environment (not per-task, not cross-org) -> alcance=PROYECTO.

title: EvoMemBench: Benchmarking Agent Memory from a Self-Evolving Perspective
benchmarks: EvoMemBench (own; built from MemoryAgentBench, BFCL-Multiturn-LongContext/Base, CL-Bench, xbench-DeepSearch, WebWalkerQA, ALFWorld) vs LoCoMo/LongMemEval/StuLife/MemoryBench/Evo-Memory/MemoryArena
fallos_mitigaciones: Finding3: appended memory becomes net-negative at large context budgets (128K, several methods fall below no-memory baseline) because it 'can introduce noise or consume useful context space without adding sufficient information'; Finding4: aggressive short-term compression loses fine-grained execution details (MemAgent/MemoBrain underperform the no-memory baseline at 16K/32K/128K on I N E P-E XEC) -> implied mitigation is matching memory granularity/compression aggressiveness to task needs rather than uniform compression.
cita: Wang et al. (2026). EvoMemBench: Benchmarking Agent Memory from a Self-Evolving Perspective.
notes: Pure benchmark (mem_tipos/representacion/operaciones/trigger/retrieval=NA per rule5): compares 15 existing memory methods (retrieval-augmented BM25/Qwen3-Emb/GraphRAG, short-term MemAgent/MemoBrain, general long-term Mem0/A-MEM/MemOS/MemoryOS, procedural AWM/SkillWeaver/AgentKB/ACE/ReasoningBank, meta-evolution MemEvolve) + long-context baselines across 4 settings (in/cross-episode x knowledge/execution). mide_lectura=SI: whole benchmark measures downstream task success attributable to memory retrieval across settings (Sec.5, Table3-6) -> RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO. Sec.3.3 explicitly defines 'Execution evolution' memory content as 'task progress, intermediate results, tool outputs, unresolved subgoals, previous decisions' -> plan_estado=SI (RQ Q4 axis is literally what this axis measures). Finding2 (Table3): memory methods stronger at retention than 'revision' (updating/suppressing/replacing memory when later evidence conflicts with earlier evidence, FactConsolidation subset) = explicit staleness/consistency evaluation -> fidelidad_procedencia=SI, FIDELIDAD. Finding3/Finding5 = explicit NEGATIVO findings (memory underperforms no-memory baseline at large context / on easy cross-episode tasks). Token usage reported as efficiency metric (Fig.2) alongside accuracy -> COSTO-TOKENS/COSTO. Scope spans TAREA (in-episode) to PROYECTO (cross-episode, shared-context reuse across episodes, e.g. C ROSS E P-K NOW/T OOL groupings).

title: MUSE-Autoskill: Self-Evolving Agents via Skill Creation, Memory, Management, and Evaluation
benchmarks: SkillsBench, SkillLearnBench
fallos_mitigaciones: Identifies 4 gaps in prior AutoSkill lines (Sec.1): creation-usage mismatch, no structured per-skill memory, static unvalidated skills, poor long-horizon context handling. Mitigated respectively via: built-in skill_create invoked from the runtime loop; per-skill .memory.md accumulating notes/failure-modes/quirks across tasks; unit-test-driven Evaluator that blocks registration until tests pass and auto-triggers Refiner on failure; adaptive short-term-memory compression + cross-session persistence. Table11 diagnostic ablation: memory-system-off round2 accuracy 60.0% vs memory-system-on 74.0% (+14.0pp), at comparable/lower token+latency cost (423.9k tok/295.4s on vs 408.4k tok/338.6s off).
cita: Lin et al. (2026). MUSE-Autoskill: Self-Evolving Agents via Skill Creation, Memory, Management, and Evaluation.
notes: Multi-level memory: short-term (task context, adaptively compressed -> TRABAJO), long-term (persistent cross-session lessons/quirks -> SEMANTICA), and skill-level .memory.md per SKILL.md (per-skill accumulated experience -> PROCEDIMENTAL). Skill catalog metadata injected into system prompt, agent 'selects the most relevant skill during planning' -> retrieval=RANKING (no embeddings/graph described). Sec.3.2 Skill Management: refinement (update_skill on test-fail=ACTUALIZACION), merging of overlapping skills=CONSOLIDACION, pruning of unused/failing skills=OLVIDO; registration blocked until tests pass=ADMISION+FIDELIDAD. Headline SkillsBench: MUSE best human-skill accuracy 59.67% (+12.72pp vs no-skill), best self-created-skill 53.42% (all-task) beating Codex 47.52%/Claude Code 44.27%; self-created skills transfer to Hermes at 51.90% > Hermes-w/-human-skills 48.02% -> explicit cross-agent transfer experiment (Table1, unique among compared methods) -> multiagente=SI. Table11 (App.) isolated memory-system on/off ablation on SkillLearnBench: 74.0% vs 60.0% round-2 accuracy (+14.0pp) with token/turn/latency reported -> COSTO. F_screening (PROCEDIMENTAL;WRITE) confirmed + added CONSOLIDACION, FIDELIDAD, MULTIAGENTE, COSTO.

title: MemPro: Agentic Memory Systems as Evolvable Programs
benchmarks: LongMemEval, LoCoMo, HotpotQA, NarrativeQA
fallos_mitigaciones: Fixed memory-construction-retrieval (MCR) pipelines struggle with heterogeneous task-specific failure modes and drift out of alignment as the memory bank evolves in scale/structure, causing incomplete retrieval, noisy evidence, or ineffective use of retrieved memories (Sec.1). Mitigated by treating the whole MCR pipeline (not just the memory bank or prompts) as an evolvable program: an Evolving Agent diagnoses recurring failure modes from a version-tree of evaluation logs and applies failure-mode-guided edit-debug refinement (Sec.4).
cita: Liu et al. (2026). MemPro: Agentic Memory Systems as Evolvable Programs.
notes: MCR pipeline formalized Sec.3: memory-bank construction Mt=UPDATE(Mt-1,dMt) from segmented raw data (WRITE;ACTUALIZACION, EVENTO-DETERMINISTA per timestep) + iterative Research-Agent retrieval-integration-reflection loop over the bank. App.A.6 retrieval-tool ablation: 'module uses three retrieval channels: BM25 keyword retrieval, BAAI/bge-m3 semantic retrieval[EMBEDDINGS], and structural[page_index] retrieval'; BM25 most important channel (removing it drops accuracy 84.93->lower) -> RANKING+EMBEDDINGS, mide_lectura=SI/RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO. Fig.3 4-way component ablation on LoCoMo (w/o Code / w/o Version-Tree / w/o Iterative-Expansion / w/o Evolution) all show clear drops vs full MemPro (84.93 GPT-4o-mini / 81.23 Qwen3). Table1/Table2 SOTA across LongMemEval/LoCoMo (LLM-as-judge) and HotpotQA/NarrativeQA (F1); MemPro-5/10/15 = 5/10/15 evolution iterations, keeps improving (+1.59/+1.95 LongMemEval, +1.06/+1.20 LoCoMo across iteration bands). Fig.4 token-cost-vs-accuracy efficiency analysis (App.A: 'Token cost is computed over task-time inference only and excludes offline evolution calls') -> COSTO-TOKENS. No multi-agent memory sharing (single Memory Agent + single Research Agent) -> multiagente=NO; no staleness/provenance verification discussed -> fidelidad_procedencia=NO.

title: Neural Procedural Memory: Empowering LLM Agents with Implicit Activation Steering
benchmarks: ALFWorld, WebShop, ScienceWorld, BabyAI
fallos_mitigaciones: Textual procedural memory (RAG-style explicit instructions) can introduce a 'text-action disconnect': the agent comprehends retrieved workflow text but fails to align it onto the execution trajectory, omitting intermediate steps (Fig.1 right, cleaning-step omission example). Mitigated by bypassing text altogether: NPM distills procedural signals directly into activation-space steering vectors injected into the residual stream, eliminating the text-to-action translation step.
cita: Zhao et al. (2026). Neural Procedural Memory: Empowering LLM Agents with Implicit Activation Steering.
notes: Training-free framework: dual-granularity contrastive experience (inter-trajectory success-vs-failure; intra-trajectory effective-vs-degenerate steps, Sec.3.1) distilled into steering vectors stored as a 'historical memory repository' of hidden-state representations (Sec.3.2) -> mem_tipos=PROCEDIMENTAL, representacion=VECTOR (continuous activation vectors, explicitly NOT the 'parametric approaches that encode knowledge within model weights permanently' the paper contrasts itself against, S2). Inference: dense retriever fetches top-K similar historical tasks -> EMBEDDINGS (S3.3) -> mide_lectura=SI (paper's core comparison: dynamic task-specific retrieval-synthesis vs static fixed CAA/Mass-Mean shifts, 'retrieving contextually relevant historical pairs...provides more accurate behavioral correction'). Table1: NPM raises MiniCPM3-4B avg 22.60->28.87, Qwen3-8B 30.63->36.32; Hybrid NPM+Workflows best overall (Qwen3-8B ALFWorld 66.42%, ScienceWorld 31.89). Fig.3 ablates intra/inter/both granularity. App.D reports storage/latency analysis (steering avoids context-window token consumption) -> COSTO/LATENCIA. Sec.5 PCA/cosine-similarity analyses of vector geometry are representational (not a formal metric) so not counted in metricas. No multi-agent sharing or explicit staleness/provenance handling.

title: Parametric Skills
benchmarks: six SWE task categories (Feature/Patch, Robustness Fix, Refactor/API Migration, Performance/Data, Diagnosis/Search, Configuration/Integration) judged by DeepSeek-V4-Flash + F1/BERTScore; HumanEval
fallos_mitigaciones: Two motivating failures of text-space skills (Sec.1): (i) instruction-following bottleneck -- models struggle to locate/adhere to key skill instructions in long/complex contexts (ICL underperforms fine-tuning, gap widens as model size decreases); (ii) skill evolution decoupled from model learning -- text-based skill-library evolution (EvoSkill/CoEvoSkills/SkillOpt) leaves the underlying model unoptimized. Mitigated by converting skills to parameter space via a hypernetwork (context-free exploitation, no context-window cost) and coupling skill self-evolution directly with parametric merging (Sec.3.4).
cita: Zhao et al. (2026). Parametric Skills.
notes: Converts free-form textual skills into LoRA adapters via a trained hypernetwork (Sec.2.2/3.1): skill description embedded -> hypernetwork generates flattened LoRA A/B factors merged into the frozen base model -> representacion=PARAMETROS. Table1: ParametricSkills beats In-Context (LLM-judge 64.09 vs 57.65, +6.44pp) and No-Skill (50.21) and SHINE baseline (48.48) across 6 SWE domains (F1/BERTScore/LLM-judge). Table2: multi-skill merging ablation -- rank-concatenation merge (Avg.Judge 60.12) beats single-LoRA (58.27) and factor-wise-linear merge (56.15), vs base model 12.44 -> CONSOLIDACION. Table3: self-evolving loop on HumanEval (generation->parametric compile->verifier accept/reject->text revision->recompile, Sec.3.4) -- initial generated-skill LoRA underperforms base (123/164=75.0%) but self-evolved LoRA reaches 139/164=84.76% (verifier gate before EMA-merge into global skill = FIDELIDAD). Continual-learning experiment: online EMA merging of accepted task skills into a global parametric skill outperforms independent per-task self-evolution -> alcance spans per-task exploitation (TAREA) and cross-task global-skill accumulation (PROYECTO). No traditional text/embedding retrieval mechanism described (skills applied by tag or merged directly, not ranked/searched) -> retrieval=NA.

title: Memp: Exploring Agent Procedural Memory
benchmarks: TravelPlanner, ALFWorld
fallos_mitigaciones: Without procedural memory, agents either (a) repeatedly attempt illegal/incorrect actions until context complexity exceeds the model's understanding capacity, or (b) complete the task but at far higher cost than the optimal path (Sec.5, egg-heating case study). Mitigated by retrieved procedural guidance that reduces trial-and-error; the Adjustment update policy specifically repairs a P Mem Error by combining a failed retrieved-memory-guided trajectory with the original memory and revising it in place (Fig.2). Validation update policy discards failed/redundant/noisy trajectories before consolidation into memory.
cita: Fang et al. (2025). Memp: Exploring Agent Procedural Memory.
notes: Systematic Build/Retrieve/Update study (Fig.2, Eq.3-7). Build (Table1): Script/Trajectory/Proceduralization all beat No-Memory on TravelPlanner+ALFWorld with fewer steps; Proceduralization (trajectory+script combined) best overall (e.g. GPT-4o ALFWorld-Test 87.14% vs 42.14% no-memory). Retrieve (Table2): key-construction ablation Random-Sample vs Query vs AveFact, cosine-similarity vector matching -> EMBEDDINGS, mide_lectura=SI. Update (Fig.3-4): Vanilla/Validation/Adjustment policies compared over sequential task groups; reflexion-based (Adjustment) update wins by +0.7 vs 2nd-best and -14 steps at final group; Fig.4 M emp beats React/Expel/AWM on ALFWorld (highest success, fewest steps). Fig.5b: procedural memory transfers from GPT-4o to Qwen2.5-14B (+5% completion, -1.6 avg steps on TravelPlanner) -> handoff=CONTENIDO (cross-model memory transfer). Abstract/S1 explicitly claim step-count and token-consumption reductions -> COSTO+ITERACION. Validation policy = admission+forgetting gate on trajectory quality -> ADMISION;OLVIDO;FIDELIDAD. Vanilla update 'consolidates' trajectories into memory 'after every t tasks' -> CONSOLIDACION, trigger=CHECKPOINT.

title: LEGOMem: Modular Procedural Memory for Multi-agent LLM Systems for Workflow Automation
benchmarks: OfficeBench
fallos_mitigaciones: Vanilla (single global-bank) retrieval may fail to surface relevant subtask memories for a given task agent when the retrieved full-task memory's subtask structure diverges from the current task even though the overall task looks similar. Mitigated by LEGOMem-Dynamic (just-in-time per-agent subtask-level retrieval during execution) and LEGOMem-QueryRewrite (query-rewriting into a draft plan before subtask retrieval), both improving task-agent-level memory relevance especially for smaller/SLM agents.
cita: Han et al. (2025). LEGOMem: Modular Procedural Memory for Multi-agent LLM Systems for Workflow Automation.
notes: Multi-agent (orchestrator + task agents, Magentic-One-style) modular procedural memory: offline construction distills SUCCESSFUL trajectories into full-task memories (task description + high-level plan executed -> plan_estado=SI, Sec.3.2.1) and subtask memories (agent behavior/tool-use), stored in a FAISS vector database indexed by dense embeddings (OpenAI text-embedding-3-large) -> representacion=VECTOR, retrieval=EMBEDDINGS, operaciones ADMISION (only successful trajectories curated). Orchestrator receives full-task memories, task agents receive allocated subtask memories -> explicit role-aware CONTENIDO handoff across distinct agents -> multiagente=SI (core RQ4 contribution). Three retrieval/allocation variants compared (vanilla, Dynamic just-in-time, QueryRewrite) -> mide_lectura=SI/RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO. Ablations on OfficeBench (300 tasks, 148 train/152 test) across LLM/Hybrid/SLM team configs: all LEGOMem variants significantly beat No-Memory and baselines Synapse/AWM; orchestrator memory critical for planning/delegation, fine-grained subtask memory most helps smaller agents. No token/latency cost table found in the body (grep negative) -> metricas=EXITO only. No staleness/provenance verification mechanism described -> fidelidad_procedencia=NO.

title: Evaluating Long-Term Memory for Long-Context Question Answering
benchmarks: LoCoMo, QMSum
fallos_mitigaciones: Adding procedural memory (PromptOpt) to RAG/episodic memory shows NEGATIVE results on LoCoMo QA -- attributed to task-mechanism mismatch (procedural memory suits planning/multi-step-reasoning/tool-use tasks, not conversational QA) and to overfitting: qualitative review shows optimized prompts 'focus too closely on specific examples instead of generalizing behavioural patterns' and repeat instructions. Memory-augmented methods also over-generate 'no information available' on adversarial questions for less-capable models, degrading multi-hop performance in the same configuration (Qwen RAG+EpMem: 6.48 F1 multi-hop vs 95.59 F1 adversarial). No explicit mitigation is proposed for these; they are diagnosed as a design/task-fit limitation for future work.
cita: Terranova et al. (2025). Evaluating Long-Term Memory for Long-Context Question Answering.
notes: Unified comparison of Full-Context vs RAG(semantic,VECTOR,bge-m3 top-k cosine-sim) vs A-Mem(agentic semantic, structured notes 'dynamically linked to related memories' forming an evolving network -> GRAFO) vs PromptOpt(procedural, LangMem-style prompt-optimization via classification+optimization steps) vs EpMem(episodic, ICL over stored question/prediction/label/reflection dicts, top-3 similarity retrieval) on LoCoMo (10 convos, up to 35 sessions/9k tok avg, 5 reasoning types) + QMSum. Table2: memory-augmented approaches reduce token usage >90% (e.g. GPT Full-Context 23265 tok/query vs RAG+EpMem 1305 tok) while competitive/better F1 (GPT RAG+EpMem rank1.83 vs Full-Context rank1.00 but much cheaper) -> COSTO-TOKENS. Table4: base-vs-instruction-tuned ranking shows architecture complexity should scale with model capability (foundation models favor RAG, stronger instruct models gain from episodic+richer semantic). Sec.4.4: 199 episodic reflections manually categorized by error type (omission 47%, temporal-misinterpretation 27%, overgeneralisation 11%). Single-agent, no cross-agent memory sharing; no staleness/provenance mechanism described.

title: Remember Me, Refine Me: A Dynamic Procedural Memory Framework for Experience-Driven Agent Evolution
benchmarks: BFCL-V3, AppWorld
fallos_mitigaciones: Prior 'passive accumulation' frameworks (raw-trajectory or trajectory-level-workflow stores) suffer 3 failure modes (Sec.1): coarse-grained trajectory-level experiences introduce irrelevant info obscuring core logic; fetched experiences applied without adaptation fail in slightly shifted scenarios; lack of timely-update strategy lets the experience pool 'degrade into a mixture of valid insights and toxic noise' over time. Mitigated by ReMe's 3-phase lifecycle: multi-faceted keypoint-level distillation (success/failure/comparative analysis) for high-quality extraction, context-adaptive reuse (usage-scenario indexing + rerank + rewrite) for task-grounded utilization, and utility-based refinement (selective-addition -- only successful trajectories distilled at runtime -- + failure-aware reflection capped at 3 retries + utility-based deletion of experiences with recall-utility below threshold beta after >=alpha retrievals) for progressive optimization.
cita: Cao et al. (2025). Remember Me, Refine Me: A Dynamic Procedural Memory Framework for Experience-Driven Agent Evolution.
notes: Experience E=<omega,e,kappa,c,tau> (scenario,content,keywords,confidence,tools) stored in a vector DB indexed by usage-scenario embedding (text-embedding-v4) -> representacion=VECTOR; validation via LLM-as-judge before storage + similarity-based deduplication -> ADMISION+CONSOLIDACION+FIDELIDAD. Retrieval: top-K=5 cosine-similarity + context-aware LLM reranker + adaptive rewriting -> EMBEDDINGS;RANKING, mide_lectura=SI (Table4 explicit rerank/rewrite ablation: No-Memory 24.41/28.50 -> +ReMe full 29.00/40.67 Avg@4/Pass@4). Table1 main results: ReMe(dynamic) beats No-Memory/A-Mem/LangMem across Qwen3-8B/14B/32B on BFCL-V3+AppWorld; memory-scaling effect: Qwen3-8B+ReMe(dynamic) Pass@4 55.03% > vanilla Qwen3-14B 54.65%; Qwen3-14B+ReMe(dynamic) Avg@4 44.66% > vanilla Qwen3-32B 40.89%. Table2 keypoint-vs-trajectory-level granularity ablation; Table3 component ablation (full-vs-selective addition, +reflection, +deletion: 40.83%->45.17% Avg@4). Fig.3 generalizes across 6 additional LLMs. Utility-based deletion (Eq.1, alpha=5/beta=0.5) = explicit OLVIDO mechanism preventing stale/toxic experience accumulation.

title: REMI: A Novel Causal Schema Memory Architecture for Personalized Lifestyle Recommendation Agents
benchmarks: NINGUNO
fallos_mitigaciones: Sparse/insufficient personal data for a query (below a similarity threshold in the causal-graph mapping) would otherwise force generic advice; mitigated via a vector-threshold fallback mechanism (Sec.4.2.1) that prompts the LLM to hypothesize plausible causal factors from general/commonsense knowledge when personal memory coverage is thin, feeding the hypothesized nodes back into the graph as the enriched starting point for reasoning.
cita: Raman et al. (2025). REMI: A Novel Causal Schema Memory Architecture for Personalized Lifestyle Recommendation Agents.
notes: Personal Causal Knowledge Graph = long-term memory (networkx, nodes=life events/states, weighted directed causal edges) -> GRAFO; FAISS-based embedding retrieval over unstructured memory logs (dual-encoder, fine-tuned all-MiniLM-L6-v2) -> VECTOR/EMBEDDINGS; Causal Reasoner does Graph-of-Thought/Tree-of-Thought n-hop (n=3) traversal -> retrieval=GRAFO too. Ablation vs 2 baselines (Sec.5-6): Memory-Only LLM (RAG, no causal reasoning) and Ablated-CSM (causal traversal, no schema planner) across 28 scenarios. Custom metrics PSS (Personalization Salience Score, cosine-sim context-in-output) and CRA (Causal Reasoning Accuracy) -> metricas=OTRA (not a standard EXITO/ITERACION/COSTO/LATENCIA metric). Overall Scores (Sec.6.3): REMI PSS 0.85-0.92 vs baselines 0.68-0.82; CRA REMI 0.4-0.8 vs Memory-Only 0.0 (across ALL prompts) vs Ablated-CSM 0.2-0.6 inconsistent -> mide_lectura=SI (PSS explicitly measures whether retrieved/memory content is reflected in output) -> RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO. Self-Reflection Loop (Sec.4.2.5) + Counterfactual Verification (Sec.4.3.3) validate causal factors/plan against the graph before finalizing -> fidelidad_procedencia=SI/FIDELIDAD. No established public benchmark used (own 28-scenario evaluation) -> benchmarks=NINGUNO.

title: CodeMem: Architecting Reproducible Agents via Dynamic MCP and Procedural Memory
benchmarks: own 25-task multi-step agentic dataset (Difficulty 1-5) evaluated on Gemini 3 Full/Claude 4.5 Sonnet/GPT-5 Chat via LLM-as-Judge; cites external M3ToolEval numbers (CodeAct vs ReAct, not own measurement)
fallos_mitigaciones: Sec.4 enumerates 4 structural penalties of vanilla CodeAct without a persistence layer: (1) Probabilistic Instability -- non-deterministic trajectory divergence for the same request across sessions; (2) Redundant Computation/Latency -- re-deriving solutions from scratch every time (Ttask=Tplan+Twrite+Tdebug+Texecute); (3) Inability to Retain Feedback -- user corrections lost once the context window closes; (4) Context Drift -- long multi-step tasks lose the high-level goal as history fills with logs/errors. Mitigated respectively by: register_skill freezing validated Python functions into a permanent per-user library for deterministic recall (solves 1+3); CodeMem-Reuse reducing cost to ~Texecute by skipping plan/write/debug phases (solves 2); write_todos as an external Pending/InProgress/Completed checklist enabling State Recovery after context truncation/crashes (solves 4).
cita: Gaurav et al. (2025). CodeMem: Architecting Reproducible Agents via Dynamic MCP and Procedural Memory.
notes: 4-tool architecture (Sec.5.1): search_functions/load_functions (Dynamic MCP tool discovery, Just-in-Time schema loading -> retrieval=GREP-ARCHIVOS not embeddings), write_todos (external plan/progress state -> plan_estado=SI), execute_code (sandbox), register_skill (freezes a validated Python function into the user's permanent library -> WRITE+ADMISION, only logic 'that matches user requirements' after a Trial/Saving/Persistence lifecycle is saved). Sec.6 real-world Outlook-OneDrive case study: agent-generated script processed 7 emails, filtered 3, uploaded 4 files in 14s (O(1) context complexity vs ReAct's O(D) Context Collapse failure mode). Table2 (Sec.7): 25-task own benchmark, Gemini 3 Full 96% min-correctness/7.00 avg-calls/100.48s P50/2.02M tokens vs Claude 4.5 Sonnet 79%/71.38s vs GPT-5 Chat 68% (but only 2.80 avg calls, 'efficiency is illusory' -- exits loop prematurely on edge cases) -> metricas=EXITO;LATENCIA;COSTO-TOKENS;OTRA(avg calls). 'Handshake' confirmation protocol before register_skill = human-in-the-loop verification -> fidelidad_procedencia=SI/FIDELIDAD. Saved skill is both the literal code (CONTENIDO) and a reusable callable interface (CONTRATO).

title: A Benchmark for Procedural Memory Retrieval in Language Agents
benchmarks: own benchmark built from ALFWorld (78 HandCodedTWAgent expert trajectories) + AgentInstruct (336 GPT-4-generated ALFWorld trajectories, 35.2% retained from 954)
fallos_mitigaciones: Documents a 'generalization cliff': embedding-based retrieval (action-only/enriched/combined) performs strongly on familiar (seen) object vocabularies but degrades sharply on novel (unseen) ones, reversing method rankings; controlled ablations attribute this to encoders treating procedures as unordered bags-of-words that discard temporal structure, with corpus scale delivering far larger gains than representation enrichment (an 'architectural ceiling in current encoders'). Partial mitigation: LLM-generated object-agnostic procedural summaries (removing object-specific references) show markedly more stable cross-context behavior than raw-action or state-aware embeddings; the paper motivates structure-aware representations and two-stage retrieval (procedural extraction separated from similarity computation) as future directions, not implemented here.
cita: K and Krishnan (2025). A Benchmark for Procedural Memory Retrieval in Language Agents.
notes: Pure retrieval-quality benchmark (mem_tipos/operaciones/trigger=NA per rule5: no write/consolidation/forgetting mechanism proposed, static pre-built dual corpora): explicitly ISOLATES procedural memory RETRIEVAL from task execution/planning (Sec.1) -> mide_lectura=SI is the entire point of the paper -> RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO, and handoff=NO since what happens after retrieval (execution/agent handoff) is explicitly out of scope by design. 6 retrieval methods compared (action-only/enriched/summary/combined embeddings via all-MiniLM-L6-v2+ChromaDB cosine-sim, plus BM25/keyword lexical baselines later excluded due to leakage) -> representacion/retrieval=VECTOR/EMBEDDINGS. Coverage-balanced 40-query benchmark (EASY/MEDIUM/HARD tiers) + IR metrics MAP/NDCG/Precision@k/Recall@k/F1@k via LLM-as-judge (GPT-5, relevance threshold>=6 calibrated via Fig.2 sensitivity analysis) -> metricas=OTRA (ranking-quality metrics, not EXITO/task-success). 5 validation studies: lexical-overlap correlation, corpus-size ablation (78 vs 336 trajectories), state-aware-vs-action-only format ablation, semantic clustering, human annotation -> evidencia_tipo=ABLATION;BENCHMARK-E2E. Generalization-cliff finding = explicit negative evidence about current memory-retrieval systems -> NEGATIVO.

title: Experience-Evolving Multi-Turn Tool-Use Agent with Hybrid Episodic-Procedural Memory
benchmarks: tau-Bench (Telecom), tau2-Bench (Retail), ToolSandbox, ACEBench
fallos_mitigaciones: Prior tool-graph memory (Liu et al. 2024a) relies solely on transition-success probability for edge weights, leading to a 'tool overuse trap' (repeatedly invoking harmless-but-task-irrelevant tools). Mitigated (Sec.4.2) by adding an efficiency term (weighted by inverse rollout-step count) to the edge-weight formula, balancing accuracy against efficiency. Separately, the paper diagnoses that coarse whole-trajectory episodic memory is too context-specific to transfer, while context-free tool-only graphs ignore dialogue/state; mitigated by the hybrid design that adaptively switches between episodic state-recall (when summarization is invoked) and procedural edge-weight-following (routine steps).
cita: Li et al. (2026). Experience-Evolving Multi-Turn Tool-Use Agent with Hybrid Episodic-Procedural Memory.
notes: State-annotated tool-transition graph G=(V,E,W,S) built from successful historical trajectories only (ADMISION): nodes=tools, edge weight w=procedural transition frequency+efficiency (CONSOLIDACION of repeated patterns), edge episodic annotation=compact LLM-generated state summaries st=phi(ht) attached when the agent invokes an autonomous summarization tool (DISCRECIONAL-LLM trigger) -> representacion/retrieval=GRAFO. Inference (Fig.2): locate last-tool node -> if summarization invoked, compare state-summary similarity across connected edges and rank top-k (RANKING); else select top-k by edge weight. Memory updated online with new successful trajectories during RL rollout (ACTUALIZACION, EVENTO-DETERMINISTA). Table1: H-EPM beats basic-retrieval and ReasoningBank baselines up to 50%+ inference gains across 4 benchmarks, more pronounced for weaker base models (GPT-4.1-mini > GPT-4.1); Table3: H-EPM+GRPO beats base-GRPO and AgentEvolver by up to 40%+ on OOD tasks, while naive SFT-on-H-EPM-trajectories overfits and hurts performance -> mide_lectura=SI/RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO. Summarized states explicitly capture 'task context, current progress, and environmental feedback' -> plan_estado=SI. No staleness/provenance verification described (success-filter is the only quality gate) -> fidelidad_procedencia=NO.

title: Unifying Dynamic Tool Creation and Cross-Task Experience Sharing through Cognitive Memory Architecture
benchmarks: GAIA
fallos_mitigaciones: Fig.4/discussion identifies an emerging drift risk (flagged, not actively mitigated in this work): as the curriculum progresses, embedding-based retrieval increasingly favors agent-created tools/subplans (episodic memory) over human-crafted demonstrations (semantic memory), moving 'from near-zero to saturation'; the authors note this 'raises questions about long-term dependency on model-generated content' and risk of 'drift toward model-specific biases,' losing human-expertise grounding -- an unaddressed self-reinforcement concern for future work.
cita: Liu et al. (2025). Unifying Dynamic Tool Creation and Cross-Task Experience Sharing through Cognitive Memory Architecture.
notes: Hierarchical memory M={Mproc,{Msem,Mep}} following CoALA (Sumers et al.): Mproc=static system-prompt/parametric behavioral knowledge, Msem=externally-provided human-crafted tools+few-shot demos (cold-start), Mep=per-agent-role online task-execution trajectories (Eq.4), all embedded at equivalent granularity (text-embedding-3-large dense + Splade sparse, Reciprocal Rank Fusion) -> representacion/retrieval=VECTOR/EMBEDDINGS. Memory added only 'upon successful task completion' -> ADMISION. Table1 SOTA on GAIA: 81.8% Pass@1, +6.6% over Alita (tool-creation, 75.2%), +10.9% over Memento (experience-sharing, 70.9%). Table3/Fig.3 component ablation: removing curriculum learning -10.3%, removing episodic memory sharing -13.9%, removing cold-start demonstrations -21.8% -> mide_lectura=SI/RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO (episodic-memory-sharing ablation directly isolates retrieval's contribution). Episodic state st explicitly includes 'task context, current progress, and environmental feedback' -> plan_estado=SI. Each agent role j keeps its OWN episodic repository ('agent-specific repositories for each sub-agent') rather than one pool shared across distinct agent roles -> multiagente=NO despite the 'Shared Memory' name (sharing is cross-TASK for the same role, not cross-agent-role).

title: Synthesizing Procedural Memory: Challenges and Architectures in Automated Workflow Generation
benchmarks: NINGUNO
fallos_mitigaciones: Identifies 4 structural bottlenecks in AUTOMATED synthesis of procedural memory (companion to CodeMem, same authors): Discovery Gap (injecting 1000+ tool JSON schemas exceeds context/degrades attention -> 'function hallucination' of non-existent parameters), mitigated by Dynamic MCP search_functions/load_functions querying a vector DB of tool descriptions Just-in-Time. Verification Gap (Structure Hallucination -- LLM guesses a wrong JSON shape for enterprise API responses, e.g. assuming a bare list instead of an {'@odata.context',...,'value':[...]} envelope, causing a runtime TypeError crash), mitigated by a mandatory 'Probe Phase' (Sample-limit-k -> Inspect-stdout -> Codify-schema-lock) before writing the final workflow. Decomposition Gap ('Reflection Trap': a LATS/MCTS search-based agent on HumanEval/83 spirals into an ineffective patch loop, generating incorrect base-9 'magic number' logic instead of deriving the closed-form 18*10^(n-2) formula, Fig.1), mitigated by Linear State Anchoring (write_todos as an external Pending/InProgress/Completed program-counter) plus intrinsic chain-of-thought derivation instead of heavy inference-time search. Scaling Gap (sequential per-item processing times out / a mid-run crash on item #4,999 forces a stateless restart with duplicates), mitigated via asyncio concurrency (~33min sequential vs ~2min concurrent estimate for 1000 emails) + proposed external persistence checkpoints (SQLite/Google Sheets) + defensive idempotent folder-creation (try/except).

title: Channel Fracture: Architectural Blind Spots in Scheduled Cross-Agent Memory Injection for Multi-Agent Orchestration Systems

fallos_mitigaciones: Central topic = 'channel fracture': a systematic SILENT failure where scheduled(cron) agent sessions cannot access the target agent's memory tools (skip_memory=True hardcoded scheduler guard + conditional memory-tool registration bypassed in cron context, Sec.2.2-2.3/Listing1-2) -- writer-side verification passes while receiver-side memory stays empty, undetectable without inverse (receiver-side) verification. cita: Liu (2026). Channel Fracture: Architectural Blind Spots in Scheduled Cross-Agent Memory Injection for Multi-Agent Orchestration Systems.
notes: Sec.2.4: Hermes Agent 'holographic memory' = SQLite-backed fact store (facts/entities/fact_entities tables) with FTS5 full-text search, categorized memory banks, entity tracking -> mem_tipos=SEMANTICA (persistent structured facts across sessions/agents/tasks per Abstract), representacion=DOCS-ARCHIVOS (structured DB tables + FTS index, no vectors/graph). Sec.3.3: three injection channels tested -- (A) direct SQLite write, (B) target-agent self-write via memory() tool call at admin's instruction (agent decides to invoke its own tool -> trigger DISCRECIONAL-LLM), (C) cron-delegated write (scheduled/periodic job -> trigger CHECKPOINT); Channel C fails completely (skip_memory=True at scheduler.py:1652 + conditional tool registration at agent_init.py:1168, Sec.4.1.3/4.1.4) -> operaciones=WRITE (the paper's entire subject is write-channel reliability, no admission/consolidation/forgetting lifecycle discussed). Sec.2.4: full-text search (FTS5) is the only described retrieval mechanism -> retrieval=GREP-ARCHIVOS. Table5/CADVP RV dimensions (RV-1..RV-4: Read Availability/Correctness/Completeness/Timeliness) + Sec.8 L2 'injected data compared against source data byte-by-byte' explicitly verify read-side correctness/completeness of memory retrieval -> mide_lectura=SI, F includes RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO. alcance=PROYECTO: holographic memory persists 'across sessions, agents, and tasks' per profile (Abstract), not single-task/session bound. multiagente=SI (cross-agent injection is the paper's core scenario, five specialized profiles Table1). fidelidad_procedencia=SI: L2 SHA-256 content-hash + timestamped log trail + byte-comparison, L3 independent cross-review agent scoring q in[0,1] with tau=0.9 threshold (Sec.8.2.2-8.2.3) -> F also FIDELIDAD. title: Trust-Aware Multi-Agent Traceability: Confidence-Calibrated Knowledge Graphs for Consistent Software Artifact Management

title: When Disagreement Means Learning (or Bias): Human-Governed Memory Consolidation and Counterfactual Diagnosis in Multi-Agent LLM Scoring
benchmarks: custom 108-item dataset (68 software-engineering work items: 38 public GitHub issues + 30 authored; 40 real-estate listings: 20 public/collected + 20 authored), 3 independent runs on gpt-4o-mini + replication on 2 further base models incl. one cross-vendor; no public benchmark
fallos_mitigaciones: Central mechanism: instance-channel leakage -- a learned correction bleeds onto unrelated same-domain Neutral items it should not affect (real-estate Neutral warm +0.353 vs Holdout-Sim +0.243), because retrieval treats every same-domain item as somewhat similar. Mitigated by human-governed consolidation: when corrections cluster (k>=3) an LLM drafts a rubric amendment, a human approves, both agents inherit it, and promoted exemplars are retired -- Neutral leak eliminated (7.73->8.12->7.72, back to baseline) while the learned lift is preserved. Separately, a canary/spot-check mechanism (10% of auto-accepts sampled, deterministic hash) guards against runaway learning: a deliberately injected bad lesson (canary phase X1, 'Long listings deserve top scores') was absorbed by 7-9/10 probe items and never flagged by the disagreement signal alone (small per-item increments stay within the agreement band); the spot-check is the explicit backstop for this poisoning-adjacent failure mode.
cita: Jawed (2026). When Disagreement Means Learning (or Bias): Human-Governed Memory Consolidation and Counterfactual Diagnosis in Multi-Agent LLM Scoring.
notes: Sec.2.4/Sec.4.5 explicitly frames the design as 'the episodic-to-semantic consolidation of complementary learning systems: fast instance memory buffers individual experiences, slow structural memory absorbs their regularities' -> mem_tipos=EPISODICA(instance channel: per-correction retrieved exemplars) + SEMANTICA(policy channel: versioned rubric criteria). Instance store = pgvector embeddings of enriched correction text (description+rationale, Sec.4.5); rubric = structured versioned text criteria -> representacion=HIBRIDA. Sec.4.1: k=5 exemplars retrieved by cosine similarity above floor theta -> retrieval=EMBEDDINGS; operaciones WRITE(re-embed+store correction), ADMISION(human approval gates rubric-amendment entry, R3 Governance), CONSOLIDACION(cluster k>=3 -> LLM drafts amendment, title contribution 1), OLVIDO(promoted exemplars retired from retrieval, Sec.4.5 point3), ACTUALIZACION(rubric version v+1 both agents inherit). trigger: instance write on human override event (EVENTO-DETERMINISTA); cluster reaching k>=3 threshold triggers drafting (PRESUPUESTO-like count threshold). Sec.6 Evaluation (C1-C4, Table1-4): entire evaluation measures retrieval-induced score effects (learning separation 0.20=+0.326 Sim vs +0.122 Neutral pooled; leakage; counterfactual attribution recall 0.045 at tau_c=0.75, Table2) -> mide_lectura=SI, F includes RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO. alcance=PROYECTO: correction/rubric store persists 'restricted to the same tenant' across all future scoring requests, cross-session. multiagente=SI (primary+auditor, structurally independent). fidelidad_procedencia=SI: R3 'every version increment names the corrections that caused it' (auditable rubric provenance), deterministic spot-check canary. metricas=EXITO (agreement rate 88.3+-0.5%, learning separation, ECE/calibration-style accuracy proxies; no token/latency numbers reported). evidencia_tipo=ABLATION(phase-based bare instance vs post-promotion comparison, tau_c threshold sweep Fig5) + BENCHMARK-E2E(108-item C1-C4 evaluation). title: HMARS: A Hierarchical Multi-Agent Memory System for Long-Context Reasoning
benchmarks: LongBench-v2-derived long-document benchmark (195 questions, custom-filtered for evidence breadth, RAG recall<=0.5) + custom multi-turn memory benchmark inspired by RealMem (120 dialogues, 24-49 turns, 5-9 key facts each)
fallos_mitigaciones: Central failure mode: passive top-K RAG retrieval discards relevant evidence BEFORE reasoning begins, especially when relevance is context-dependent/scattered across distant regions (Fig.1, Abstract) -- 'RAG stores context; it does not provide a memory system for managing, accessing, and reasoning over evidence.' Mitigated by full-fanout query-conditioned assessment (every sub-agent/region assessed, no early top-K exclusion) plus mid-agent shared regional coordination. Separately, Sec.4.3/Appendix E notes agentic sequential-compression baselines (Chain-of-Agents, MemAgent) 'can lose fine-grained evidence when answers require broad, non-adjacent support' -- an explicit competing-approach failure mode HMARS avoids by never discarding regions.
cita: Li et al. (2026). HMARS: A Hierarchical Multi-Agent Memory System for Long-Context Reasoning.
notes: Sec.3.1-3.2: long document/interaction history partitioned into bounded local regions per sub-agent (page-level access); each sub-agent produces a local memory card (summary,topics,entities,page_index) via Prompt1, mid-agents aggregate cards into shared regional memory (Eq.3-4) -> mem_tipos=TRABAJO (bounded per-document/per-conversation working memory, not cross-session persistence), representacion=DOCS-ARCHIVOS (structured hierarchical page/card records, contrasted explicitly against embedding-only baselines), operaciones=WRITE(card creation)+CONSOLIDACION(cards aggregated into region-level summary uj/submapj/crossrefj). trigger=EVENTO-DETERMINISTA: cards built during 'offline indexing phase' at document ingestion, query-conditioned assessment triggered per query. Core retrieval mechanism is NOT embedding top-K but hierarchical LLM-based query-conditioned page selection/scoring (mid-agent broadcasts query interpretation+hints, sub-agents select pages, Eq.5-6) -> retrieval=RANKING (closest closed-vocab fit; baselines use EMBEDDINGS for comparison but HMARS's own mechanism is agent-based relevance assessment). Sec.4.4 Evidence Coverage Analysis (Table3): explicitly measures supporting-chunk recall (HMARS 0.994 vs RAG K=5,4K 0.571 / K=10,1K 0.331 / K=20,1K 0.572) to isolate memory-access quality from final-answer prompting -> mide_lectura=SI, F RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO. alcance=TAREA (memory built/used per single document or per single multi-turn dialogue, not shared across projects). multiagente=SI (sub-agents+mid-agents+base agent hierarchy). fidelidad_procedencia=SI: page_index preserves original token offsets enabling reconstruction of grounded text spans -> explicit evidence-grounding/provenance mechanism, F FIDELIDAD. Table2: HMARS best overall (83.8% vs Dense Rerank N=100 80.0%, Full-Context 73.0%, GraphRAG 70.7%, CoA-7B 19.6%, MemAgent-14B 27.0%) -> metricas=EXITO. Table3: ~13K prompt tokens vs ~20K(RAG) -> metricas=COSTO-TOKENS; FLOPs/query (~5.2x10^16) -> metricas also OTRA (distinct compute-cost metric). evidencia_tipo=ABLATION(Sec.4.5 coverage/coordination ablation: full-fanout vs dispatched vs no-mid-agent, dropping 0.838->0.762/0.748; Sec.4.6 page-size/sub-agent-capacity granularity sweep)+BENCHMARK-E2E(Table2 vs 5 baseline families)+MEDICION-COSTO(Table3, Fig5 accuracy-compute tradeoff). F differs from F_screening(RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO;MULTIAGENTE): added WRITE, CONSOLIDACION, FIDELIDAD. handoff=CONTENIDO: memory cards/summaries/grounded pages are the actual content passed between sub-agents, mid-agents, and the base agent. plan_estado=NO.

title: HyphaeDB: A Living Knowledge Topology for Agent-First Memory
benchmarks: NINGUNO
fallos_mitigaciones: Sec.9.2 Limitations, 'Contradiction resolution': the system automatically DETECTS contradictions (Sec.5.2, two semantically similar but opposing cells) but does NOT resolve them -- explicit unmitigated gap, resolution options (human arbitration, salience/recency-wins voting) left as future configurable choices. Sec.5.4 'Organic Knowledge Decay' is itself a staleness-handling mechanism: unaccessed cells decay via s(t)=s0*0.99^dt and stop propagating once below threshold, while a new decision superseding a stale one propagates through the region to inform affected agents.

title: From Signals to Structure: How Memory Architecture Drives Language Emergence in LLM Agents
benchmarks: custom Lewis signaling game (referential communication task, gpt-5.4-mini sender/receiver, 200 rounds x 3 studies, 8-object pool, capacity sweep |V|^L in {4..125}); no public benchmark
fallos_mitigaciones: Study2 finding: stateless 'memory only' agents show a high-capacity collapse -- accuracy falls from 0.80(cap=25) to 0.52(cap=64) as collision rate hits 1.0 (every object's modal message collides with another's); the rolling 20-round window cannot accumulate enough evidence per code as the code space expands, and Study3 shows doubling the window (20->40 rounds) produces NO improvement at cap=64, confirming the failure is structural (no persistent carrier of conventions) not merely window-length. This collapse is avoided, not fixed, by switching to a persistent-notebook architecture (scratchpad), which keeps rising to 0.90 at cap=125. Separately, the codebook-meta condition's intended CONSOLIDACION mechanism fails outright: 'rather than developing structural insights... the note freezes by round 30 into generic operational reminders' and 'never becomes higher-order'; combined with the codebook's own lack of a pruning mechanism (stale/conflicting slot entries accumulate over 200 rounds), codebook-meta ends as the WORST private-memory condition (0.460+-0.14), explicitly 'worse than the simpler codebook it extends' -- an unmitigated design failure the paper reports as a negative result.
cita: Talebirad et al. (2026). From Signals to Structure: How Memory Architecture Drives Language Emergence in LLM Agents.
notes: Table1/'Memory Architectures': five conditions (memory only=window-only baseline, env board=shared public convention table, scratchpad=free-form notebook overwritten each round, codebook=10-slot list edited in-place, codebook meta=slot list+persistent meta-note) all layered on a shared rolling window of last-20 (message,target,success) triples -> mem_tipos=TRABAJO (all memory is scoped to a single 200-round game run, not persisted across tasks/sessions); representacion=DOCS-ARCHIVOS (free text/JSON fields: notebook text, slot-list entries, window triples -- no vectors/graph/params in any condition). 'Every memory store is a field of the agent's structured JSON output... the model writes it, the harness parses it and re-injects it' -> operaciones WRITE; scratchpad 'overwritten each round' and codebook 'edited in place... persist verbatim until explicitly overwritten' -> ACTUALIZACION; the fixed 20-round rolling window inherently drops older interactions -> OLVIDO; codebook-meta's meta-note is an explicit (if failed) attempt at CONSOLIDACION ('a persistent abstract meta-note for language-level rules'). trigger: codebook's action in{append,edit,none} is chosen by the LLM's own structured output each round -> DISCRECIONAL-LLM; all conditions update once per round regardless -> also EVENTO-DETERMINISTA. No selective retrieval step exists in ANY condition: the full persistent store is always re-injected wholesale into the next prompt (no relevance filtering) -> retrieval=NA, mide_lectura=NO. alcance=TAREA: memory scoped to one 200-round game instance. multiagente=SI: sender+receiver, 'agents never see each other's private memory' except the environment-compiled shared env board. fidelidad_procedencia=NO: no source/staleness verification mechanism (pure controlled experiment on memory format vs language-emergence quality). Table2/3: accuracy (env board 0.827 best but near-zero TopSim=memorized lookup, not a productive code; scratchpad 0.867+-0.023 at cap=25, most reliable private-memory condition) -> metricas=EXITO; TopSim/Best-MI/collision-rate are specialized compositionality/language-structure metrics -> metricas also OTRA. evidencia_tipo=ABLATION(Study1: 5 architectures at fixed capacity; Study3: window-size sweep m in{5,10,20,40} isolating consolidation-vs-history-length)+BENCHMARK-E2E(Study2: 16-configuration capacity sweep, accuracy vs chance=0.25). F differs from F_screening(MULTIAGENTE only): added WRITE, CONSOLIDACION, NEGATIVO (codebook-meta's consolidation attempt explicitly fails and underperforms its non-consolidating baseline -- an honest negative result about a memory-architecture mechanism). handoff=NO: agents communicate ONLY through the constrained signal channel m in V^L; private memories are never shared or handed off (explicit design constraint), and env board is environment-compiled not agent-to-agent handoff. plan_estado=NO.

title: Memory Is Not Live State — Cross-Agent Memory Governance by Transplanting the Reflective Context Governor onto Agent Memory (memgov v0.1.0)
benchmarks: NINGUNO (single production workspace deployment: 73 memory files across 4 stores, 7 committed rows, one detect-verify-repair cycle; no public benchmark)
fallos_mitigaciones: The paper's entire subject is the 'stale-snapshot problem': persistent memory is a snapshot of the world at write time that does not update when the world moves, which is dangerous specifically for status-bearing claims ('not yet deposited','awaiting review','tool X is broken'). Documented incident (Sec.2, 2026-07-07): an agent's memory still asserted a paper was unpublished a day after it was published; caught only by consulting a machine-readable deposit ledger before acting. Three compounding root causes identified: (1) store fragmentation across project-scoped directories (a fact in one store invisible elsewhere), (2) a session-start guard comparing against the wrong (stale) index, firing unsatisfiable warnings that trained the user to ignore them (alert fatigue), (3) cross-agent staleness (a second agent's 12-day-old memory still described an already-repaired toolchain as broken). Mitigated by memgov v0.1.0: a SHARED_STATE commitment surface (rows overwritten in place with a verification anchor), a deterministic drift scanner producing a CONFLICT_MAP, a non-compensatory review queue (a flagged line can only be redeemed by verifying against its anchor, nothing auto-deleted), and a freshness heartbeat with governed friction (suppression markers to avoid retraining the alert-fatigue failure of root-cause 2). First scan: 73 files vs 7 committed rows -> 17 suspected drifts (confirmed true positives: 3 papers misremembered as unpublished, a repaired toolchain misremembered as broken) -> 14 remaining after verified repair.
cita: Toeda (2026). Memory Is Not Live State — Cross-Agent Memory Governance by Transplanting the Reflective Context Governor onto Agent Memory (memgov v0.1.0).
notes: QUALITY/RECONSIDERAR FLAG: self-published preprint (author's own company MOBIUS LLC; DOI 'reserved, live on Zenodo publication' i.e. not yet formally deposited at extraction time), near-total self-citation (7 of 9 references are the same author's own prior deposits), explicit 'AI co-observer: Claude Fable 5' co-drafting disclosure, and the evidence base is a SINGLE workspace over a SINGLE day (author's own Sec.9 Limitations: 'Single workspace, single day, two agents... this is not yet evidence of general usefulness'); extracted per protocol, inclusion decision left to human reviewer -- note the paper is unusually self-aware/transparent about these limits (explicit falsifiability section, Sec.8). Sec.1: memory = Markdown files agents write at session end describing project/status facts -> mem_tipos=SEMANTICA (status-bearing claims about world state, e.g. 'not yet deposited (DOI:TBD)'), representacion=DOCS-ARCHIVOS ('both agents' memories are Markdown on disk', explicitly 'no embeddings, no model calls' Sec.6). operaciones=WRITE(session-end writes) + ACTUALIZACION(SHARED_STATE rows 'overwritten in place by whichever session changes durable state'); no OLVIDO ('Nothing is auto-deleted'). trigger: memory writes at session end + drift-scan/freshness-heartbeat run via SessionStart hooks (EVENTO-DETERMINISTA); freshness heartbeat also threshold-based (files untouched beyond 2 days, suppressed 3 days after reconciliation) -> CHECKPOINT. retrieval=GREP-ARCHIVOS: 'Deterministic and inspectable. Regex over Markdown; no embeddings' (Sec.6). mide_lectura=NO: the scanner measures STALENESS/drift precision (a fidelity axis), not retrieval-for-use quality; no relevance-ranked reading mechanism exists to measure. alcance=PROYECTO: SHARED_STATE spans the whole 'MOBIUS workspace' (multiple repos, both agents), cross-session. multiagente=SI (Claude Code + GPT Codex, cross-agent governance is the paper's core contribution). fidelidad_procedencia=SI (the paper's entire mechanism: verification anchors, drift detection, commitment surface, append-only measurement ledger). metricas=OTRA: suspected-drift counts (17->14) and queue precision (true positives vs noise) are a domain-specific detection metric, not EXITO/ITERACION/COSTO-TOKENS/LATENCIA; time-to-detection and repair-latency are stated as PLANNED (Sec.8) not yet measured with numbers. evidencia_tipo=BENCHMARK-E2E(a real production system measured on real data: 73 files, 17->14 drifts)+CUALITATIVA(the incident narrative and root-cause analysis dominate the paper). F differs from F_screening(FIDELIDAD;MULTIAGENTE): added WRITE, NEGATIVO (the paper's central contribution IS documenting a real memory-system failure/near-miss -- rule7(b) evidencia negativa sobre memoria). handoff=CONTENIDO: SHARED_STATE row overwrite is explicitly named in the text as 'the cross-agent handoff' (Sec.4, component1). plan_estado=SI: status-bearing claims tracked as memory ('not yet deposited','awaiting owner review before deposit','HOLD') are literally task/deliverable progress-state content.

title: A hierarchical memory architecture overcomes context limits in long-horizon multi-agent computational modeling
benchmarks: custom PKPD model-selection benchmark (20 synthetic datasets) + PK parameter-recovery benchmark (20 profiles from 100,000 synthetic) + literature pipeline benchmark (17 cases: R01-R10 retrieval, E01-E05 extraction w/ 3 hallucination traps, S01-S02 synthesis) + real QSP case studies (Hall 2024 body-weight GLP-1RA, Gattoni cardiac electrophysiology, Kir atenolol PBPK, Shah & Betts mAb PBPK); baseline GitHub Copilot (GHCP); no public benchmark
fallos_mitigaciones: Naive multi-agent context handling (full conversation-history concatenation) causes O(N x T) unbounded token growth and context degradation over long-horizon multi-session projects -- mitigated by capping every memory layer (scratchpad <=20,000/8,000 chars, decision log <=16,000 chars) and EVICTING completed work, keeping mid-term state bounded (median 301 tokens, max 4,050 across 104 runs) instead of growing with conversation length. Separately, hallucination-resistance is explicitly tested via adversarial 'trap' cases in the literature-extraction pipeline: an unretrievable PMID (HTTP404) -> system reports 'no records found' rather than fabricating model details (E01); two off-domain papers supplied -> correctly declined extraction (E02,E04); a mismatched-but-correct-paper PMID -> system detects the mismatch, autonomously locates the correct paper (E05). The PI Agent's mass-balance audit also autonomously DETECTED a mass-conservation inconsistency in a published paper's own parameter table (lung plasma flow exceeding summed peripheral-tissue flows) and imposed a flow-balancing constraint to restore conservation.
cita: Tewari and Kimko (2026). A hierarchical memory architecture overcomes context limits in long-horizon multi-agent computational modeling.
notes: Abstract/Fig.1: explicit THREE-LAYER architecture -- short-term (bounded conversation window + capped scratchpad, updated per turn), mid-term (structured project-state JSON: active requests, recently-modified files, jobs, milestones, session summaries; updated per session), long-term (project-independent domain knowledge: ~24,000-char QSP handbook, physics checklists, RAG over source-paper text) -> mem_tipos=TRABAJO(short-term)+SEMANTICA(mid-term project-state facts)+PROCEDIMENTAL(long-term handbook/physics-checklist validation protocols); representacion=HIBRIDA(structured JSON state + RAG/embedding retrieval of literature). operaciones: WRITE(state updates), ADMISION('capping each state category'), CONSOLIDACION(auto-summarizing decision log, last-3 session summaries), OLVIDO(explicit 'evicting completed work'), ACTUALIZACION(session-level state updates). trigger: updates per-turn/per-session (EVENTO-DETERMINISTA) under explicit character/token budget caps (<=20,000/8,000/16,000 chars) driving eviction -> PRESUPUESTO. retrieval=EMBEDDINGS: 'retrieval augmented generation (RAG) from indexed project publications' for long-term literature layer. Table2/Literature pipeline (Table2): retrieval accuracy 7/10->10/10 after author-anchored reformulation, extraction 5/5 (incl. 3 hallucination traps), synthesis 2/2 -- explicitly isolates and measures memory-READ/retrieval quality -> mide_lectura=SI, F RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO. alcance=PROYECTO: 'long-horizon research workflows requiring multi-session continuity...across 104 project runs'. multiagente=SI (PI + 5 specialist sub-agents: optimization, modeling, reporting, infrastructure, review). fidelidad_procedencia=SI: hallucination-resistance trap cases, autonomous mass-conservation-inconsistency detection in a PUBLISHED paper, calibrated-confidence synthesis flagging author-reported vs inferred values. metricas: PKPD model selection 100%(20/20) vs GHCP 70%; PK recovery 70% vs 20% -> EXITO; Table1 token/cost analysis ($5.14 low-cost-writer vs $10.51 frontier, 5.5x more input tokens) -> COSTO-TOKENS; wall-clock 105min(MAS) vs 18-25min(GHCP), literature-pipeline mean query times 299/175/942s, PI-oversight ablation 28min->60min -> LATENCIA. evidencia_tipo=ABLATION(Fig.3c feature-ablation removing PI Agent physics oversight: accuracy preserved, wall-clock roughly doubles 28->60min)+BENCHMARK-E2E(PKPD/PK-recovery vs GHCP, literature pipeline Table2)+MEDICION-COSTO(Table1). F differs from F_screening(CONSOLIDACION;MULTIAGENTE): added WRITE, RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO, FIDELIDAD, COSTO. handoff=CONTENIDO: mid-term project-state JSON (tasks,files,decisions,milestones) is the structured content that persists and is read across sessions/agents. plan_estado=SI: mid-term state explicitly includes 'recent jobs, milestones, and the last three session summaries' plus 'the five most-recent active user requests (with a running total)' -- literal task/progress-state content.

title: RepLLM: Toward Automatically Reproducing Network Research Results
benchmarks: custom 7-paper network-systems reproduction set (NCFlow, GRooT, Rateless IBLT, SelfStarter, NetDice, Teal, NetChain from SIGCOMM/NSDI); baselines Standalone LLM, Claude Code CLI (low/medium/high); no public benchmark
fallos_mitigaciones: Sec.6.8.2 Impact of Shared Memory (Table6, ablated on SelfStarter): ALL shared-memory-removal variants exhibit the SAME failure pattern -- apparent execution SUCCESS with semantically INCOMPLETE outputs (misleading pass/fail signal). Without Shared Memory entirely: paper context reduced two orders of magnitude, yields a trivial script that succeeds only by checking for an output directory. Without Architecture Memory: runnable scaffold but core modules unimplemented. Without Structured Paper Memory: parser relies on mocked behavior, hollow summaries despite consuming 1.1M tokens. Without Interface Memory: later modules drift from earlier interface commitments, causing a failed configuration-parsing case to be treated as success. Explicit conclusion: 'token efficiency alone is misleading in long-horizon agentic reproduction; the memory layer is essential for enforcing semantic completeness and cross-stage consistency under context constraints.' Full pipeline mitigates by keeping the four memory components (Shared/Architecture/Structured-Paper/Interface) jointly active.
cita: Jiang et al. (2026). RepLLM: Toward Automatically Reproducing Network Research Results.
notes: Sec.3/Fig.2: 4-agent pipeline (Content Parsing Agent, Architecture Design Agent, Code Generation Agent, Audit & Repair Agent) coordinated through an explicit 'Shared Memory mechanism' (paper.json, appendix.json, arch.json, data_schema/, code/) 'to ensure global context consistency' -> mem_tipos=TRABAJO (task-scoped working store for ONE reproduction run), representacion=DOCS-ARCHIVOS (standardized JSON representation, key-value stored, no vectors/graph/params). Sec.4.1: CPA 'reorganize[s] raw document content into a structured JSON representation' -> operaciones CONSOLIDACION; Sec.3.1.3 repair loop 'reads current code and context, fixes discrepancies, updates the files' -> ACTUALIZACION; WRITE = all phases persist artifacts to Shared Memory. title: MIRIX: Multi-Agent Memory System for LLM-Based Agents
benchmarks: ScreenshotVQA (novel benchmark introduced in this paper: 5,000-20,000 screenshots per sequence x 3 PhD students, 87 questions total) + LOCOMO
fallos_mitigaciones: Sec.3.2: without explicit retrieval triggering, 'the language model often defaults to its parametric knowledge, which may be outdated or incorrect' -- worked example: user tells the agent 'The CEO of Twitter is Linda Yaccarino' (stored in memory), and days later when asked 'Who is the CEO of Twitter?' with that message no longer in the visible conversation history, the model may incorrectly answer 'Elon Musk' from stale parametric knowledge instead of consulting stored memory. Mitigated by the Active Retrieval mechanism: the agent is required to generate a topic BEFORE answering/acting, and this topic auto-triggers retrieval from all six memory components (top-10 per component), injected into the system prompt tagged by source -- eliminating the need for explicit 'search your memory' prompting on every turn.
cita: Wang and Chen (2025). MIRIX: Multi-Agent Memory System for LLM-Based Agents.
notes: Sec.1/Fig.1/Sec.3.1: six explicit memory components map almost 1:1 onto the RQ1 vocabulary -- Core Memory(persona+human blocks, always-visible)=TRABAJO; Episodic Memory(time-stamped events: event_type,summary,details,actor,timestamp)=EPISODICA; Semantic Memory(concepts/entities/relationships independent of time, w/ source field)=SEMANTICA; Procedural Memory(how-to guides/workflows/scripts as steps lists)=PROCEDIMENTAL; Resource Memory(docs/images/voice_transcripts)+screenshot-based multimodal input=MULTIMODAL; Knowledge Vault(verbatim secrets, folded into SEMANTICA facts here since no dedicated vault token exists). representacion=HIBRIDA: structured typed entries (fields per component) + multiple retrieval methods (embedding_match, bm25_match, string_match, Sec.3.2) -> retrieval=EMBEDDINGS;RANKING;GREP-ARCHIVOS. operaciones: WRITE(Memory Managers 'update their respective memories in parallel'), ADMISION(Meta Memory Manager 'determines which memory components are relevant, routing the input'), CONSOLIDACION('ensuring that redundant information is avoided within each memory type'), ACTUALIZACION(Core Memory 'triggers a controlled rewrite process' at 90% capacity; Semantic entries 'persist unless conceptually overwritten'). trigger: memory update fires 'when new input is received from the user' (EVENTO-DETERMINISTA); app-level batching 'once 20 unique screenshots are collected, the memory update process is triggered' (PRESUPUESTO, count threshold). title: Smarter Together: Creating Agentic Communities of Practice through Shared Experiential Learning
fallos_mitigaciones: Central motivating problem (Sec.1): memory-less coding agents suffer 'silos and amnesia' -- crucial information is (i) eventually dropped from the current session's context, (ii) not shared between sessions, and (iii) not shared between agents working with different users -- 'each interaction starts a new learning loop which has a limited lifespan.' Mitigated by Spark's shared collective memory layer where every agent interaction is captured as a portable trace, merged into a collective knowledge space via continuous autonomous curation, and redistributed to agents facing similar future challenges -- restoring the self-healing property that human developer communities of practice had before AI intermediation. The curation loop also explicitly tracks 'which memory patterns and paths effectively guide (and do NOT guide) coding agents toward increasingly more optimal solutions', i.e. it learns from unsuccessful recommendation patterns, not only successful ones.
cita: Tablan et al. (2025). Smarter Together: Creating Agentic Communities of Practice through Shared Experiential Learning.
notes: Sec.1.1/3: Spark treats 'every coding agent interaction as a potential learning event' captured as a structured/portable 'trace' of experience -> mem_tipos=EPISODICA; traces are 'analyzed to extract generalizable knowledge patterns... clustered by semantic similarity, and curated' into best-practice recommendations -> mem_tipos also SEMANTICA(distilled patterns)+PROCEDIMENTAL(coding best-practice/API-usage guidance, the domain is explicitly software development). Sec.3.1 Knowledge Base: documentation 'represented in multiple modalities (such as embeddings or raw text search indices)'; Retrieval Agent uses a 'hybrid search-and-generation approach combin[ing] generic semantic similarity estimates via vector search, text search at multiple levels of lexical scope' -> representacion=HIBRIDA, retrieval=EMBEDDINGS;RANKING. operaciones: WRITE('Spark captures multi-level contexts around each coding problem, the recommendation...and feedback'), ADMISION(curation 'in relation to different optimization criteria' gates what becomes durable curated knowledge vs raw trace), CONSOLIDACION('extract generalizable knowledge patterns, clustered by semantic similarity, and curated'), ACTUALIZACION('Memory-augmented Learning: Memory is augmented based on feedback'; 'Retrieval rankings are refined based on what worked...previously'). trigger: trace capture 'after each interaction' (EVENTO-DETERMINISTA); curation runs over 'Memory Epochs' that 'repeat iteratively' (CHECKPOINT, Sec.3.2). Sec.'Paper Summary'+Sec.4.4: separately measures (a) downstream code-quality lift from WITH-SPARK vs NO-SPARK across 3 models on DS-1000, AND (b) 'the intrinsic quality of recommendations generated by Spark against a wide range of criteria... helpfulness levels of up to 98.2%' -- a direct intrinsic evaluation of retrieved/generated recommendation quality -> mide_lectura=SI, F RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO. alcance=ORGANIZACION: explicitly a 'shared agentic memory... used collectively by a group of AI agents operating in the same broad task domain' across DIFFERENT users/agents (community-of-practice scope), broader than a single project. multiagente=SI (the paper's core premise: multiple coding agents jointly contribute to and draw from one memory). fidelidad_procedencia=SI: recommendation workflow explicitly includes step 6 'referencing and linking specific sections' of source documentation, and curation tracks 'what worked (and did not work) previously' as evidence for knowledge quality. Fig.1: WITH-SPARK lifts mean code quality (1-5 LLM-judge scale) above NO-SPARK for all 3 models (Qwen3-Coder-30B, Haiku-4.5, GPT5-Codex), with a small open-weights 30B model matching a much larger frontier model's quality when boosted -> metricas=EXITO. F differs from F_screening(WRITE;MULTIAGENTE): added CONSOLIDACION, RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO, FIDELIDAD. handoff=CONTENIDO: recommendations (documentation excerpts, API examples, curated best-practice pointers) are the substantive content redistributed from the collective memory to individual agents. plan_estado=NO.

title: PBFT-Backed Semantic Voting for Multi-Agent Memory Pruning
benchmarks: custom simulated 4-agent MAS environment (500 epochs); voting accuracy evaluated against a custom human-annotated set of 200 memory items; no public benchmark (future work explicitly proposes AgentBench)
fallos_mitigaciones: Central topic: 'ensuring that distributed memories remain synchronized, relevant, and free from the accumulation of outdated or inconsequential data -- a process analogous to biological forgetting' in multi-agent settings, while guarding the collective forgetting DECISION itself against Byzantine (malicious or faulty) agents. Mitigated by three integrated mechanisms: (1) multi-scale temporal decay (short/medium/long-horizon exponential decay combined into a threshold-gated staleness score, triggering forget PROPOSALS, not automatic deletion) to flag stale items; (2) DistilBERT-based context-aware semantic relevance re-scoring (beyond pure time-based heuristics); (3) PBFT consensus tolerating up to f Byzantine agents among N>=3f+1, requiring 2f+1 matching votes across pre-prepare/prepare/commit phases before any memory item is actually deleted -- reported 92% consensus success rate under simulated Byzantine fault injection, with the remaining 8% failing safely (item re-evaluated next epoch) rather than corrupting the memory state.
cita: Duong (2025). PBFT-Backed Semantic Voting for Multi-Agent Memory Pruning.
notes: QUALITY/RECONSIDERAR FLAG (integrity concern beyond ordinary low-rigor): the Results section (Sec.V) contains verbatim editorial/meta-commentary that appears to be unedited LLM-generated analysis leaked into the published text, e.g. 'The user's original draft mentioned a 16% improvement; this 88% accuracy represents a substantial level of correctness. (If the 16% was an improvement *over a baseline*, that baseline would need to be defined and tested against)' and 'Further analysis would involve...ablation studies removing the semantic component...However, the current evaluation provides strong evidence for the protocol's viability.' This strongly suggests the reported numbers/discussion were drafted by an LLM assistant without careful human review before submission -- a serious signal for human reconsideration of inclusion/reliability of the reported statistics, even though the architecture description (Sec.III, Algorithms 1-4) is coherent and internally consistent; extracted per protocol, decision left to human reviewer. Sec.III-A: 'These memories are centrally indexed and stored...but the decision to retain or forget a memory item is a collective one' -> mem_tipos=SEMANTICA(generic shared knowledge base, content type unspecified beyond 'knowledge-based systems'); representacion=HIBRIDA(Pinecone 768-dim vector embeddings + SQLite structured metadata/UUIDs). operaciones=OLVIDO(the protocol's entire purpose: 'Co-Forgetting Protocol' for 'synchronized memory pruning')+ACTUALIZACION('Commit Changes: All deletions are then committed...ensuring memory state is consistently updated'); no WRITE/ADMISION contribution claimed (paper addresses pruning of ALREADY-stored items, not initial admission). trigger=CHECKPOINT('an epoch is triggered every 100 agent interactions', Sec.III-D) + EVENTO-DETERMINISTA(within each epoch, decay score D(t)<delta deterministically triggers a forget PROPOSAL, Algorithm2). retrieval=EMBEDDINGS(Pinecone vector similarity infrastructure + DistilBERT semantic relevance scoring). mide_lectura=NO: no evaluation of retrieval/read quality for downstream task use -- only forgetting-DECISION accuracy (vs human annotation) and cache-hit-rate (an access-latency efficiency metric, not a quality-of-content-read metric). alcance=PROYECTO: shared knowledge base persists for the MAS's whole operational lifetime (500 simulated epochs), not task-bound. multiagente=SI (4-agent weighted PBFT voting, 2 planning-weighted + 2 perception/execution-weighted). fidelidad_procedencia=NO: no source/staleness-of-CONTENT verification described (agent reliability confidence ci weights VOTES, not provenance of memory content itself). Sec.V explicitly states NO ablation was performed ('Further analysis would involve...ablation studies removing the semantic component' -- future work) -> evidencia_tipo=BENCHMARK-E2E(500-epoch simulated run)+MEDICION-COSTO(latency measurement), NOT ABLATION.
