title: Latent Collaboration in Multi-Agent Systems
benchmarks: GSM8K, AIME24, AIME25, GPQA-Diamond, MedQA, ARC-Easy, ARC-Challenge, MBPP-Plus, HumanEval-Plus
fallos_mitigaciones: Sec.3.1 'Input-Output Distribution Alignment': directly inserting freshly generated last-layer hidden states H as input embeddings for the next latent step risks OUT-OF-DISTRIBUTION activations, because these dense high-level representations 'differ from the statistical patterns of learned token embeddings' -- an unmitigated naive design would degrade downstream generation quality. Mitigated (training-free) by a linear alignment operator W_a (computed once via pseudo-inverse of the output embedding matrix, W_a ~= W_out^+ W_in, and reused across all subsequent latent steps) that maps each output hidden vector back into the valid input-embedding space, keeping the alignment cost computationally negligible while preserving distributional consistency between latent and discrete representations.
cita: Zou et al. (2026). Latent Collaboration in Multi-Agent Systems.
notes: Abstract/Sec.1/3.2: 'a shared latent working memory preserves and transfers each agent's internal representations and latent thoughts' -- explicitly named 'working memory' -> mem_tipos=TRABAJO (scoped to a single multi-agent reasoning run over one question, not persisted across tasks/sessions). Sec.2 'KV Cache as Working Memory': memory = layer-wise Key-Value caches (accumulated dense hidden-state vectors), not a retrieval-oriented vector DB -> representacion=VECTOR (continuous vector representations; PARAMETROS rejected since this is runtime ACTIVATION state, not the model's trained weights). Sec.3.1-3.2: each agent auto-regressively APPENDS new last-layer hidden states to its own KV cache (WRITE); cross-agent transfer PREPENDS the predecessor's full layer-wise KV cache into the successor's (ACTUALIZACION/extension of working memory) -- no filtering, forgetting, or admission gate: transfer is explicitly WHOLESALE and 'lossless' (Theorem3.3), not selective -> retrieval=NA (nothing is selectively retrieved; the ENTIRE prior working memory is always transferred in full), mide_lectura=NO (no measurement of selective-read precision; the paper instead formally PROVES full-transfer fidelity, captured under fidelidad_procedencia). trigger=EVENTO-DETERMINISTA: transfer happens at a fixed architectural point (after an agent completes its m latent steps, deterministic pipeline sequencing across Sequential/Hierarchical MAS), not LLM-discretionary. fidelidad_procedencia=SI: 'Communication Fidelity' is one of the paper's three foundational principles, formalized in Theorem3.3 ('Information Preservation via Latent Working Memory') proving outputs are equivalent to directly inputting the preceding agent's full output -- an explicit, proven content-fidelity guarantee. alcance=TAREA: latent working memory transferred within ONE inference run over a single question, not persisted. multiagente=SI (sequential planner/critic/refiner/solver and hierarchical code/math/science+summarizer settings, 5 backbone models). Table1-3: up to 14.6% higher accuracy vs baselines -> metricas EXITO; 70.8%-83.7% output-token reduction -> COSTO-TOKENS; 4x-4.3x faster end-to-end inference (2.6x-7x speedup even vs vLLM-optimized TextMAS) -> LATENCIA. Implementation Details: m in {0,10,20,40,80} latent-steps swept as a hyperparameter -> evidencia_tipo ABLATION (in addition to BENCHMARK-E2E across 9 benchmarks x 5 backbones, and MEDICION-COSTO via extensive token/speed tables). F differs from F_screening(MULTIAGENTE;COSTO): added WRITE, FIDELIDAD. handoff=CONTENIDO: the substantive reasoning content (latent thoughts + input context) travels agent-to-agent, just encoded as continuous vectors rather than text. plan_estado=NO.

title: Adaptive Memory Admission Control for LLM Agents
benchmarks: LoCoMo
fallos_mitigaciones: Central topic: 'agents either accumulate large volumes of conversational content, including hallucinated or obsolete facts, or depend on opaque, fully LLM-driven memory policies that are costly and difficult to audit' -- retention of hallucinated/outdated information 'can propagate errors into future interactions', while overly conservative admission risks discarding information essential for task continuation. Mitigated by A-MAC's five-signal composite admission score: Confidence C(m) 'directly mitigat[es] hallucination propagation' by requiring ROUGE-L-grounded textual support from prior conversation turns before a candidate is admitted (Eq.2); Novelty N(m) prevents redundant storage via embedding dissimilarity; Recency R(m) exponential decay + Type-Prior T(m) jointly bias against transient/low-value content. Sec.4.3 Ablation Study (Table2) quantifies exactly which factor matters most for reliable admission: removing Type Prior causes the LARGEST F1 drop (0.583->0.476, essentially collapsing to the naive Equal-Weights baseline), while removing Confidence/Recency causes only small drops (-0.015/-0.013) -- an explicit, measured ranking of which safeguard against unreliable memory content is most load-bearing.
cita: Zhang et al. (2026). Adaptive Memory Admission Control for LLM Agents.
notes: Sec.1/3.1: candidate memories are 'semantically atomic piece[s] of information' extracted from multi-turn conversation history for 'multi-session reasoning' -> mem_tipos=SEMANTICA(persistent facts/preferences/identity statements, the Type-Prior feature explicitly distinguishes these from transient content) + EPISODICA(candidates extracted per-turn from dialogue, some event-like). representacion=HIBRIDA: atomic text records + Sentence-BERT embeddings used for the Novelty signal (Eq.3). Eq.1/Algorithm1: S(m)=w1*U+w2*C+w3*N+w4*R+w5*T, admit if S(m)>=theta -> operaciones=ADMISION (the paper's entire contribution, 'memory admission as a structured decision problem' rather than an implicit byproduct); WRITE(candidate extraction+storage); CONSOLIDACION+ACTUALIZACION(Algorithm1 lines5-7: on conflict with an existing memory, 'retain the higher-scoring representation and merge' -- explicit merge-on-conflict). trigger=EVENTO-DETERMINISTA: admission is evaluated deterministically for every extracted candidate (Algorithm1), not LLM-discretionary about WHEN to check, not budget-threshold-based. retrieval=NA/mide_lectura=NO: the paper addresses ONLY the write/admission gate, not how memories are later retrieved for downstream QA (no retrieval mechanism is described or evaluated). alcance=PROYECTO: long-term memory persists 'beyond the context window' across multi-session interaction with the same user. multiagente=NO (single-agent memory-admission architecture; F_screening also omits MULTIAGENTE). fidelidad_procedencia=SI: Confidence C(m) is an explicit grounding/hallucination check (ROUGE-L alignment against supporting conversational spans, Eq.2) before content is trusted enough to enter memory. Table1: A-MAC F1=0.583 vs A-mem(SOTA)=0.541(+7.8%), MemoryBank=0.452(+29.0%), MemGPT=0.324(+80%), with highest precision(0.417) among LLM-based methods at near-perfect recall(0.972) -> metricas EXITO; Table1/4: 31% lower latency than A-mem (2644ms vs 3831ms/candidate), latency breakdown showing the single LLM call (Utility) dominates at 97.6% while 4 rule-based features complete in <65ms combined -> metricas LATENCIA. evidencia_tipo=ABLATION(Table2 explicit per-feature ablation + Table3 threshold sensitivity)+BENCHMARK-E2E(Table1 vs 4 baselines on LoCoMo test N=225)+MEDICION-COSTO(Table4 latency breakdown). F differs from F_screening(WRITE;COSTO): added FIDELIDAD, CONSOLIDACION (no dedicated ADMISION facet exists in the closed F vocabulary). handoff=NO: single-agent, single-user persistent memory across that user's own sessions -- no cross-agent or cross-user content transfer is described. plan_estado=NO: admitted content is user facts/preferences/identity statements, not task-plan/progress state.

title: Enhancing Software Engineering Through Closed-Loop Memory Optimization
benchmarks: SWE-bench-Verified
fallos_mitigaciones: Untrained (NFT) memory model Mtheta generates redundant/harmful memory that DEGRADES SE performance (Tab.1-2, e.g. Devstral+DeepSeek-1.5B SR down3.50pp/down6.00pp cross-episode); mitigated via trajectory-based rejection sampling (Alg.1, Eq.1 S3.2) that filters candidate memories failing the acceptance criterion (for-all-i delta_i>=0 AND exists-i delta_i>0) before SFT/RL training of the memory model.
cita: Guo et al. (2026). Enhancing Software Engineering Through Closed-Loop Memory Optimization.
notes: S2.1/A.2: memory Mk stored in a single markdown file Memory.md, integrating 'lessons learned, codebase structures identified, reasoning patterns discovered, and task-relevant contextual information' -> mem_tipos=SEMANTICA;PROCEDIMENTAL, representacion=DOCS-ARCHIVOS (A.2 preliminary study: 9 candidate structures tested -- String/Dict/List/Tree/Graph/Python/Given/Discretionary/Ours -- Ours=markdown wins Table3, dAbs>=17.65% LA(-1), Table3). S2.3/S2.1 cross-episode Mk=Mtheta(R,S(Mk-1,tau_k)) combines prior memory+new trajectory each task completion -> operaciones=WRITE;CONSOLIDACION;ACTUALIZACION, trigger=EVENTO-DETERMINISTA (after task Tk completes). retrieval=NA: whole Memory.md is injected wholesale into agent context, no ranking/embedding/graph search component described. mide_lectura=SI: the entire MemOp framework defines memory utility as causal downstream impact -- S2.2 Eq.1 measures Delta_i(Mj) vs no-memory baseline across NQ=10 metrics (SR/LA/Eresolve/LE), i.e. it directly measures the utility of READING/using generated memory during task-solving -> RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO in F. alcance=PROYECTO: Alg.1 samples NT tasks per repository R and cross-episode memory accumulates 'repository-level shared knowledge base' within the same repo (S3.4/S4.2). Table6/Fig.22 (F.3 Computation Overhead): API cost per-100-instances ($11.73-$86.18 construction), Delta_rel>=9.79% total computational cost reduction (abstract, S4.2) -> metricas=COSTO-TOKENS, evidencia_tipo=MEDICION-COSTO. A.2 Table3 ablates 9 memory-structure variants vs no-memory baseline + Fig.4 ablates SFT-only vs SFT+RL training stages -> evidencia_tipo=ABLATION. Tables1-2 SWE-bench-Verified single/cross-episode results (up-to-5.25% SR, 4.63% Eresolve gains) -> BENCHMARK-E2E. F_screening was WRITE;COSTO (abstract-only); confirmed against full text adds CONSOLIDACION (cross-episode memory evolution S2.3), RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO (utility-of-reading is the paper's core contribution), PROCEDIMENTAL (memory encodes reasoning/debugging patterns, not just facts), and NEGATIVO(b) (NFT-Mtheta/naive memory consistently HURTS SE performance, Tab.1-2, motivating the trained/validated memory design).

title: EET: Experience-Driven Early Termination for Cost-Efficient Software Engineering Agents
benchmarks: SWE-bench Verified; SWE-bench Lite (experience generation)
fallos_mitigaciones: Context pollution: raw/irrelevant retrieved experiences 'waste tokens and distract the agent' (S3.1); mitigated via TF-IDF similarity threshold tau_sim + top-1-only retrieval + structured abstraction (task_description/execution_summary/confidence fields, only SUCCESSFUL trajectories retained) instead of raw traces. Table3 (RQ2): Naive-EET (raw trajectory context, no abstraction) only reaches -26.0% cost / -3.1% resolved vs EET's -31.8% cost / +2.7% resolved, confirming structured abstraction beats raw memory injection.
cita: Guo et al. (2026). EET: Experience-Driven Early Termination for Cost-Efficient Software Engineering Agents.
notes: S3.1: each resolved issue is distilled into a structured experience object (task_description/execution_summary/evaluation_result=pass-only/confidence/confidence_reason) -> mem_tipos=EPISODICA(per-issue trajectory)+PROCEDIMENTAL(actionable debugging/stopping signals), representacion=DOCS-ARCHIVOS. operaciones=WRITE;ADMISION: 'we retain only high-quality experience... evaluation_result field is set to pass for all stored experiences' (S3.1) = explicit success-only admission filter. trigger=EVENTO-DETERMINISTA (experience generated after each historical issue resolution completes). retrieval=RANKING: TF-IDF text-similarity of task_description against experience base, threshold tau_sim, top-1 only (S3.1). mide_lectura=SI: S5.3 RQ3 ablation w/o-experience-injection drops resolution rate by 10.4pp despite cutting cost a further 30.7% (Table4) -- direct causal measurement of the utility of READING retrieved experience -> RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO in F. alcance=ORGANIZACION: experience base built from SWE-bench-Lite (207 tasks, many repos) is applied cross-repository to SWE-bench-Verified issues (500 tasks, different repos); explicit zero-repository-overlap transfer check (Trae Agent, 50 issues) still cuts cost $12.7->$9.6 at matched 14.0% SR (S5.1/App.F), i.e. experience generalizes beyond a single project. Table1: EET cuts total cost 19.3%-55.1% (avg 31.8%) across 6 agent x backend configs with resolution-rate loss <=0.2% (some configs +7.8%/+7.2%); Table2 early-termination rate avg 11.3% of issues. F_screening was COSTO only; full text confirms/adds WRITE, RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO (RQ3 ablation), PROCEDIMENTAL (experience captures reusable debugging patterns per S5.1 cross-repo transfer discussion).

title: Cost and Accuracy of Long-Term Memory in Distributed Multi-Agent Systems Based on Large Language Models
benchmarks: LoCoMo
fallos_mitigaciones: Graph-based LTM (Graphiti, cognee) accuracy gap vs vector/full-context is 'driven by retrieval incompleteness rather than reasoning failure' (Table III: cognee/Graphiti 25.58-28.18% 'unknown' responses vs 8.38-11.14% for mem0/RAG/full-context) -- a structural retrieval-coverage weakness the paper measures but does not itself mitigate (pure evaluation study).
cita: Wolff and Bennati (2026). Cost and Accuracy of Long-Term Memory in Distributed Multi-Agent Systems Based on Large Language Models.
notes: Pure independent testbed/benchmark paper (no own memory mechanism) -> mem_tipos/representacion/operaciones/trigger/retrieval=NA per rule5; it MEASURES accuracy (LLM-as-judge, majority-of-3) + system-level cost (CPU/RAM/disk/network/TCO) of three 3rd-party LTM frameworks -- mem0 (vector), Graphiti (graph), cognee (hybrid) -- plus RAG and full-context baselines, on all ten LoCoMo conversations (1,540 QA pairs) under unconstrained vs constrained (150ms latency/512KB-s bandwidth/30ms jitter) simulated cloud-edge network (SIII Method/Operation). Table III: mem0 highest at 81.08% accurate, RAG 78.31%, full-context 77.16%, Graphiti 56.03%, cognee 55.27%. mide_lectura=SI (accuracy IS the primary read-quality metric) -> RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO in F. Table IV per-category breakdown includes a Temporal question category (mem0 55.48% highest, Graphiti 31.83% lowest) = a staleness/knowledge-update-adjacent axis explicitly reported -> fidelidad_procedencia=SI, FIDELIDAD in F. alcance=SESION: LoCoMo's up-to-32-session multi-session dialogues are the unit of study; 'Memory backends are logically wiped between conversations' (Threats-to-Validity/Internal) confirming per-conversation/session scope, not cross-project accumulation. multiagente=NO despite 'Distributed Multi-Agent Systems' framing in the title/abstract: the DMAS label refers to the distributed EDGE/CLOUD deployment topology of pipeline components (coordinator/responder/memory service, toxiproxy) simulating network constraints, NOT memory shared across multiple distinct AI agents with separate goals -- matches F_screening's absence of a MULTIAGENTE tag. TCO/Pareto: 'RAG matches the upper cluster at 8.4 times lower total cost of ownership than mem0, and both are the only non-dominated backends on the Pareto frontier' (abstract/Fig.2) -> COSTO in F, MEDICION-COSTO. NEGATIVO(b): 'full-context forwarding underperforms mem0 despite supplying the entire conversation for each question' (abstract) = negative evidence that naive maximal-context 'memory' does not guarantee better accuracy than a compressed/precise memory design. F_screening was COSTO;RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO; full text confirms and adds FIDELIDAD + NEGATIVO.

title: MemRec: Collaborative Memory-Augmented Agentic Recommender System
benchmarks: Amazon Books, Amazon Goodreads, MovieTV, Yelp (InstructRec splits)
fallos_mitigaciones: Cognitive Overload: naively injecting raw neighbor memories 'bombards the LLM with noise, resulting in hallucinations and diminished instruction adherence' (S2.1.1); mitigated via Information-Bottleneck-inspired 'Curate-then-Synthesize' (LLM-generated domain curation rules R_domain prune neighbors Eq.1-2, then LM_Mem synthesizes distilled confidence-scored facets Eq.3). Prohibitive Collaborative Updates: naive synchronous propagation scales O(|N'k|) LLM calls with redundant repeated user-context tokens per neighbor; mitigated via Asynchronous Collaborative Propagation batching self-reflection+neighbor updates into one call, achieving O(1) call complexity (S2.1.3, Eq.5-6).
cita: Chen et al. (2026). MemRec: Collaborative Memory-Augmented Agentic Recommender System.
notes: S2.1: unified collaborative memory graph G=(V,E), V=UsersuItems, each node stores an evolving semantic memory Mv -> mem_tipos=SEMANTICA, representacion=GRAFO. S2.1.1 Collaborative Memory Retrieval: zero-shot LLM-as-Rule-Generator curates top-k' neighbors via domain-adaptive multiplier rules (Eq.1-2, Fig.3) then LM_Mem synthesizes them into structured preference facets Mcollab with a confidence score + explicit 'Supporting Neighbors' evidence list per facet (Eq.3, Fig.4-5) -> retrieval=GRAFO;RANKING, and the confidence+cited-neighbor-evidence design is a genuine provenance/grounding mechanism -> fidelidad_procedencia=SI, FIDELIDAD in F ('Grounding the reasoning in Mcollab ensures that the generated rationale is factually supported by broader community evidence', S2.1.2). S2.1.3 Async Collaborative Propagation triggered per new user-item interaction event (Eq.5-6) -> trigger=EVENTO-DETERMINISTA, operaciones=WRITE;CONSOLIDACION;ACTUALIZACION. mide_lectura=SI: S3.3 RQ2 explicitly ablates architectural decoupling vs a Naive Collaborative Agent (uncurated raw context, single-stage) -- Naive plateaus from information bottleneck while MemRec gains +34% relative H@1 on Books (Fig.6) -- directly measures the utility of curated READING -> RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO in F, evidencia_tipo=ABLATION. Tables 2-3: MemRec beats all baselines (LightGCN/SASRec/P5/Vanilla-LLM/iAgent/RecBot/AgentCF/i2Agent) on all 4 datasets, p<0.05, e.g. Goodreads H@1 +28.98% -> BENCHMARK-E2E. S3.4 RQ3 online-inference cost/latency Pareto analysis across deployment configs -> COSTO in F, MEDICION-COSTO. alcance=ORGANIZACION: Table1 shows one shared graph spans 3K-12K users x 30K-121K items per dataset (whole-community scope, not per-project/session). multiagente=NO: 'collaborative' here means collaborative-filtering signal sharing ACROSS USERS/ITEMS on one graph, not multiple distinct AI agents sharing memory (single LM_Mem + single LLM_Rec pipeline) -- matches F_screening's absence of a MULTIAGENTE tag. F_screening was WRITE;COSTO; full text confirms and adds CONSOLIDACION, RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO, FIDELIDAD.

title: Aeon: High-Performance Neuro-Symbolic Memory Management for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
benchmarks: HNSW (FAISS) comparison on synthetic 'Dense Forest' dataset (own, D=768, N in 10^4-10^6)
fallos_mitigaciones: 'Vector Haze': Flat-RAG/bag-of-embeddings architectures retrieve 'semantically similar but episodically disjointed facts that confuse rather than aid the agent' (S1/S2.1); mitigated via the Atlas hierarchical spatial index constraining search to the agent's active context region plus the Trace episodic DAG providing temporal/causal structure (S3.6).
cita: Arslan (2026). Aeon: High-Performance Neuro-Symbolic Memory Management for Long-Horizon LLM Agents.
notes: Pure systems/engineering paper with ZERO downstream task-accuracy evaluation (no SWE-bench/LoCoMo/QA benchmark; only micro/macro latency-throughput-compression benchmarks on a synthetic 'Dense Forest' D=768 dataset + an HNSW/FAISS comparison, S5-6) -> mide_lectura=NO (measures retrieval SPEED, never retrieval CORRECTNESS/utility), so RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO is correctly excluded from F. S3.2 Atlas = SIMD-accelerated INT8-quantized spatial vector index (semantic concepts) + S3.6 Trace = neuro-symbolic episodic DAG (TraceEvent nodes Vuser/Vsystem/Vconcept, temporal Enext + reference Eref edges into Atlas) -> mem_tipos=EPISODICA;SEMANTICA, representacion=HIBRIDA (vector+graph). operaciones=WRITE;OLVIDO: S3.3 WAL insert path + S3.4 Sidecar Blob Arena (append-only, generational GC discarding tombstoned/dead blobs) + S6.9 Trace GC (compaction, tombstone scan). This is STORAGE-level garbage collection/eviction (OLVIDO), NOT content-level summarization/merging of memory (no CONSOLIDACION mechanism found anywhere in the text: grep for consolidat/summar/dedup/merge in the full PDF returns nothing beyond GC/tombstone terminology) -- corrects F_screening's CONSOLIDACION tag, which appears to have been an abstract-only misread of 'generational garbage collection'. trigger=NA: the paper never specifies a concrete policy for WHEN a new semantic concept gets allocated/written (abstracted away to the Python 'Shell' managing 'LLM interaction, prompt engineering', S3.1) nor when compaction runs (GC-ratio=0.5 appears only as an evaluation-harness setting, S6.9), so this axis is genuinely undefined. S4.2.1 Multi-Tenant Isolation: SLB sharded 64-way by hash(session_id), 'Session A will never evict or access cache entries from Session B', scaling to >100,000 concurrent sessions on one node -> alcance=SESION, multiagente=NO (explicit ISOLATION, i.e. the opposite of sharing, matches F_screening's absent MULTIAGENTE tag), and this cross-tenant leakage prevention is itself a memory-security design choice -> SEGURIDAD in F. Table2/Fig.1: INT8 SDOT 4.70ns vs FP32 26.5ns (5.6x), 3.1x on-disk compression, WAL overhead <1% (Table4, within measurement noise), P99 EBR read latency 750ns under 16-thread contention -> COSTO in F, evidencia_tipo=MEDICION-COSTO;ABLATION (WAL on/off Table4, FP32-vs-INT8 Table2-3, flat-vs-Atlas Fig.4, beam=1/3/3+CSLS Table5).

title: Learning Query-Aware Budget-Tier Routing for Runtime Agent Memory
benchmarks: LoCoMo, LongMemEval, HotpotQA
fallos_mitigaciones: Offline query-agnostic memory construction ('build once, use always') is 'wasteful' (spends computation regardless of query need) and 'brittle' (irreversible preprocessing may discard query-critical information, S1); mitigated via runtime on-demand extraction that keeps raw history intact (never offline-processed) and defers processing until query time, combined with an explicit RL-trained cost-aware budget-tier router (Eq.7-10) that trades task performance against extraction cost per module.
cita: Zhang et al. (2026). Learning Query-Aware Budget-Tier Routing for Runtime Agent Memory.
notes: S3-4: BudgetMem performs RUNTIME on-demand memory extraction m=f_mem(q,Cq) over a STATIC raw chunk store C that is never offline-processed (S3 'Inputs': 'This step only segments raw text for indexing and does not perform any offline extraction, summarization, or rewriting') -> mem_tipos=SEMANTICA(entity/temporal/topic facts+summary, Eq.4-6);TRABAJO(memory m is rebuilt fresh per query, not persisted for reuse), representacion=DOCS-ARCHIVOS(text chunks/structured fields/NL notes). operaciones=NA: no WRITE/ADMISION/CONSOLIDACION/OLVIDO/ACTUALIZACION of a persistent memory store is defined -- the mechanism is query-triggered on-demand EXTRACTION+ROUTING over an immutable chunk store, which the RQ2 operaciones vocabulary does not cover. retrieval=EMBEDDINGS: Contriever dense retriever selects Cq subset from C (S5.2). trigger=EVENTO-DETERMINISTA(extraction triggered per incoming query, S3)+PRESUPUESTO(the paper's central contribution IS an explicit, RL-learned, cost-aware BUDGET-TIER router selecting LOW/MID/HIGH per module via reward r=r_task+lambda*alpha*r_cost, Eq.7-10, S4.3). mide_lectura=SI: Table1 measures F1/Judge task performance directly as a function of the extraction/reading budget across LoCoMo/LongMemEval/HotpotQA against 7 strong baselines (ReadAgent/MemoryBank/A-MEM/LangMem/Mem0/MemoryOS/LightMem), e.g. BudgetMem-CAP avg F1 59.99/Judge 61.06 (LLaMA) vs best baseline LightMem 35.45/49.21 at comparable cost -> RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO in F, evidencia_tipo=BENCHMARK-E2E. Fig.2 sweeps performance-cost frontiers across 3 orthogonal tiering strategies (implementation/reasoning/capacity) on LoCoMo -> evidencia_tipo=ABLATION;MEDICION-COSTO (cost measured as $ from token usage x service pricing, S5.1). alcance=SESION: primary benchmarks (LoCoMo/LongMemEval) are multi-session dialogue histories; HotpotQA is included as a long-context QA transfer task, not a persistent-scope axis. F_screening was COSTO;RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO; full text confirms both facets with no additions needed.

title: HyMem: Hybrid Memory Architecture with Dynamic Retrieval Scheduling
benchmarks: LOCOMO, LongMemEval(-s)
fallos_mitigaciones: 'Forgetting' phenomena from over-compression: quantified failure breakdown shows ~15% of LOCOMO failures are retrieval errors and ~5% are information loss from compression (S3.1); mitigated via dual-granularity storage (Level-1 summary + Level-2 raw text) with dynamic escalation to raw Level-2 text only when the lightweight module detects 'contextual incompleteness' (a 'forgetting' state), plus a reflection module that iteratively refines/decomposes queries when answers are incomplete (S3.2-3.4).
cita: Wang et al. (2026). HyMem: Hybrid Memory Architecture with Dynamic Retrieval Scheduling.
notes: S3.1: dual-granularity storage -- Level-1 event summaries (vectorized E(si)=ei) + Level-2 raw dialogue text (pi), with explicit many-to-one links from Level-1 to Level-2 'to support memory backtracking during the recall stage' -> mem_tipos=EPISODICA(event units)+SEMANTICA(distilled summaries: context/time/location/participants), representacion=HIBRIDA, operaciones=WRITE;CONSOLIDACION, and the explicit backtracking link IS a provenance/verification path from compressed to raw source -> fidelidad_procedencia=SI, FIDELIDAD in F. S3.2-3.3: lightweight module does cosine-similarity top-k retrieval over Level-1; escalates to deep module (coarse recall top-N + LLM self-retrieval + backtrack to Level-2) only when contextual incompleteness detected -> retrieval=EMBEDDINGS;RANKING, trigger=EVENTO-DETERMINISTA (storage-time event-boundary partition trigger). S4.1 Table1: HyMem SOTA on LOCOMO overall (89.55%) and LongMemEval-s (78.80%) vs A-Mem/Mem0/Zep/LightMem/Nemori/Mirix/MemU/Naive-RAG/Full-Context -> BENCHMARK-E2E. S4.2 Table2: HyMem 97.4s/1.2k-tokens vs e.g. Mem0 583.4s/1.0k-tokens (-83.3% latency vs Mem0, -74.9% vs SimpleMem) -> COSTO/LATENCIA in metricas, MEDICION-COSTO. S4.4 Table3 full ablation of Level1/Level2 x Light/Deep/Reflection modules: removing Level-2+deep module -17.40% accuracy; removing lightweight module forces all-deep processing (token cost 850->3192, though ~70% of queries need only lightweight in practice) -> ABLATION, mide_lectura=SI/RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO. S4.5 Fig.6: LLMLingua-2 compression-ratio sweep shows accuracy degrades as compression increases; event-level compression (~30% of original length) beats LLMLingua-2 at matched ratios, confirming aggressive/naive compression hurts -> NEGATIVO(b). F_screening was COSTO;RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO; full text confirms and adds WRITE, CONSOLIDACION, FIDELIDAD, NEGATIVO.

title: Shodh-Memory: A Neuroscience-Grounded Cognitive Memory Architecture for Artificial Intelligence Agents
benchmarks: NINGUNO (no standardized external benchmark evaluated; explicit scope limitation -- LOCOMO deferred to future work, S5.1/S6.3); internal Criterion.rs micro/macro-benchmarks + synthetic scenarios only (cross-domain association chains, temporal event chains, entity co-occurrence)
fallos_mitigaciones: The paper frames prior systems' 'Uniform treatment' (S1: 'All memories receive equal importance regardless of type, age, or access patterns') as a design failure and treats false-positive retrieval of misleading memories as costlier than false negatives (S3.3.1); mitigated via asymmetric importance plasticity (additive boost eta_I=0.025 on positive feedback vs multiplicative decay delta_I=0.10 on negative feedback, Eq.2, with a recovery floor Imin=0.05) plus the piecewise decay model (aggressive early exponential clears noise within tc=3 days before transitioning to a heavy-tailed power-law, Eq.1).
cita: Sharma (2026). Shodh-Memory: A Cognitive Memory System for Edge-Native AI Agents.
notes: NOTE: the PDF's own title ('...A Cognitive Memory System for Edge-Native AI Agents') differs from the corpus input.jsonl title ('...A Neuroscience-Grounded Cognitive Memory Architecture for Artificial Intelligence Agents') -- same key/author/content, apparently a later preprint revision; on-topic, not flagged RECONSIDERAR. S3.1: three-tier Cowan-model hierarchy (T1 Working, capacity=100 items; T2 Session, RocksDB+Vamana/SPANN; T3 Long-Term, unlimited semantic-fact store) with biologically-motivated promotion thresholds (working->session: importance>=0.35 & age>=30min; session->long-term: importance>=0.5 & age>=24h) -> mem_tipos=TRABAJO;EPISODICA;SEMANTICA, operaciones includes ADMISION (the promotion gate). S3.2 piecewise exponential-to-power-law decay (Eq.1, tc=3days) + Imin=0.05 floor -> OLVIDO. S3.3 dual plasticity: importance plasticity (Eq.2, asymmetric feedback-driven update) + Hebbian synaptic plasticity (Eq.3, tier-dependent learning rates) + multi-scale LTP (Burst/Weekly/Full) -> ACTUALIZACION. S3.5 Semantic Consolidation: episodic memories aged>=7days clustered by Jaccard similarity (>=2 supporting memories) converted to semantic facts via a multi-extractor pipeline, runs 'during idle periods' -> CONSOLIDACION, trigger=CHECKPOINT (idle-period consolidation)+EVENTO-DETERMINISTA (Hebbian update on co-activation). 'Compressed semantic memories retain LZ4-compressed provenance links to source episodic memories' (S3.5) -> fidelidad_procedencia=SI, FIDELIDAD in F. S3.4 retrieval fuses BM25(Tantivy)+vector(MiniLM-L6-v2)+graph spreading-activation (ACT-R-inspired, Eq.6) with density-dependent fusion weights (Eq.7) -> retrieval=RANKING;EMBEDDINGS;GRAFO, representacion=HIBRIDA. S5.1 explicit scope statement: 'comprehensive retrieval accuracy evaluation on standardized benchmarks such as LOCOMO... remains important future work'; only internal Criterion.rs latency/throughput microbenchmarks (Tables3-5, sub-20ms end-to-end) + synthetic-scenario Precision@k/Recall@k/MRR comparisons of graph-augmented vs vector-only retrieval (20-40% Recall@5 / 30% MRR gains, explicitly caveated as 'controlled scenarios, not standardized datasets') -> mide_lectura=SI (retrieval-quality metrics ARE reported, just not on a named benchmark) -> RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO in F; evidencia_tipo=ABLATION (graph-vs-vector-only isolation)+MEDICION-COSTO (extensive latency/throughput/scaling tables). S4.2.1 Multi-Tenant Isolation (SLB sharded per session_id) -> alcance=SESION ('Session Memory' is the paper's own T2 tier name); multiagente=NO (isolation design, not sharing, matches F_screening's absent MULTIAGENTE tag). F_screening was CONSOLIDACION;COSTO; full text confirms and adds WRITE, RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO, FIDELIDAD.

title: Routing Memory: Lightweight Long-Term Memory for Agentic LLMs via Vector-Quantized Routing
benchmarks: MS-MARCO, LoCoMo, ReAct agent (synthetic), Wikipedia single-pool (own)
fallos_mitigaciones: Multi-hop queries requiring evidence from semantically distant regions of memory are a genuine limitation of bucket-based routing: LoCoMo multi-hop category shows a -17% deficit vs dense retrieval (Table5, S'Discussion'); mitigated via a confidence-gated Hybrid RM-Dense Fallback (Eq.7, S3.6) that recovers 67% of the RM-dense gap at gamma=0.65 with only 13.6% of queries falling back to dense retrieval (Table6).
cita: Sertel (2026). Routing Memory: Lightweight Long-Term Memory for Agentic LLMs via Vector-Quantized Routing.
notes: S3.2-3.3: VQ codebook (K-means, K=256) assigns 1-2 byte routing codes per item -> 768x compression vs fp16 dense embeddings (Table1); multi-bucket probe (top-n centroids, Eq.2) + intra-bucket cosine reranking (Eq.3) -> representacion=VECTOR (still fundamentally embeddings, just quantized), retrieval=EMBEDDINGS;RANKING. mem_tipos=NA: RM is a content-agnostic routing/indexing LAYER demonstrated interchangeably over MS-MARCO passages, LoCoMo conversation turns, ReAct agent traces, and Wikipedia paragraphs (S4 Datasets) -- it does not define what TYPE of content is memorized, only HOW it is indexed/retrieved. operaciones=WRITE only (initial batch codebook training + item encoding); trigger=NA and no ADMISION/CONSOLIDACION/OLVIDO/ACTUALIZACION: the codebook 'is static after training; online updates for streaming data are not currently supported' (S7 Limitations) -- no runtime write-triggering or memory-mutation policy is described, only offline/batch index construction. mide_lectura=SI: Recall@k/MRR/cluster-purity are the paper's primary and near-exclusive evaluation currency across Tables2-15 -> RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO in F. S5.4/Table4-5 LoCoMo: session-aware embedding enrichment (Eq.5, prepends session/date/speaker metadata to each turn before encoding; 'queries are not enriched') surpasses Dense Recall@5 by +16.4% (0.272 vs 0.234), +81% on Temporal category, but -17% on Multi-hop -> alcance=SESION (LoCoMo's session-structured conversational memory is the flagship agent-memory demonstration), fallos_mitigaciones/NEGATIVO(b) anchor. S5.7/Table8-10 score-based passage filtering cuts LLM context tokens 37-42% same-domain / 75-78% cross-domain (Table14, million-scale); Table10 projects $318-$31,800/month savings at 1M queries across 4 commercial APIs -> COSTO in F, metricas=COSTO-TOKENS, evidencia_tipo=MEDICION-COSTO. S6 Table15 codebook-K ablation + S5.3 cluster-purity-vs-recall decomposition + S5.8.1 K-selection heuristic comparison -> evidencia_tipo=ABLATION. S5.10 million-scale (1M items): RM maintains ~100% recall ratio to dense at 732x compression and 2x latency advantage -> BENCHMARK-E2E. F_screening was RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO;COSTO; full text confirms and adds WRITE (index construction) and NEGATIVO (multi-hop deficit, Table5).

title: AMV-L: Lifecycle-Managed Agent Memory for Tail-Latency Control in Long-Running LLM Systems
benchmarks: NINGUNO (own long-running production-style serving workload; evaluated against TTL and LRU baselines under identical workloads; no standardized external benchmark used)
fallos_mitigaciones: TTL bounds item AGE but not COMPUTATIONAL FOOTPRINT: retrieval candidate-set and vector-scan work grow unbounded as retained items accumulate, producing heavy-tailed latency (13.8% of requests exceed 2s, S2). LRU is 'value-agnostic... can evict long-lived but high-utility information under phase shifts' (S1/S4). Both are mitigated by AMV-L's value-driven tiered eligibility (hot/warm/cold, Eq. unified value-update rule Sec.5) that decouples total retained memory from the request-path retrieval-eligible set (S4.5 system invariant), cutting the >2s-request fraction to 0.007% relative to TTL.
cita: Bamidele (2026). AMV-L: Lifecycle-Managed Agent Memory for Tail-Latency Control in Long-Running LLM Systems.
notes: S4-6: three-tier lifecycle (hot/warm/cold) with a continuously-updated scalar utility value V(m) (unified update rule S5.2: V(m) <- min{V(m)*e^(-lambda*Dt) + alpha*I_access + beta*I_contrib, Vmax}), value-driven promotion/demotion/eviction (theta_E eviction threshold applies only in cold tier) with hysteresis to prevent oscillation -> operaciones=WRITE(insertion)+ADMISION(tier-eligibility gate for the hot/warm retrieval-candidate set)+OLVIDO(cold-tier eviction)+ACTUALIZACION(continuous per-item value update, S5). trigger=EVENTO-DETERMINISTA(value updated 'lazily when an item is touched by a request')+CHECKPOINT(tier migration/eviction performed asynchronously 'off the critical path' as background maintenance, S4.3). representacion=VECTOR (each item carries content/metadata/embedding/scalar-value; shared vector index with candidate-ID tier scoping, S8). retrieval=EMBEDDINGS;RANKING (cosine similarity top-n over the tier-bounded candidate set R=T_H u Sample_k(T_W), S7). mem_tipos=TRABAJO (the hot tier literally IS the bounded 'request-path working set', the paper's central framing) + SEMANTICA (user facts/preferences, domain facts) + EPISODICA (summaries of prior interactions) -- S2: 'Memory records include user facts and preferences, summaries of prior interactions, intermediate task artifacts, retrieved documents, and system-generated observations'. plan_estado=SI: 'intermediate task artifacts'/'intermediate task state' are EXPLICITLY named memory content types (S1: 'autonomous services maintain intermediate task state over extended executions'; S2). fidelidad_procedencia=SI: S8 request path 'records which memory was used in the answer for attribution and feedback, and returns the answer with citations' -> explicit provenance/attribution mechanism -> FIDELIDAD in F. mide_lectura=SI: retrieval QUALITY is explicitly preserved and measured across policies -- 'matching retrieval quality (value means within ~0-2%)' vs LRU (abstract) -> RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO in F. alcance=PROYECTO: framing is long-running per-deployment/per-agent persistent memory beyond any single session ('coding agents retain project context... over extended executions', S1), not scoped to one conversational session. Abstract headline: vs TTL, AMV-L improves throughput 3.1x, reduces latency 4.2x(median)/4.7x(p95)/4.4x(p99), cuts >2s-request fraction 13.8%->0.007%; vs LRU trades +26%/+3% median/p95 for -15% p99/-98% >2s and ~6% fewer tokens/request at matched retrieval quality -> COSTO+LATENCIA in metricas, MEDICION-COSTO, BENCHMARK-E2E (full-stack production-style serving system evaluated under identical long-running workloads vs 2 baselines). No internal ablation of AMV-L's own components found (grep for ablat/hysteresis-disabled sensitivity study returns nothing) -> evidencia_tipo excludes ABLATION. NEGATIVO(b): TTL's and LRU's failure modes under long-running accumulation are direct negative findings about common (naive) memory-retention strategies. F_screening was CONSOLIDACION;COSTO; full text finds NO content-consolidation mechanism (pure numeric lifecycle/tiering, not memory-content merging) so CONSOLIDACION is DROPPED and replaced with WRITE, RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO, FIDELIDAD, NEGATIVO.

title: Structured Distillation for Personalized Agent Memory: 11x Token Reduction with Retrieval Preservation
benchmarks: NINGUNO (no external community benchmark; own single-user corpus of 4,182 Claude-Code conversations / 14,340 exchanges across 6 SE projects + 201 curated recall queries evaluated across 107 search configurations)
fallos_mitigaciones: Prevailing LLM-compaction-under-context-pressure is 'lossy summarization... no schema, no extraction targets, no contract about what survives... summaries of summaries degrade iteratively, information from early exchanges is progressively destroyed' (S1); mitigated by structured distillation with a mandatory verbatim back-reference (ground truth is never discarded, only indexed) plus the 'surviving vocabulary principle' (LLM told to reuse exact participant terminology rather than paraphrase freely) -- only 27.0% of top-15-IDF verbatim tokens survive into distilled text, yet 96.8% of QUERY vocabulary is retained (S3.2), explaining why retrieval quality survives aggressive compression.
cita: Lewis (2026). Structured Distillation for Personalized Agent Memory: 11x Token Reduction with Retrieval Preservation.
notes: S3.2 Table1: each exchange -> compound 'palace object' (exchange_core+specific_context LLM-generated / room_assignments LLM-generated thematic tags / files_touched regex-extracted), each carrying a back-reference (conversation_id/ply_start/ply_end) to its verbatim source -> mem_tipos=EPISODICA (per-exchange conversation memory), representacion=HIBRIDA (structured text objects + separate FAISS vector index [MiniLM-L6-v2, 384-dim] + BM25 lexical index, S3.3), fidelidad_procedencia=SI (explicit back-reference/drill-down provenance + two-tier index-vs-display separation, 'the user always reads the unmodified original', S3.2/contribution4) -> FIDELIDAD in F. operaciones=WRITE(distillation)+ADMISION(<100-char exchanges filtered as trivial, S3.1). trigger=EVENTO-DETERMINISTA (ply/exchange-boundary completion defines the segmentation unit, S3.1). Table2: 4,182 conversations/14,340 exchanges -> 12,427 distilled objects, 371->38 avg tokens = 11x corpus-level compression (9.9x per-item). retrieval=EMBEDDINGS(HNSW/Exact vector)+RANKING(BM25-Okapi/BM25-FTS lexical scoring + RRF/Weighted/Additive/CombMNZ fusion, S3.4). mide_lectura=SI: the paper's ENTIRE evaluation (107 configs, 201 queries, 214,519 consensus-graded pairs, 5 local LLM graders + calibrated Opus 6th-grader, S4.3-4.4) is a direct measurement of retrieval-quality preservation under compression -> RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO in F. S5.1-5.2 Table3: best pure-distilled config reaches 96% of best-verbatim MRR (0.717 vs 0.745); best cross-layer (BM25-verbatim + HNSW-distilled fusion) slightly EXCEEDS best-verbatim (MRR 0.759, 102%) -> BENCHMARK-E2E. Mechanism-dependent result: vector search (HNSW/Exact) shows NO significant degradation on distilled text (10/10 non-significant post-Bonferroni, |d|<=0.25) while ALL 20 BM25 configs degrade SIGNIFICANTLY (|d|=0.031-0.756, Table10) -> evidencia_tipo=ABLATION (107-config x 4-mechanism systematic comparison with significance tests), and this mechanism-dependent BM25 failure is a genuine NEGATIVO(b) finding (a naive lexical-search-over-compressed-memory combination measurably hurts recall, even though vector-search-over-compressed-memory does not). alcance=PROYECTO: single-user corpus spans 6 distinct software-engineering projects (Table2), explicitly framed as 'the intended deployment setting: persistent memory over one developer's long-running agent history' (S4.1), broader than one project yet still single-user (not multi-user/ORGANIZACION). Token-budget result (contribution3): 1,000 exchanges fit in ~39,000 tokens vs ~407,000 verbatim -> COSTO in F, metricas=COSTO-TOKENS, evidencia_tipo=MEDICION-COSTO. handoff=PUNTEROS;CONTENIDO: the distilled object is literally a pointer/index (conversation_id+ply-range) that resolves to full verbatim CONTENT when a later session recalls it -- the paper's central architectural claim (contribution4: 'two-tier architecture... separates index from display'). F_screening was COSTO;RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO; full text confirms and adds WRITE, FIDELIDAD, NEGATIVO.

title: Did You Check the Right Pocket? Cost-Sensitive Store Routing for Memory-Augmented Agents
benchmarks: LoCoMo & LongMemEval query taxonomies (used to derive synthetic store-routing labels, not run directly); own 150-question QA evaluation (GPT-3.5-turbo, GPT-4o-mini) + 1,000-query synthetic routing benchmark
fallos_mitigaciones: S5.3 'Why Does Uniform Underperform?' identifies two failure modes of retrieving from all stores: (1) needle-in-a-haystack signal dilution at ~787 tokens, and (2) 'Conflicting information' -- LTM may retain a STALE fact that contradicts an updated Summary-store fact (worked example: LTM's pre-reorg note causes GPT-4o-mini to answer 'Michael Torres' instead of the current 'Jennifer Williams'); mitigated by selective store routing (oracle/hybrid) that avoids querying stale/irrelevant stores in the first place, cutting context tokens 62% while INCREASING QA accuracy.
cita: Gaikwad (2026). Did You Check the Right Pocket? Cost-Sensitive Store Routing for Memory-Augmented Agents.
notes: S3.1-3.2: the paper routes across 4 MemGPT-style stores -- STM (short-term/current conversation), Summary (compressed user facts/preferences/ongoing projects), LTM (summaries of past conversations), Episodic (raw transcripts) -> mem_tipos=TRABAJO(STM)+SEMANTICA(Summary)+EPISODICA(LTM+Episodic). representacion=NA, retrieval=NA, operaciones=NA, trigger=NA: this paper is EXCLUSIVELY about a meta-level WHICH-STORE-to-query routing decision, explicitly bypassing within-store mechanics -- 'We concatenate full store contents instead of performing top-k retrieval within each store... production systems often apply ranking or filtering within each memory store' (S7 Limitations) -- so how content is represented/written/retrieved WITHIN a store is never defined here. mide_lectura=SI regardless: the core evaluation directly measures the downstream UTILITY of memory reading via store-selection choices (Table2: oracle 86.7% vs uniform 81.3% QA accuracy at 299 vs 787 tokens, -62% context, GPT-4o-mini) -> RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO in F. S5.3 'Conflicting information' example (Summary='Jennifer Williams' current manager vs LTM's stale pre-reorg 'Michael Torres' note) is a direct cross-source staleness/consistency case (FIDELIDAD 'costuras', rule7) -> fidelidad_procedencia=SI, FIDELIDAD in F. Table1 synthetic routing (1,000 queries/7 types): Uniform=100% coverage/8% exact-match/waste=2.9; Hybrid=94%/58%/1.2; Oracle=100%/100%/0. Table2 LLM QA (150 Qs): oracle beats uniform on BOTH accuracy (86.7% vs 81.3%) AND tokens (-62%), gap widening in the long-context regime (72% vs 60%) -> this uniform-retrieval underperformance despite MORE context is a clear NEGATIVO(b) finding -> NEGATIVO in F. S6.1 Table3 feature ablation (linguistic-only 57% coverage baseline -> +semantic signals +33pp=90% -> +embedding-similarity-tiebreak +4pp=94%) -> evidencia_tipo=ABLATION. S6.2: routing overhead <1ms rule-based / ~5ms embedding-based vs 500-2000ms LLM inference -> metricas=LATENCIA, evidencia_tipo=MEDICION-COSTO. benchmarks derive synthetic store-labels FROM LoCoMo+LongMemEval taxonomies (S5.1/S9) plus an own 150-question QA benchmark -> BENCHMARK-E2E. alcance=SESION: stores explicitly span 'current conversation' through 'historical sessions' for one user (S3.1). F_screening was COSTO;RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO; full text confirms and adds FIDELIDAD (staleness/conflicting-source example) and NEGATIVO (uniform-retrieval-with-more-context underperforms selective routing).

title: MemX: A Local-First Long-Term Memory System for AI Assistants
benchmarks: Two custom Chinese-language benchmark scenarios (Default, High-Confusion, own); LongMemEval (external, 500 queries)
fallos_mitigaciones: The low-confidence rejection rule addresses spurious recalls when no answer exists in the memory store (S3.6, threshold tau=0.50 tuned via sweep). Separately, tag-signature deduplication -- intended to prevent template duplicates from crowding out results -- COUNTER-INTUITIVELY HURTS recall on the tag-free LongMemEval fact-granularity dataset: the full pipeline underperforms a vector-only baseline by 5.0pp Hit@5 because all fact-level memories share an identical (empty) tag signature, so dedup discards co-relevant facts from the same session (S5.4, Table7); this contrasts with the SAME mechanism improving Hit@3 by +2.7pp on the tagged custom scenarios (Table9), showing the mitigation is data-dependent and can itself become a failure mode.
cita: Sun (2026). MemX: A Local-First Long-Term Memory System for AI Assistants.
notes: S3.2 Data Model: memories table (content/embedding/type/tags/metadata/importance + access_count/retrieval_count + timestamps) + memory_links table (7 relation types: similar/related/contradicts/extends/supersedes/caused_by/temporal, NOT YET integrated into the search pipeline -- 'planned extension', S2/S6) -> mem_tipos=SEMANTICA(user facts/preferences)+PROCEDIMENTAL(explicit 'procedural' memory type: deployment checklists, debugging strategies, incident procedures)+EPISODICA(incident resolutions), representacion=HIBRIDA (vector+FTS5-text+link-table-graph, though graph unused in retrieval). fidelidad_procedencia=NO (conservative call): memory_links SCHEMA explicitly supports contradicts/supersedes/temporal relations but is not yet functionally wired into retrieval -- treated as a planned/unimplemented feature, spot-check flag. Algorithm1/S3.3-3.6: hybrid pipeline -- embed query (Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B, 1024-dim) -> parallel vector recall (DiskANN/brute-force cosine) + FTS5 keyword recall -> RRF fusion (k=60) -> four-factor re-rank (semantic/recency/frequency/importance, Eq.1-3) -> z-score+sigmoid normalize (Eq.4) -> low-confidence rejection gate -> content+tag-signature dedup -> top-k + stats write-back -> retrieval=EMBEDDINGS(vector)+RANKING(RRF/four-factor rerank)+GREP-ARCHIVOS(FTS5 keyword full-text), operaciones=WRITE(insertion)+ACTUALIZACION(retrieval_count/last_retrieved_at written back on EVERY search, Algorithm1 line11, S3.7 explicit access-vs-retrieval separation). trigger=NA: paper is retrieval-pipeline-focused; the WRITE-time policy for creating new memory entries is never detailed. mide_lectura=SI: Hit@k/MRR/Coverage@k/Miss-Empty-Rate/Miss-Strict-Rate are the paper's core evaluation currency (Table3, Table5-6) -> RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO in F. Table3: Default scenario Hit@1=91.3%/MRR=0.935 (1,014 records); High-Confusion Hit@1=100%/Coverage@5=75% (600 records) -> BENCHMARK-E2E. S5.4 Table5-6 LongMemEval (500 Qs, 4 ability types, 3 granularities session/round/fact): fact-level DOUBLES Hit@5 (24.6%->51.6%) and MRR (0.183->0.380) vs session-level; temporal/multi-session reasoning remain weak (<=43.6% Hit@5, 'confirming these abilities require mechanisms beyond single-query vector recall... that MemX does not yet implement') -> NEGATIVO(b) limitation finding. S5.5/Table8: FTS5 vs naive LIKE keyword search gives a 1,100x speedup at 100,486 records (3,483ms->34.6ms), keeping end-to-end search under 90ms at 220,349 records -> COSTO in F, metricas=LATENCIA, evidencia_tipo=MEDICION-COSTO. S5.6 Table9 cumulative pipeline-component ablation (V/V+K/V+K+Rej/Full) + S5.3 Table4 rejection-threshold sweep -> evidencia_tipo=ABLATION. alcance=SESION: explicit 'single-user, locally-deployed AI assistant' framing, persisting across many interaction sessions (LongMemEval spans 19,195 sessions), not project-code-scoped. F_screening was RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO;COSTO; full text confirms and adds WRITE and NEGATIVO.

title: D-MEM: Dopamine-Gated Agentic Memory via Reward Prediction Error Routing
benchmarks: LoCoMo; LoCoMo-Noise (own contribution)
fallos_mitigaciones: Synchronous 'append-and-evolve-all' systems (e.g. A-MEM) process EVERY utterance through an O(N^2) evolution pipeline, causing 'severe write-latency, unbounded API token costs, and catastrophic context window pollution caused by conversational noise' (S1); mitigated via the RPE-gated Critic Router that tiers inputs into SKIP/CONSTRUCT_ONLY/FULL_EVOLUTION. Separately, the paper self-reports its own limitation: the Utility-based skip mechanism causes A-MEM to lead on Single-hop retrieval (44.7% vs 21.6%) because 'short, low-complexity factual statements... receive near-zero Utility scores and are correctly routed to SKIP' -- described as 'a principled efficiency trade-off rather than a system failure' (S5.1/S6.1).
cita: Song and Xin (2026). D-MEM: Dopamine-Gated Agentic Memory via Reward Prediction Error Routing.
notes: S4.1-4.2: Agentic RPE = bounded multiplicative gate RPE(xt)=min(1.0, I(Utility>=tau)*[Utility*(Surprise+beta)]) combining Z-score-normalized semantic Surprise (cosine-similarity vs sliding-window historical mean/std, correcting embedding anisotropy) + LLM-classified long-term Utility (Transient/Short-Term/Persistent tiers, JSON-schema-constrained lightweight LLM call) -> trigger=DISCRECIONAL-LLM(utility classification uses an LLM call)+PRESUPUESTO(the whole architecture is an explicit compute-budget/cost-aware tiered gate). Critic Router routes each turn via theta_low=0.3/theta_high=0.7 into SKIP(bypass,0 cost)/CONSTRUCT_ONLY(O(1) atomic node into fast STM buffer)/FULL_EVOLUTION(O(N) deep graph restructuring: dynamic linking + retroactive update of historical nodes, reserved for 'factual contradictions or paradigm-shifting preference changes') -> operaciones=WRITE(Note Construction)+ADMISION(the tiered RPE gate IS an admission-control mechanism)+CONSOLIDACION(FULL_EVOLUTION graph restructuring/linking)+ACTUALIZACION(retroactive update of historical nodes). mem_tipos=EPISODICA(per-utterance atomic memory nodes)+SEMANTICA(evolving knowledge-graph facts/preferences, inherited A-MEM paradigm), representacion=HIBRIDA(knowledge graph + vector embeddings for surprise/retrieval + raw-text STM/Shadow buffers). fidelidad_procedencia=SI: FULL_EVOLUTION is explicitly triggered by and designed to resolve 'factual contradictions' and 'continuously resolve conflicts... maintain a highly accurate, contradiction-free internal state' (S1/S3.2) -> FIDELIDAD in F. S4.3 Zero-Cost Retrieval Augmentation: hybrid BM25+vector RRF fusion (entity precision) + O(1) Shadow-Buffer FIFO fallback (raw text of SKIPped turns, defends adversarial queries) -> retrieval=EMBEDDINGS;RANKING;GRAFO. mide_lectura=SI: S5.1-5.2 Table1-2 report per-category F1/BLEU (Single/Temporal/Open/Multi-hop/Adversarial) -> RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO in F. title: D-Mem: A Dual-Process Memory System for LLM Agents
benchmarks: LoCoMo, RealTalk
fallos_mitigaciones: 'Lossy abstraction' from query-agnostic memory compression is the central problem addressed: aggressive query-independent compression strips crucial contextual nuance (unstated temporal logic, multi-hop dependencies), leaving agents unable to answer queries requiring rigorous deduction (S1); mitigated via a query-guided System2 Full-Deliberation fallback + Quality-Gating escalation policy. Separately, an honest negative finding: 'When deploying Qwen3-235B-Instruct on the highly noisy RealTalk dataset, the addition of explicit filtering counterintuitively degrades performance compared to the unfiltered Mem0* (e.g. LLM score drops from 62.5 to 60.0)... erroneous pruning of critical context' (S4.2) -- aggressive context filtering is model-alignment-dependent and can itself hurt.
cita: You et al. (2026). D-Mem: A Dual-Process Memory System for LLM Agents.
notes: S3.1 Mem0* (System1, enhanced Mem0): Extraction Phase conditions LLM on top-10 similar existing memories + last-8-messages -> extracts salient memories Omega; Update Phase retrieves top-5 similar historical memories per omega_i, DISCARDS low-relevance items via cosine-similarity threshold>0.8 (ADMISION), then an LLM cross-references new-vs-background memories for contradictions/redundancies -> dictates ADD/UPDATE/DELETE/NOOP per item (Fig.1 PartA) -> operaciones=WRITE(ADD)+ADMISION(cosine>0.8 filter)+CONSOLIDACION(contradiction/redundancy cross-referencing)+OLVIDO(DELETE)+ACTUALIZACION(UPDATE) -- ALL 5 non-NA operaciones tokens explicitly present. mem_tipos=EPISODICA(per-turn extracted facts)+SEMANTICA(salient conversational facts/preferences), representacion=HIBRIDA(vector DB System1 + raw chunked dialogue text System2 Full Deliberation). trigger=EVENTO-DETERMINISTA ('The maintenance pipeline dynamically triggers upon the ingestion of the new interaction round at step t', S3.1). retrieval=EMBEDDINGS(top-K/30/10/5 vector similarity throughout)+RANKING(0-10 relevance scoring + multi-stage filtering, S3.3). fidelidad_procedencia=SI: explicit LLM cross-referencing of new-vs-background memories 'to evaluate potential contradictions and redundancies' (S3.1) PLUS the Quality-Gating rubric's 'Faithfulness & Consistency' dimension (S3.2) -> FIDELIDAD in F. mide_lectura=SI: F1/LLM-as-judge/BLEU across LoCoMo+RealTalk (Table1-2, per-category breakdown Fig.2), and Quality Gating literally assesses the initial retrieved answer's Relevance/Faithfulness/Completeness before deciding whether to escalate -> RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO in F. Fig.2 per-category F1 gain of Quality-Gating over Mem0* scales with question difficulty (Single-Hop smallest, Temporal/Open-Domain largest) -> evidencia_tipo=ABLATION (3-policy comparison Majority-Voting/Consensus/Quality-Gating, Table1-2 fallback-rate breakdown). alcance=SESION (LoCoMo 10 long-term dialogues ~24K tokens avg / RealTalk 10 conversations ~16K words avg). title: Knowledge Access Beats Model Size: Memory Augmented Routing for Persistent AI Agents

notes: S3-A Cross-Model Memory Injection: after EACH inference call, the routing layer stores the VERBATIM conversation turn-pair (Q+A, session-timestamp-prefixed) + Matryoshka embedding + user-level metadata into a Milvus vector DB, partitioned by user (multi-tenant isolation) -> operaciones=WRITE only (explicit design choice: 'we store verbatim conversation turn-pairs rather than LLM-generated summaries, avoiding the hallucination risk that would compound with retrieval noise' -- no ADMISION/CONSOLIDACION/OLVIDO/ACTUALIZACION found), trigger=EVENTO-DETERMINISTA ('After each inference call...'), mem_tipos=EPISODICA (explicit verbatim-turn-pair design), representacion=HIBRIDA (dense Matryoshka embeddings + BM25 sparse index, S3-D). retrieval=EMBEDDINGS(cosine over Matryoshka embeddings)+RANKING(BM25 n-gram + RRF/weighted/BM25-dominant fusion, S3-D). mide_lectura=SI: the entire paper is a direct causal measurement of memory-read utility on downstream F1 -> RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO in F. fidelidad_procedencia=NO: no staleness/contradiction/consistency-across-sources mechanism for memory CONTENT is implemented (turn-pairs simply appended verbatim; 'RAG poisoning' is cited only as an external risk, not a mechanism this paper builds). title: SNT-MEM: Operator-Structured Memory Management Framework
benchmarks: LongBench (multi-document QA, real Llama-3-8B integration, S4.2); synthetic 1024-slot 'Long-Context Benchmark' simulation vs vanilla-RAG/Mem0-style baselines (S4.1, own/unnamed)
fallos_mitigaciones: Theorem3.1 'Necessity of Pruning or Compression' proves any finite-capacity memory receiving unbounded input MUST implement pruning or compression to maintain retrieval fidelity above epsilon>0 -- the unbounded-growth/sobre-retencion failure mode; mitigated via the Irreversible-Loss (pruning) + Subspace-Mapping (compression) operator pair (S2.5 'Capacity as an Emergent Constraint'). The real-world validation (Table3) shows this bounding comes at a real, honestly-reported cost: F1 QA accuracy on LongBench DROPS from 48.2 to 47.1 (-2.2%) in exchange for 4.2x token compression and a bounded 8GB memory ceiling.
cita: Yazir (2026). SNT-MEM: Operator-Structured Memory Management Framework for Self-Regulating AI Systems.
notes: RECONSIDERAR: this paper is a highly abstract, quantum-formalism-heavy theoretical framework (density operators/CPTP maps/von-Neumann entropy over generic 'memory modes', S2) whose PRIMARY validation is a synthetic simulation (Table2: 1024-slot memory, 1000 timesteps, vs vanilla-RAG/Mem0-style baselines that are not concretely specified as real systems, S4.1); only S4.2 (2 sentences) + Table3 touches a real model (Llama-3-8B on LongBench multi-doc QA), and even there the 'Baseline' configuration is left unspecified -- extraction proceeds per protocol but the thin real-world grounding + heavy abstraction warrants human reconsideration of inclusion. S2.2 Eq.3: memory evolves via a FIXED composition of all 7 CPTP operators applied EVERY timestep -> trigger=EVENTO-DETERMINISTA (deterministic per-timestep composition, not event/LLM/budget-gated in the ordinary sense). Table1/S2.4 explicit operator-to-memory-function mapping: Irreversible-Loss='low-utility pruning/forgetting' (Eq.9, post-selection+renormalization) -> operaciones includes OLVIDO; Subspace-Mapping='representation transformation/consolidation' (Eq.10, Kraus-operator compression) -> CONSOLIDACION; Liminal='capacity bounds/working memory limit' (Eq.8, soft threshold) -> ADMISION; Table6 defines an explicit Write complexity O(log N) -> WRITE; Cyclic-Reset='bounded refresh cycles/refractory period' (Eq.5) -> ACTUALIZACION -- all 5 non-NA operaciones tokens map onto the 7-operator taxonomy, inferred from an abstract mathematical formalism. mem_tipos=NA and representacion=VECTOR (closest practical analogue to the density-matrix/salience-state formalism): the framework is explicitly content-agnostic, no discussion of WHAT type of information -episodic/semantic/procedural- is stored. retrieval=NA: Table6 gives only complexity classes (Retrieval-cache O(1), Retrieval-store O(log N)) via vague 'Phase Nexter'/'Phase Reverser' operators, no concrete mechanism ever specified. S4.1 Table2 (50 runs, synthetic benchmark): 63.3%+-2.1% memory reduction vs vanilla-RAG, 22.3%+-1.8% vs Mem0-style, 3.8x+-0.3x retrieval speedup -> COSTO in F, metricas=COSTO-TOKENS/OTRA, evidencia_tipo=MEDICION-COSTO. S4.2/Table3 (real Llama-3-8B, LongBench, >32k-token contexts): 4.2x token compression, TTFT 140ms->42ms, memory ceiling unbounded->fixed@8GB, F1 DROPS 48.2->47.1 -> mide_lectura=SI (F1 QA IS measured) -> RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO in F, NEGATIVO in F, evidencia_tipo=BENCHMARK-E2E. S4.3 Table4: systematic per-operator ablation (removing each of 7 operators, measuring Memory/Speed/Consolidation-loss %) shows every operator contributes uniquely -> evidencia_tipo=ABLATION. alcance=TAREA: the only concrete grounding (S4.2) is single-document/single-long-context QA (LongBench), not multi-session persistent dialogue memory. title: Hybrid Governance Architecture: A Self-Improving Memory Substrate for LLM Agents with Progressive Cost Reduction and Deterministic Replay
benchmarks: MS-MARCO (L1 retrieval quality, R@5); 14 own controlled experiments (E1-E14): 12 simulated workloads + 2 live GPT-5.4-nano API measurements (E13/E14); no LoCoMo/LongMemEval/SWE-bench used
fallos_mitigaciones: LLM output stochasticity is a core failure mode addressed: 'the same query run 20 times produces between 2 and 8 syntactically distinct tool call variations' (S1), and E14 confirms raw LLM consistency of only 55-90% (mean 79%) across repeated identical inputs; mitigated via deterministic Stage3 replay (100% consistency by construction). Separately, adversarial/OOD queries risk triggering an UNSAFE fast-path replay on a deceptive input; mitigated via 3 safety coherence checks (slot-extraction-method / template-skeleton-similarity<0.75 / >20%-novel-content-words), achieving zero silent failures across 300 adversarial and out-of-distribution probes (E3, S3.6).
cita: Sertel (2026). Hybrid Governance Architecture: A Self-Improving Memory Substrate for LLM Agents with Progressive Cost Reduction and Deterministic Replay.
notes: S3: three-layer substrate -- L1 Routing Memory (VQ semantic retrieval, 1-byte routing codes, 768x compression vs dense fp32, R@5=0.959 on MS-MARCO retaining 99.6% of dense recall, S3.1) + L2 Deterministic Vault (SHA-256-hashed exact key-value store w/ policy tags PUBLIC/INTERNAL/SENSITIVE/RESTRICTED, accessed only on gate escalation, L1-only exact-match=22.5%/77.5%-near-miss vs L2=100%/0%-near-miss, E4, S3.2) + L3 Semantic Neuron Layer (stores 'routing experience': tool selected + params extracted + extraction method + success, maturing through 4 stages New->Developing->Reliable->Autonomous, Table1, S3.3) -> mem_tipos=EPISODICA(per-decision routing experience)+SEMANTICA(L1 semantic content)+PROCEDIMENTAL(L3 literally stores tool-use DECISION/procedure chains), representacion=HIBRIDA. Governance Gate (S3.4, Algorithm1) fuses confidence(L1)+margin+sensitivity+neuron-maturity(L3) to select 1-of-5 execution paths (Table2) -> operaciones=WRITE(new items)+ADMISION(gate=admission-routing; exact-key/high-sensitivity ALWAYS forced to DeterministicPath)+CONSOLIDACION(S3.5: Active consolidation on every API call updates neuron edge weights; Passive consolidation runs BETWEEN SESSIONS with 6 ops incl. edge-finalization/co-occurrence-mining/codebook-reshaping/vault-compaction, E10: 35 ops/0 LLM calls)+OLVIDO(salience-guided forgetting, S(m)=0.4*recency+0.3*frequency+0.3*importance Eq.1, 4-tier lifecycle keep/summarize/migrate/delete, E11: 1000->614 items=38.6% reduction, RESTRICTED/SENSITIVE items NEVER deleted)+ACTUALIZACION(neuron maturation/edge-weight updates). trigger=EVENTO-DETERMINISTA(active consolidation on every completed query)+CHECKPOINT(passive consolidation runs between sessions)+PRESUPUESTO(drift-detection threshold qerr>1.3x-baseline triggers codebook reshaping E9; the architecture's central thesis IS progressive cost reduction via threshold-gated tiered execution). retrieval=EMBEDDINGS(L1 VQ vector routing)+RANKING(dot-product bucket rerank + score-based token filtering)+GRAFO(L3 neuron edge weights/co-occurrence mining). fidelidad_procedencia=SI: L2 SHA-256 integrity hashes + drift-detection (staleness of routing index) + S3.6 Safety Mechanisms (3 coherence checks verifying a cached decision remains valid before replay, zero silent failures across 300 adversarial/OOD probes) -> FIDELIDAD in F. SEGURIDAD in F: explicit policy-tag access control, sensitivity=HIGH ALWAYS forces exact DeterministicPath (never a semantic near-miss on sensitive data). mide_lectura=SI: E1 R@5(MS-MARCO), E2 gate-accuracy(94% phase-weighted, 0% unsafe-fast-path-rate), E4 L1-vs-L2 exact-match contrast -> RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO in F. S5.4 Table5 E2 gate ABLATION (Full-Gate/No-L3-Signal/No-Sensitivity/No-Margin/Always-L1/Always-LLM): removing L3 signal collapses accuracy 94%->38.7% while removing sensitivity/margin has NO effect under normal workload -> evidencia_tipo=ABLATION. S5.1-5.2 E12(1000-episode sim, 3 phases incl. drift-injection)+E13(400 LIVE GPT-5.4-nano queries): 89.5% cumulative token savings (E12) / 78.1% real-token savings vs Dense-RAG (E13, 15,630 vs 71,479 tokens, Table3) -> COSTO in F, metricas=COSTO-TOKENS, evidencia_tipo=MEDICION-COSTO;BENCHMARK-E2E. S5.3 E14: Stage3 replay achieves 100% deterministic consistency vs the SAME LLM's raw output achieving only 55-90% consistency (mean 79%, Table4) -> NEGATIVO(b) finding about relying on raw unmediated LLM decisions -> NEGATIVO in F, fallos_mitigaciones anchor. handoff=CONTENIDO;CONTRATO: L3 neurons encode a reusable DECISION CONTRACT (which tool, which parameters, how derived) that persists and replays across future episodes/sessions ('Passive consolidation runs between sessions', S3.5). alcance=SESION: framed around a persistent long-running agent across many episodes (E12's 1,000-episode integration test; S4 Workload characterization). F_screening was WRITE;RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO;CONSOLIDACION;COSTO;FIDELIDAD; full text confirms all five and adds SEGURIDAD and NEGATIVO.

title: Deep Researcher Agent: An Autonomous Framework for 24/7 Deep Learning Experimentation with Zero-Cost Monitoring
benchmarks: NINGUNO
fallos_mitigaciones: Unbounded context growth in long-running agents causes degraded LLM performance, escalating API costs, and eventual context-window overflow (S3.3); mitigated via the Two-Tier Constant-Size Memory bounded at ~5,000 chars with LOSSY-BY-DESIGN auto-compaction (oldest milestone entries dropped past 1,200 chars; only 15 most-recent decisions retained) -- explicitly described as mirroring how humans forget routine details while keeping key milestones. title: Learning When to Remember: Risk-Sensitive Contextual Bandits for Abstention-Aware Memory Retrieval in LLM-Based Coding Agents

cita: Iscan (2026). Learning When to Remember: Risk-Sensitive Contextual Bandits for Abstention-Aware Memory Retrieval in LLM-Based Coding Agents.
notes: S2.1/Eq.6, Fig.2: pattern-variant-episode memory schema mi=(pi,Vi,Ei) -- pattern(canonical repository-agnostic symptom+root-cause class)+variant(context-specific fix strategy+command/path/stack signatures)+episode(concrete observed failure+validation+feedback) -> mem_tipos=PROCEDIMENTAL(reusable fix-strategy knowledge, explicit repair-procedure focus)+EPISODICA(episode layer=concrete observed past-failure instances). representacion: S2.9 'The benchmark implementation is local-first and deterministic: it does not require hosted LLM calls, EXTERNAL EMBEDDING SERVICES, or network access' -- NO vector embeddings used; retrieval evidence is lexical/structural/entity/command/path/stack matching (S2.3/2.4) -> representacion=DOCS-ARCHIVOS, retrieval=GREP-ARCHIVOS(lexical baseline 'lexical_only')+RANKING(candidate compatibility scoring st,i=F(qt,ct,i), top1/top2-score+margin features, Table1). It does NOT WRITE memory, does not compress memory off-line, does not resolve contradictions between competing entries, and does not decide when an old episode should be retired. It only answers ONE QUESTION AT READ TIME: is this retrieved memory safe to inject right now?' -> operaciones=NA (paper explicitly disclaims write/admission-at-write/consolidation/forgetting; its entire mechanism is a READ-TIME injection gate) and correspondingly trigger=NA (no write/consolidate/forget trigger to characterize). mide_lectura=SI: the ENTIRE evaluation (Recall@1/3, MRR, nDCG@3, false-positive rate, offline-replay success rate, hot-path proxy success) IS a direct measurement of read/injection-decision utility -> RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO in F (mandatory, rule3). alcance=PROYECTO: 'repository-local operational knowledge' explicitly reused across many debugging episodes within the SAME codebase over time (S1), beyond a single task/session. multiagente=NO (single coding agent). fidelidad_procedencia=SI: the system's core function IS a safety/verification gate deciding whether retrieved memory is trustworthy enough to inject ('is this retrieved memory safe to inject right now', S1) using historical-false-positive-rate/session-rejection/structural-compatibility features (Table1) -- squarely FIDELIDAD (verification before use). title: ScrapMem: A Bio-inspired Framework for On-device Personalized Agent Memory via Optical Forgetting
benchmarks: ATM-Bench (Mei et al. 2026, four-year real-world multimodal personal-data benchmark)
fallos_mitigaciones: Parametric memory 'is prone to catastrophic forgetting and lacks interpretability'; retrieval-based methods 'struggle to align heterogeneous modalities... leading to weak performance on causal, temporal, and logical reasoning' (S2.1); mitigated via unified scrapbook-page multimodal aggregation + graph-structured EM-Paths. Robustness finding: even under severe Optical-Forgetting visual degradation (JPEG quality down to 40-70, resolution scaling to 0.60-0.85), R@10 remains stable around 66% because 'retrieval performance does not rely heavily on high-quality visual inputs' -- structural EM-Graph nodes/paths preserve stable semantics (S5.3).

title: When Stored Evidence Stops Being Usable: Scale-Conditioned Evaluation of Agent Memory
benchmarks: LongMemEval; LoCoMo
fallos_mitigaciones: The paper's contribution IS a failure-taxonomy, not a mitigation: it decomposes reliability loss under evidence-preserving irrelevant-memory growth into pexh(budget-exhaustion: retrieval-call count exceeds the stated budget) vs pwrong(wrong-within-budget: agent stays within budget but answers incorrectly) -- e.g. flat interfaces (OpenClaw) mainly show pwrong(noisy/insufficient returned context), planar (Mem0) shows search-and-stopping instability with either regime dominating depending on agent size, hierarchical single-pass (HippoRAG) shows rising pwrong, hierarchical multi-hop (LiCoMemory) shows pexh that shrinks with larger agent models (S5.2-5.3).
cita: Shao et al. (2026). When Stored Evidence Stops Being Usable: Scale-Conditioned Evaluation of Agent Memory.
notes: This is a pure EVALUATION-PROTOCOL paper, not a memory mechanism: 'Our goal is not to introduce a new benchmark or memory architecture, but to turn this construction into a trajectory-level evaluation protocol for agent-memory systems' (S1) -> mem_tipos=NA/representacion=NA/operaciones=NA/trigger=NA (rule5: explains what it MEASURES instead below), evaluating SIX EXISTING memory interfaces (flat: OpenClaw/MemOS-text; planar: Mem0/MemOS-Tree; hierarchical: HippoRAG/LiCoMemory) across THREE agent sizes (Qwen3-8B/32B/235B) without proposing its own. Protocol (S3): for each query, fix annotated task-relevant evidence E(q) while injecting Nirr(s) IRRELEVANT sessions per a shared scale ladder s0..s4 (evidence-preserving scaling, following LongMemEval); log agent-memory trajectories; report 4 diagnostics -- Pass@B(Eq.1, budget-compliant reliability), P90R(Eq.2, tail retrieval-call quantile), failure-regime decomposition pexh/pwrong(Eq.3), and breakdown onset s*_alpha(Eq.4, first scale where reliability<70%). mide_lectura=SI: the ENTIRE evaluation IS a measurement of memory-read reliability/utility at scale -> RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO mandatory in F (rule3). alcance=SESION: LongMemEval/LoCoMo multi-session dialogues with injected irrelevant sessions. multiagente=NO (single agent per trial). fidelidad_procedencia=NO: explicitly OUT OF SCOPE -- 'We do not claim to measure... stale/contradictory memory management' (S1 Scope paragraph). Table1: HippoRAG loses 16.0-20.0pp Pass@B0 from s0->s4 across all 3 agent sizes despite ALWAYS staying within the 2-call budget (pexh=0, S5.1); LiCoMemory shows agent-dependent behavior, Qwen3-8B already below threshold at s0(53.5%) while Qwen3-32B/235B remain reliable through s4(>400 irrelevant sessions, breakdown onset s*_0.7>400) -> central finding is NEGATIVO(b)-style evidence that stored evidence becomes UNUSABLE as irrelevant memory accumulates even when the gold evidence never leaves the accessible history ('When Stored Evidence Stops Being Usable' -- title itself is the negative finding). Table2/Fig.3: failure-regime decomposition shows Mem0(planar) exhibits search-and-stopping instability(pexh 79.2-83.6% for larger agents vs pwrong 85.6% for Qwen3-8B); this decomposition -- systematically varying ONLY memory scale s while holding evidence/agent/interface/budget fixed -- constitutes a rigorous controlled single-variable study -> evidencia_tipo=ABLATION(scale-ladder sweep)+BENCHMARK-E2E(LongMemEval/LoCoMo across 6 memory systems x 3 agents)+MEDICION-COSTO(P90R retrieval-call-tail burden, metricas=ITERACION). F_screening was RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO;COSTO; full text confirms both and adds NEGATIVO.

title: Remember the Decision, Not the Description: A Rate-Distortion Framework for Agent Memory
benchmarks: LoCoMo; LongMemEval; MemoryArena
fallos_mitigaciones: Existing memory systems organize experience around DESCRIPTIVE criteria (relevance/salience/summary quality) rather than DECISION-relevant distinctions; the paper shows this is a real, measured failure: on LoCoMo, descriptive similarity is 'a statistically significant but weak predictor of evidence compatibility (Spearman rho=0.103, AUC=0.548)... description-based retrieval recovers only 66% of gold evidence, compared to 83% for DeMem, and 85% of description-based errors trace directly to evidence miss/dilution caused by this mismatch' (S1, Appendix E.13); mitigated via the decision-centric rate-distortion reformulation: DeMem's certified online learner splits a memory slot ONLY when data certify decision conflict (Theorem1 exact forgetting boundary), rather than merging/splitting by descriptive similarity.
cita: Zou et al. (2026). Remember the Decision, Not the Description: A Rate-Distortion Framework for Agent Memory.
notes: S3.1/Eq.3, Fig.1: DeMem maintains K bounded RUNTIME memory slots -- a query-aware encoder Mt=gt(Ht,Qt) routes each dialogue history into one of K slots, and a decision rule pi acts only from the current query + selected slot, never the full history -> mem_tipos=TRABAJO (explicit bounded 'runtime memory' interface constraining WHAT the policy can access at decision time, Fig.1 example shows slot content as short textual states e.g. '[camping-answer state] Melanie & kids recently camped...'). representacion=DOCS-ARCHIVOS: slot content is compressed TEXTUAL state summaries (Fig.1), no vector-DB/graph store described for the memory itself (embeddings are used only for the certification/routing SCORE, not as the storage representation). operaciones: WRITE(gt routes new history-query pairs into slots)+CONSOLIDACION(K-state compression of raw histories into a bounded partition, Section3.1-3.4 'compresses interaction histories into a limited set of runtime memory states')+OLVIDO(Theorem1 'exact FORGETTING boundary for what can be safely FORGOTTEN' is the paper's central theoretical contribution -- histories sharing a common near-optimal action can be safely merged/forgotten)+ACTUALIZACION(Algorithm1 'Refresh: compute P_e+1<-GreedyColorK(E_e)' -- the slot partition is refreshed every epoch based on newly certified cannot-link conflicts). trigger=EVENTO-DETERMINISTA(split triggered when data CERTIFY dt(x,x')>epsilon, a computed/deterministic statistical-certification condition, S4.1)+CHECKPOINT(the partition Pe is FROZEN for each epoch and only refreshed at epoch boundaries, Algorithm1). retrieval=EMBEDDINGS+RANKING(the LoCoMo-instance worked example, Fig.1, shows a 'Dialogue Encoder'/'Decision Encoder' computing split-trigger/conflict scores e.g. 0.3513/0.4511 used to route/certify slot assignment). mide_lectura=SI: cumulative regret, memory-distortion curves, and LoCoMo/LongMemEval/MemoryArena QA accuracy are the paper's entire empirical currency (Fig.2, Table1) -> RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO in F. alcance=SESION (LoCoMo/LongMemEval multi-session conversational benchmarks). multiagente=NO (single-agent decision policy). fidelidad_procedencia=NO (the paper addresses decision-relevant COMPRESSION, not staleness/contradiction/provenance verification of content). Table1: DeMem reaches Overall=0.911-0.920 on LoCoMo (GPT-4o-mini/GPT-4.1-mini) vs the next-best baseline Mnemis 0.888/0.906 and vs Zep/RAG/Mem0/LangMem/FullContext/Nemori/EMem-G all clearly lower -> BENCHMARK-E2E. Fig.2: synthetic Decoupled-Bandit ablation sweeps memory-budget K vs regret and description-decision MISMATCH severity, isolating exactly why description-aware baselines (Feature-KMeans/Feature-RAG/CLUB) fail as mismatch grows -> ABLATION. NEGATIVO in F: the rho=0.103/AUC=0.548 finding is direct NEGATIVO(b)-style evidence that descriptive-similarity-based memory (the dominant paradigm in prior systems) is a weak, and can be a misleading, criterion for what to remember. title: RecMem: Recurrence-based Memory Consolidation for Efficient and Effective Long-Running LLM Agents
benchmarks: LoCoMo; LongMemEval-S
fallos_mitigaciones: 'Existing memory systems invoke LLMs to process EVERY incoming interaction for memory extraction, and such an eager memory consolidation scheme leads to substantial token consumption' (S1); mitigated via recurrence-based consolidation -- LLM-based extraction is invoked only when an incoming interaction finds a sufficient number (>=theta_count) of semantically similar interactions already buffered in the cheap subconscious layer, cutting memory-construction tokens by up to 87% (7.8x) while EXCEEDING baseline accuracy. Separately, event-level episodic abstraction 'may omit fine-grained but query-critical details, leading to lossy long-term memory' (S1.3), mitigated via the Semantic Refinement mechanism that revisits raw interactions to recover missing persistent facts.
cita: Dai et al. (2026). RecMem: Recurrence-based Memory Consolidation for Efficient and Effective Long-Running LLM Agents.
