notes: S3.1-3.4: three-tier architecture -- subconscious memory (lightweight vector-indexed raw interaction units, no LLM at write time)+episodic memory (temporally-anchored event narratives, merge-first strategy)+semantic memory (atomic facts via 'Semantic Refinement') -> mem_tipos=EPISODICA;SEMANTICA (paper's own explicit convention, S3.1), representacion=VECTOR (subconscious/episodic/semantic all encoded and indexed via dense encoder Phi(.), no graph/doc-file store used; S3.6 notes graph is only a HYPOTHETICAL alternative structure, not implemented: 'the higher memory layers can also adopt alternative structures (e.g., knowledge graph)'). operaciones=WRITE(Eq.4 subconscious ingestion of every turn)+ADMISION(Eq.5 recurrence-count gate |Ri|>=theta_count decides which clusters get PROMOTED to LLM-consolidated tiers -- an explicit write-admission control)+CONSOLIDACION(Eq.7 LLM-based episodic-narrative synthesis + Eq.9 semantic-fact extraction, S3.3-3.4)+ACTUALIZACION(Eq.6 merge-first in-place episode update: 'E* <- LLMmerge(E*, ui) if cos(vi,vE*)>=theta_sim'). trigger=EVENTO-DETERMINISTA(similarity/count condition computed per new arriving unit)+PRESUPUESTO(explicit recurrence-COUNT threshold theta_count gating consolidation, S3.2, tunable 4-5 per benchmark). retrieval=EMBEDDINGS(cosine similarity throughout, text-embedding-3-small)+RANKING(top-k budgeted retrieval across subconscious/episodic/semantic stores, ksub=10/kepi=5/ksem=10, S3.5). mide_lectura=SI: QA accuracy (GPT-4o-mini-as-judge) is the paper's primary metric across both benchmarks (Table1-2) -> RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO in F. alcance=SESION (LoCoMo/LongMemEval-S multi-session). multiagente=NO. fidelidad_procedencia=SI: Semantic Refinement's 'Fact Maintenance... prevents redundancy by filtering out known information in V while updating EVOLVING user states (e.g., preference changes)' (S3.4) -> FIDELIDAD in F. Table1-2: RecMem achieves the HIGHEST overall accuracy among memory systems on both LoCoMo(72.47/84.18%) and LongMemEval-S(69.20/76.80%) while reducing construction tokens up to 87%(7.8x) vs Mem0/A-Mem/MemoryOS -> BENCHMARK-E2E+MEDICION-COSTO. Appendix C hyperparameter sensitivity analysis of theta_sim/theta_count shows accuracy 'varies smoothly... within a narrow band' -> ABLATION. F_screening was WRITE;COSTO;CONSOLIDACION; full text confirms all three and adds RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO, FIDELIDAD.

title: DimMem: Dimensional Structuring for Efficient Long-Term Agent Memory
benchmarks: LoCoMo-10; LongMemEval-S
fallos_mitigaciones: 'Existing memory systems face a fidelity-efficiency trade-off: raw dialogue histories are expensive, while flat facts or summaries may discard the structure needed for precise recall' (Abstract); mitigated via explicit dimensional structuring (type/time/location/reason/purpose/keywords per memory unit) instead of flat text. Separately, 'purely embedding-based updates may miss conflicts with different wording or over-merge semantically similar but temporally distinct memories' (S3.4); mitigated by using cheap dimensional filters (type + typed-keyword overlap) as a candidate-generation layer BEFORE expensive embedding/LLM-based consolidation, so conflicting-but-dissimilar or similar-but-distinct memories are correctly routed.
cita: Qiu et al. (2026). DimMem: Dimensional Structuring for Efficient Long-Term Agent Memory.
notes: S3.1/Eq.1-2: each memory mi=<id,C,T,D,rho> has explicit type T in {fact,episodic,profile} and dimensional field D={time,location,reason,purpose,keywords} -> mem_tipos=EPISODICA(explicit 'episodic' type)+SEMANTICA(explicit 'fact' + 'profile'=long-term personal semantics types, both map to declarative/semantic knowledge). representacion=HIBRIDA: tri-path retrieval combines lexical(BM25)+dense(embedding)+dimension-structured-field matching over the same atomic records (S3.3, Eq.6) -- neither pure vector nor pure doc-store. operaciones=WRITE(S3.2 overlap-aware extraction into normalized dimensional records)+ADMISION(S3.4 'dimensions as a CHEAP CANDIDATE-GENERATION layer: records first grouped by type and filtered by typed-keyword overlap, THEN verified by embedding similarity before LLM consolidation' -- an explicit pre-write admission filter)+CONSOLIDACION(S3.4 Eq.9 LLM-consolidator decides MERGE/SUPERSEDE/KEEPBOTH per type-conditioned semantics)+OLVIDO(SUPERSEDE = explicit 'deprecation' of the outdated record, Fig.2c caption: 'dimension-aware insertion, merging, and deprecation')+ACTUALIZACION(SUPERSEDE updates stale facts, S3.4: 'newer contradictory facts may SUPERSEDE older ones'). trigger=EVENTO-DETERMINISTA (candidate-pair generation runs automatically as each new record is written, S3.4). retrieval=GREP-ARCHIVOS(BM25 lexical route Rbm25)+EMBEDDINGS(dense route Rdense, MiniLM)+RANKING(Eq.7 weighted dimension-agreement score sdim fused with the other two routes via Dedup union, S3.3). mide_lectura=SI: QA accuracy is the paper's central metric (Table1-2) with a dedicated retrieval-component ablation (Table3-4: removing dimension-scoring/'Lexical+Dense Retrieval' variant) -> RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO in F. alcance=SESION (LoCoMo-10/LongMemEval-S). multiagente=NO. fidelidad_procedencia=SI: type-conditioned SUPERSEDE explicitly resolves factual contradictions ('newer contradictory facts may SUPERSEDE older ones', S3.4) -> FIDELIDAD in F. Table1-2: DimMem achieves 81.43%/78.20% overall on LoCoMo-10/LongMemEval-S, outperforming MemoryOS/MemOS/A-Mem/LightMem/SimpleMem, while reducing LoCoMo per-query token cost by 24% (Table1 Tokens/Query column) -> BENCHMARK-E2E+MEDICION-COSTO, metricas=EXITO;COSTO-TOKENS. Table3-4: three-way controlled ablation (Content-Only Memory/Lexical+Dense-Retrieval-only/No-Causal-Intent-Dims) isolates that the dimensional REPRESENTATION itself (not just retrieval routing) is the dominant factor -- Content-Only causes the largest overall drop (-8.6% to -10.4pp) -> ABLATION. F_screening was RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO;COSTO; full text confirms both and adds WRITE, CONSOLIDACION, FIDELIDAD.

title: DeferMem: Query-Time Evidence Distillation via Reinforcement Learning for Long-Term Memory QA
benchmarks: LoCoMo; LongMemEval-S
fallos_mitigaciones: 'Existing memory systems typically process memory BEFORE future queries are known, then retrieve the resulting units based on similarity rather than their utility for answering the query. This workflow leaves downstream answerers to denoise retrieved candidates and reconstruct query-specific evidence' (Abstract/S1); write-time compression/forgetting/updating 'commits to a query-agnostic view of what matters and may discard or blur details that later become crucial.' GAM's iterative deep search is flagged as a related failure: 'step-by-step expansion... makes it difficult to determine when to stop and can incur substantial token and latency overhead' (S2). DeferMem mitigates both by DEFERRING all compression to query time: raw history is preserved verbatim (segment-link structure, no write-time consolidation) and a DistillPO-trained RL policy performs query-conditioned evidence distillation only after the query is known, achieving the fastest runtime and zero commercial-API token cost among evaluated systems.
cita: Yin and Tang (2026). DeferMem: Query-Time Evidence Distillation via Reinforcement Learning for Long-Term Memory QA.
notes: S3.1-3.2, Eq.1: DeferMem explicitly decouples memory into R(high-recall retriever, write-time)+D(query-conditioned evidence distiller, query-time) and DELIBERATELY avoids write-time compression: 'instead of compressing memory before future queries are known, DeferMem uses a lightweight segment-link structure to organize RAW conversation history' -> mem_tipos=EPISODICA (raw verbatim conversational history preserved, not extracted facts/summaries); representacion=HIBRIDA: message-level VECTOR index (Eq.3-6, cosine similarity) + segment-link GRAPH-like structure connecting semantically related segments across the whole history (S3.2, 'sparse semantic structure that traces recurring or evolving topics'). operaciones=WRITE ONLY: segment/boundary/link construction at ingestion (Eq.2-6) is the sole memory-store mutation; the paper explicitly avoids write-time CONSOLIDACION/OLVIDO/ACTUALIZACION by design (contrasted against prior systems that 'maintain [memory] through compression, forgetting, or updating mechanisms', S1) -- the query-conditioned DISTILLATION step (D) operates on retrieved candidates at READ time, not as a memory-store operation. trigger=EVENTO-DETERMINISTA (segment boundaries detected per-message via local attention-score peaks + cosine-similarity refinement, Eq.3-5, a deterministic per-arrival computation). retrieval=EMBEDDINGS(Eq.3-6 cosine-similarity top-k message hits)+RANKING(DistillPO's RL-trained message-selection+evidence-rewriting IS a learned query-conditioned reranking/filtering of the high-recall candidate set, S3.3)+GRAFO(segment-link expansion: 'expand along local semantic spans and cross-history semantic continuities' via the segment-link structure, S3.2). mide_lectura=SI: QA accuracy + memory-operation token/time cost are the paper's central results (Table1) -> RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO in F. alcance=SESION (LoCoMo/LongMemEval-S multi-session). multiagente=NO. fidelidad_procedencia=SI: DistillPO's decomposed reward explicitly verifies 'whether the distilled evidence is ALIGNED with the selected messages, FAITHFUL, and self-contained' (S3.3, reward components r0-r7) -> FIDELIDAD in F (verification of content faithfulness before downstream use). Table1: DeferMem achieves the best QA accuracy on BOTH benchmarks (70.0% LongMemEval-S, 88.25/97.09% LoCoMo non-adv/adv) while incurring 0k commercial-API tokens for memory operations and the shortest runtime (3.1x faster than LightMem on LongMemEval-S, 9.8x on LoCoMo) -> BENCHMARK-E2E+MEDICION-COSTO, metricas=EXITO;COSTO-TOKENS;LATENCIA. Table2: controlled hyperparameter sweep of segment-boundary threshold tau1 and segment-link threshold tau2, reporting Recall/Recall-01/retrieved-tokens tradeoffs -> ABLATION. F_screening was RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO;COSTO; full text confirms both and adds WRITE, FIDELIDAD.

title: M.A.K.S: Multidimensional Access Knowledge Scoring for Long-Horizon LLM Agent Memory Management
benchmarks: NINGUNO
fallos_mitigaciones: 'Current techniques such as FIFO, LRU, and attention-based evictions use a BINARY approach to manage memory by either retaining or IRREVERSIBLY DELETING data. No current system preserves its evicted memories for later recovery' (Abstract/S1); mitigated via the three-zone (FULL/PARTIAL/GHOST) gradual, REVERSIBLE fidelity-degradation architecture with a Ghost Store and cue-triggered reconsolidation, so 'content is compressed but not erased' (S3.3). Validated via the 'Needle in a Compressed Haystack' stress test: M.A.K.S reconsolidates the critical target fact (token ratio 4.58x) whereas FIFO eviction 'produces total retrieval failure' under the same memory-pressure condition.
cita: Mehraj, Kafeel, and Musa (2026). M.A.K.S: Multidimensional Access Knowledge Scoring for Long-Horizon LLM Agent Memory Management.
notes: S3.1/Table2: memory encoded as structured Memory Units M with content+access_history+CONNECTIONS(memory_id,weight)+entropy_score+fidelity+cached scores -> mem_tipos=TRABAJO (explicitly 'Session-level' scope in the comparison table, managing the fixed-size active context window, S2.5/Table2). representacion=HIBRIDA: text content storage + explicit graph 'connections' array used for the centrality (C) survival-score dimension -> both textual and relational-graph structure. S3.2 survival score S(t)=[F_n x C^beta x H_norm x F_R] x e^(-lambda*t) (temporal decay+frequency+graph-centrality+Shannon-entropy+spaced-reinforcement) determines a THREE-ZONE fidelity function (S3.3): FULL(full content)/PARTIAL(truncated to first 500 chars)/GHOST(truncated to first 100 chars, moved to cold Ghost Store) -> operaciones=WRITE(Memory Unit creation)+CONSOLIDACION(the FULL->PARTIAL->GHOST fidelity transitions ARE progressive content COMPRESSION/truncation, not deletion)+OLVIDO(temporal decay term e^(-lambda*t) 'makes sure that unreactivated memories simply disappear naturally' toward GHOST, though never literally erased -- a soft/reversible forgetting)+ACTUALIZACION(S3.4 Ghost Reconsolidation: matched Ghost memories are restored to PARTIAL fidelity with cached_r reset via a fresh reinforcement boost aᵢ=1.0 before each LLM query). trigger=EVENTO-DETERMINISTA: 'M.A.K.S manages memory decay and consolidation DETERMINISTICALLY via algorithms behind-the-scenes without LLM-level intervention' (S2.2); reconsolidation-check runs automatically 'prior to each LLM invocation' (S3.4). retrieval=GREP-ARCHIVOS: Ghost Store matching is explicit KEYWORD extraction + linear scan/inverted-index over tokenized memory content (S3.4) -- NOT embedding-based ('<2ms for Ghost Stores with 1,000 entries... inverted indices will be used in cases where Ghost Stores have more than 10,000 entries'). mide_lectura=SI: the 'Needle in a Compressed Haystack' experiment directly measures reconsolidation/retrieval success under memory-bottleneck stress (token ratio 4.58x vs FIFO's total failure) -> RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO in F. alcance=SESION (lambda explicitly 'calibrated for session-level memory... a single conversation timescale'). multiagente=NO. fidelidad_procedencia=NO (the mechanism addresses graceful degradation/recall, not content staleness-verification or cross-source consistency). Ablation experiment 'corroborates the inclusion of the Ghost Zone and reconsolidation pipeline in architectural support structures' -> ABLATION; Needle-in-Compressed-Haystack (own synthetic stress test, no external LoCoMo/LongMemEval benchmark used -> benchmarks=NINGUNO) -> BENCHMARK-E2E(controlled M.A.K.S-vs-FIFO comparison); overhead benchmarking shows lazy evaluation gives 9.25x sweep speedup at 5,000 memory units, overhead <1% of LLM inference latency -> MEDICION-COSTO, metricas=EXITO;COSTO-TOKENS;LATENCIA. F_screening was CONSOLIDACION;COSTO; full text confirms both and adds WRITE, RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO.

title: MemForest: An Efficient Agent Memory System with Hierarchical Temporal Indexing
benchmarks: LongMemEval-S; LoCoMo
fallos_mitigaciones: 'Wrong-time retrieval' (S2.3.1): unordered embedding-similarity records do not encode temporal order/predecessor relations, so a query like 'Where did Bob live before moving to Miami?' can retrieve the wrong time point (answering 'Boston' or 'Miami' instead of the correct intermediate 'Davis'); mitigated via MemTree's explicit leaf-order temporal hierarchy. Separately, mutable-profile designs face a 'growing-or-compressing dilemma' (S2.3.2): keeping all evidence makes maintenance cost grow with N, while compression discards intermediate states/transition evidence; mitigated via the persistent/derived-artifact separation with localized per-node dirty-path refresh.
cita: Chen et al. (2026). MemForest: An Efficient Agent Memory System with Hierarchical Temporal Indexing.
notes: S3.1: canonical facts (temporally-anchored, retrieval-ready text + source refs + entity mentions) are the stable write unit -> mem_tipos=EPISODICA(temporal state trajectories/event evidence, e.g. the Bob-residence example)+SEMANTICA(entity/user facts). representacion=HIBRIDA: MemTree is a hierarchical TIME-ORDERED TREE index (S3.2, Fig.4: leaves=time-local evidence, internal nodes=interval summaries, root=coarse recall) PLUS derived node embeddings for retrieval -> both tree/graph-structural and vector. operaciones=WRITE(parallel chunk extraction into canonical facts, S3.1)+CONSOLIDACION('Canonical fact consolidation repairs the semantic fragmentation inherently introduced by' parallel extraction, S3 intro)+ACTUALIZACION(S3.1 'a later update only needs to invalidate and regenerate the derived artifacts whose dependency paths intersect the affected scopes' -- localized per-node dirty-path refresh, Table1 O(log N) critical path). trigger=EVENTO-DETERMINISTA (each new session/chunk arrival deterministically triggers extraction+local MemTree insertion). retrieval=EMBEDDINGS(node embeddings, derived-artifact layer)+RANKING(coarse-to-fine interval-summary browsing, S3.2)+GRAFO(hierarchical tree traversal root->leaf, Fig.3 Tree Browser). mide_lectura=SI: pass@1/pass@8 accuracy on LongMemEval-S/LoCoMo is the paper's central metric (Table/Fig.1b efficiency-accuracy frontier) -> RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO in F. alcance=SESION(session trees preserve per-session chronology)+PROYECTO(entity/scene trees persist across MANY sessions, a user's whole multi-year history, S3.2). multiagente=NO. fidelidad_procedencia=SI: the paper's central concern IS temporal-state consistency/correctness across evolving memory (avoiding 'wrong-time retrieval', preserving historical/transition states rather than a single mutable latest-state summary that silently loses intermediate truth) -> FIDELIDAD in F. Fig.1: MemForest achieves 79.8% pass@1 on LongMemEval-S (best among stateful baselines) while sustaining ~6x higher write throughput than EverMemOS -> BENCHMARK-E2E+MEDICION-COSTO, metricas=EXITO;LATENCIA;COSTO-TOKENS ('avoid unnecessary LLM calls and token usage', S2.4). Section6 dedicated ablation studies of design choices (parallel extraction, MemTree vs flat/mutable alternatives) -> ABLATION. F_screening was RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO;COSTO; full text confirms both and adds WRITE, CONSOLIDACION, FIDELIDAD.

title: Joint Agent Memory and Exploration Learning via Novelty Signals
benchmarks: ScaleWoB (96 web apps, 86 train / 10 held-out test)
fallos_mitigaciones: 'Agent memory lacks reliable step-level supervision: we usually do not know what each memory state should encode... Latent memory is usually more efficient but much harder to supervise, because its compressed vectors lack human-readable semantics' (S1); mitigated via novelty-driven joint training that provides 'natural, annotation-free supervision for the memory module' using deterministic code-coverage signals. Separately, a comparative failure mode: 'local baselines exhibit an early plateau due to premature exploration stagnation... these methods prune their context, inevitably discarding critical historical information as the session progresses' (S4.2), contrasted with JAMEL's non-pruning latent compression that avoids context truncation entirely.
cita: Tian et al. (2026). Joint Agent Memory and Exploration Learning via Novelty Signals.
notes: S3.2/Eq.4-5: each historical (observation,action) pair is compressed by a FROZEN vision-language model into a single latent EOS-token embedding hi; Mt=[h1,...,ht-1] is the full memory state, projected via a learned linear aligner W into the POLICY's embedding space and prepended as a soft prefix -> mem_tipos=TRABAJO(bounded per-episode/session working state, not a persisted cross-session store)+PARAMETRICA(non-textual, opaque continuous vector representation injected directly into the model's embedding space, explicitly contrasted against 'explicit textual memories' which 'are interpretable... can be inspected, revised, or heuristically filtered', S1). representacion=VECTOR (dense embedding tokens, no text/graph/doc storage). operaciones=WRITE ONLY: each step is compressed and appended to the growing sequence Mt, with NO admission/consolidation/forgetting/update -- all latent tokens are retained ('JAMEL aligns with this comprehensive retention strategy by avoiding context truncation. Instead, JAMEL compresses all historical information into latent memory tokens', S4.2). trigger=EVENTO-DETERMINISTA(each interaction step deterministically triggers compression+append, Eq.4). retrieval=NA: there is no selective search/ranking mechanism -- the ENTIRE memory sequence is always prepended wholesale as a soft prefix (Eq.5), exactly analogous to a full-inclusion (non-retrieval) memory design. mide_lectura=SI: the ENTIRE experimental design (Table1 baseline comparison, ablation-like per-app breakdown Fig.3, Case Study S4.3) directly tests whether the memory-conditioned policy successfully USES accumulated history to avoid repeating exhausted behaviors and discover novel states -> RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO in F. alcance=TAREA: memory is scoped to ONE bounded app-exploration session/task (T=50 steps per app), not a persisted cross-day store. multiagente=NO. fidelidad_procedencia=NO. Table1/Fig.2: JAMEL-9B reaches 20.7 avg cumulative reward, competitive with cloud ReAct-vision(20.9) and exceeding ReAct-text(19.9), while clearly beating open-weight MAI-UI-8B(8.4) and Mobile-Agent-v3.5(5.9) -> BENCHMARK-E2E. Table2: JAMEL uses 2.76x/2.81x/17.85x/21.92x FEWER input tokens than Mobile-Agent-v3.5/MAI-UI/ReAct-Text/ReAct-Vision respectively -> COSTO in F, metricas=COSTO-TOKENS, evidencia_tipo=MEDICION-COSTO. S4.3 Case Study: JAMEL's OWN failure mode is explicitly documented -- on Pinduoduo, 'persistent modal overlays' cause 'prolonged plateaus... exceptionally dense interfaces can still challenge the compressed memory representation' -> NEGATIVO(a)-style honest limitation, evidencia_tipo=CUALITATIVA (per-app qualitative pattern analysis, Fig.3, not a controlled with/without-memory ablation). F_screening was COSTO; full text confirms it and adds WRITE, RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO, NEGATIVO.

title: Agent Memory: Characterization and System Implications of Stateful Long-Horizon Workloads
benchmarks: MemoryAgentBench (MAB); MemoryArena; LongMemEval_S_* (within MAB)
fallos_mitigaciones: The paper's central diagnostic finding IS the failure mode: 'these design choices drastically and asymmetrically redistribute cost... These costs are invisible to accuracy metrics, yet critically dominate at deployment scale' (S1) -- e.g. Paradigm III/IV systems shift majority of end-to-end ENERGY into construction (invisible at query time, Fig.3), spanning a 26.7x energy range (BM25 582kJ to Letta 15,429kJ, Table3) that accuracy-only benchmarks completely hide. Mitigation is operational, not architectural: 'we derive 10 system recommendations covering construction scheduling, capability floors, amortization via query volume, freshness-latency tradeoffs, and fleet-scale management' (Abstract). Section4.6 further identifies the freshness-latency tradeoff: when construction lags session arrival, a system must either block queries until writes commit or SERVE STALE memory.
cita: Omri et al. (2026). Agent Memory: Characterization and System Implications of Stateful Long-Horizon Workloads.
notes: This is a pure SYSTEMS-CHARACTERIZATION / profiling paper, not a memory mechanism: 'We present the first systems characterization of agent memory' (Abstract), building 'a system-oriented taxonomy classifying agent memory systems along four axes' and 'a phase-aware profiling harness' to CHARACTERIZE TEN EXISTING systems (long_context, BM25, embedRAG, GraphRAG, HippoRAG v2, Mem0, SimpleMem, A-Mem, Letta, MIRIX, Table1) spanning four paradigms, without proposing its own mechanism -> mem_tipos=NA/representacion=NA/operaciones=NA/trigger=NA (rule5: explains what it MEASURES instead, below). retrieval=NA: characterizes the varied retrieval pipelines of the ten evaluated systems (lexical/dense/graph-expand/PPR-rerank/tool-mediated) rather than proposing its own. mide_lectura=SI: the entire profiling harness measures per-phase (construction/retrieval/generation) latency, token volume, GPU energy, and accuracy across systems (Fig.2-3, Table3) -> RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO mandatory in F (rule3). alcance=SESION (LongMemEval_S_*/MemoryArena multi-session; each sample ~360K tokens history, 60 queries). multiagente=NO (MIRIX 'multi-type routing' across episodic/semantic/procedural/resource stores is NOT multi-agent sharing). fidelidad_procedencia=SI: Section4.6 explicitly studies the 'freshness-latency tradeoff' -- whether a system serves STALE memory when construction lags behind session arrival -- a direct staleness/consistency concern -> FIDELIDAD in F. Fig.2: on LongMemEval_S_*, Mem0 achieves <0.1s/query vs ~38s for long-context (GPT-4.1-mini) while matching/exceeding accuracy -> BENCHMARK-E2E. Table3: end-to-end energy spans 26.7x (BM25 582kJ -> Letta 15,429kJ); normalized J-per-correct-answer spans from BM25's 4,145J floor to MIRIX's 144,629J (a 28-47x premium) -> MEDICION-COSTO, metricas=EXITO;COSTO-TOKENS;LATENCIA. NEGATIVO in F: 'These costs are invisible to accuracy metrics' is itself P5-style negative evidence about how memory systems are currently EVALUATED (accuracy-only benchmarks systematically hide massive, deployment-critical cost disparities). F_screening was COSTO; full text confirms it and adds RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO, FIDELIDAD, NEGATIVO.

title: COMA: Adaptive Context Budget Management for Memory-Augmented RAG via Query-Aware Zone Allocation, Memory-Conditioned Retrieval, and Cognitive Memory Consolidation
benchmarks: Synthetic Multi-Turn Corpus (own, 3 scenarios: standard/memory_heavy/retrieval_heavy, 20 turns/50 docs each); Real Research Corpus (own, 10 canonical NLP papers)
fallos_mitigaciones: 'Existing frameworks treat context assembly as a concatenation problem: rank by relevance, truncate to fit' (Abstract) -- (1) budget partitioning is hardcoded/absent, (2) retrieval is query-only and ignores what the agent already knows, causing token waste on redundant chunks that overlap working memory, (3) memory management (MemGPT/Letta, Mem0, Zep) 'relies on hand-crafted rules for consolidation, eviction, and decay' that cannot adapt; mitigated via the query-aware budget allocator, memory-conditioned MMR-style retriever (Eq.1), and Ebbinghaus-decay consolidation engine respectively. Honest self-reported tradeoff: COMA's groundedness score is LOWER than Naive RAG (0.464 vs 0.687) because 'the judge scores groundedness relative to retrieved chunks only, penalizing answers that draw on working memory items promoted from prior turns' (S6) -- a measurement artifact, not a real quality deficit.
cita: Biswas (2026). COMA: Adaptive Context Budget Management for Memory-Augmented RAG via Query-Aware Zone Allocation, Memory-Conditioned Retrieval, and Cognitive Memory Consolidation.
notes: S3.D: three-tier Atkinson-Shiffrin-inspired architecture -- Tier1 sensory buffer (per-turn staging, ephemeral)+Tier2 WORKING MEMORY (bounded 50-item store)+Tier3 long-term memory (persistent, FAISS-indexed) -> mem_tipos=TRABAJO(explicit 'Working Memory' tier)+EPISODICA(one of the 5 prompt-assembly ZONES is explicitly 'episodic' = prior conversation turns, and long-term store generically holds conversational facts/experiences). representacion=VECTOR (FAISS dense embeddings throughout, no graph/doc-file store). operaciones: WRITE(sensory ingestion)+ADMISION(S3.E 'Extract: items with importance score>=0.3 are promoted' sensory->working -- an explicit write-admission gate)+CONSOLIDACION(named 'Memory Consolidation Engine', S3.E: Consolidate working->long-term + Merge pairwise-cosine-similarity>0.85 dedup of long-term items, 'prevents semantic fragmentation')+OLVIDO(Decay Sweep archives items below Ebbinghaus-retention threshold theta=0.3, Eq.5)+ACTUALIZACION(working-memory eviction priority P(m,t) Eq.4 recomputed with recency/frequency on every access). trigger=PRESUPUESTO(consolidation triggered 'when working memory utilization exceeds 80%', S3.E)+CHECKPOINT(the full consolidation cycle 'runs every N=5 turns', S3.E). retrieval=EMBEDDINGS(FAISS ANN cosine similarity, Stage1)+RANKING(Eq.1 memory-conditioned MMR-style reranking penalizing candidates overlapping working memory, Stage2). mide_lectura=SI: the paper introduces a dedicated MemoryRecall@K metric (Eq.7) plus 3 other custom metrics measuring context-memory read quality -> RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO in F. alcance=SESION (20-turn multi-turn conversational scenarios). multiagente=NO ('multi-agent memory sharing' explicitly listed as future work, not implemented). fidelidad_procedencia=SI: each working-memory item explicitly carries 'source provenance' + a SHA-256 hash index prevents duplicate insertion into long-term memory (S3.D.3) -> FIDELIDAD in F. Table IV/V: COMA achieves 37.1% lower token usage (99,585 vs 158,233 on the real research corpus), 2x higher MemoryRecall@20 (1.000 vs 0.000 for Naive RAG/No-Memory), and 5.4x ContextEfficiency vs Naive RAG -> BENCHMARK-E2E+MEDICION-COSTO, metricas=EXITO;COSTO-TOKENS;LATENCIA. Explicit 3-baseline ablation (Naive RAG/Fixed Allocation/No Memory) isolates each of COMA's 3 components' individual contribution -> ABLATION. F_screening was CONSOLIDACION;COSTO; full text confirms both and adds WRITE, RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO, FIDELIDAD, NEGATIVO.

title: MemRefine: LLM-Guided Compression for Long-Term Agent Memory
benchmarks: LoCoMo; scaled LoCoMo-style (3x, 10x longer conversations, own); LongMemEvalS
fallos_mitigaciones: 'As interactions accumulate, the memory store grows without bound and fills with redundant entries that inflate storage cost and degrade retrieval by crowding out the most useful evidence,' especially acute on resource-constrained/on-device platforms with hard memory budgets (S1); mitigated via storage-budgeted LLM-guided compression that defers delete/merge/preserve decisions to factual judgment rather than surface similarity. Critique of single-criterion baselines: 'two textually similar entries may carry redundant facts that can be removed, complementary facts that should be merged, or distinct facts that both warrant preservation' -- fixed-similarity-threshold (RuleSim) and PageRank-centrality (RulePR) heuristics cannot distinguish these three cases and are empirically shown to underperform the LLM judge (Fig.4).
cita: Kim et al. (2026). MemRefine: LLM-Guided Compression for Long-Term Agent Memory.
notes: S3: MemRefine is explicitly a POST-CONSTRUCTION module inserted 'after memory construction and before retrieval, leaving the host construction and retrieval pipelines unchanged' -- it operates over entries with 'textual content, an embedding vector, and, depending on the host framework, links/timestamps/metadata' (S3.1) drawn from example entries about factual/biographical content (Fig.2: 'Jon has danced since childhood...') -> mem_tipos=SEMANTICA. representacion=HIBRIDA: validated on BOTH an A-MEM-style GRAPH of linked structured notes AND the non-graph Mem0 vector-entry pipeline, explicitly framework-agnostic (S4 'Memory frameworks'). operaciones: NO WRITE (explicitly decoupled from construction: 'all judge and merge calls are issued during memory maintenance rather than at query time... the host construction and retrieval pipelines remain untouched', S3.2 Practical Implications) and NO ADMISION (operates only on EXISTING items, never admits new ones) -> CONSOLIDACION(explicit MERGE action, Algorithm1 line13-17: an LLM synthesizes one entry from two, inheriting union-of-links, recomputed embedding)+OLVIDO(explicit DELETE action, Algorithm1 line10-12, pruning dangling links). trigger=PRESUPUESTO: the entire compression loop is explicitly gated by a fixed storage-budget ratio rho, 'while size(M')>B' (Algorithm1 line1,4) -- textbook budget-triggered maintenance. retrieval=EMBEDDINGS(candidate-pair proposal via all-MiniLM-L6-v2 cosine similarity, S3.2 'Candidate Pair Selection')+RANKING(arg-max most-similar-pair selection loop). mide_lectura=SI: downstream QA F1/EM/accuracy on the COMPRESSED store is the paper's entire evaluation currency (Table1) -> RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO in F. alcance=SESION (LoCoMo/LongMemEvalS multi-session, plus 3x/10x SCALED conversation-length stress tests). multiagente=NO. fidelidad_procedencia=SI: the LLM judge's core function is EXPLICITLY to verify factual consistency/redundancy between memory entries ('decides, based on FACTUAL CONTENT rather than surface wording, whether it should be deleted, merged, or preserved', S1) -- squarely FIDELIDAD ('costuras'/consistency between memory sources, rule7). Table1: MemRefine holds F1 nearly flat under moderate compression on standard LoCoMo (0.40->0.39 A-MEM-graph at 70% budget) while realized storage meets every target budget across both frameworks and 3 benchmark settings -> BENCHMARK-E2E+MEDICION-COSTO(realized-vs-target storage ratio tracked as a result). Fig.4: RuleSim/RulePR rule-based ablation baselines (same candidate-pair loop, heuristic instead of LLM judgment) underperform MemRefine at every budget, isolating the LLM judge's necessity -> ABLATION; Fig.3 category-wise F1-change breakdown is a further controlled analysis. F_screening was CONSOLIDACION;COSTO; full text confirms both and adds RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO, FIDELIDAD.

title: Learning What to Remember: A Cognitively Grounded Multi-Factor Value Model for Agentic Memory
benchmarks: LongMemEval-S; own synthetic confound study (60 train / 60 test cases, 4 gold + 16 distractors each)
fallos_mitigaciones: The paper's central contribution IS exposing a measurement pitfall as the 'failure mode': 'scoring goal relevance against the held-out evaluation question -- an oracle that peeks at the future query -- saturates gold-evidence retention at ~0.98... this measures RETRIEVAL, not FORGETTING' (Abstract/S4.2); a real agent has not seen the evaluation question at consolidation time, so query-defined retention benchmarks cannot, on their own, demonstrate a forgetting advantage. Mitigated via the blind evaluation protocol, where goal relevance is computed only against consolidation-time-available information (session topic), revealing that similarity-only and recency-only policies 'collapse toward the chance floor' (0.286 and 0.368 respectively vs. 0.30 random) while the learned multi-factor value retains 0.770.
cita: Chen and Cheng (2026). Learning What to Remember: A Cognitively Grounded Multi-Factor Value Model for Agentic Memory.
notes: S3.1/Eq.1-2: each memory m (a stored conversational turn) is scored by a learned linear value V(m)=sum(wi*fi(m)) over 7 cognitively-grounded factors (emotional intensity, goal relevance, self/user relevance, reliability populated API-free; value alignment, task utility, usage history held at 0 in these experiments, table1) -> mem_tipos=EPISODICA (memory items are individual conversational turns from LongMemEval-S's multi-session histories, flagged gold-evidence turns). representacion=VECTOR (all-MiniLM-L6-v2 sentence embeddings drive the goal-relevance/self-relevance factors). operaciones=WRITE(S3.2 'Encoding depth: higher-value items are encoded more deeply' into 4 tiers at write time, the PROPOSED framework mechanism)+OLVIDO(Eq.3 explicit forget score = recency x usage x 1/value; 'items with the highest forget score are dropped first when the store exceeds budget' -- this IS the mechanism the paper's own experiment directly tests, S4.2) -- NO ADMISION/CONSOLIDACION/ACTUALIZACION tested or described (the paper explicitly isolates ONLY the budgeted keep/drop decision: 'we do not run an answerer or the full encode/forget/retrieve loop here', S4.2). trigger=PRESUPUESTO: a fixed keep-fraction budget kappa (e.g. 30%) explicitly gates which items are forgotten (Eq.3, S4.2). retrieval=EMBEDDINGS(sentence-transformer cosine similarity for goal/self-relevance factors)+RANKING(V(m) ranks candidates for both the keep/drop decision AND, per S3.2, retrieval rank). mide_lectura=NO: the paper explicitly frames MEASURING RETRIEVAL as the pitfall to avoid -- 'the oracle regime... measures retrieval, not forgetting' -- and its own blind-regime headline metric deliberately isolates the WRITE-time forgetting/retention decision without running any answerer or retrieval step ('we report gold-evidence retention rather than QA accuracy', explicit Limitation L1: 'retention is a proxy for end-task accuracy, not downstream QA correctness'); RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO therefore NOT required in F. alcance=SESION (LongMemEval-S multi-session chat histories, ~500 turns/case). multiagente=NO. fidelidad_procedencia=SI: the 'reliability' factor is explicitly a 'provenance heuristic (user-stated > model-stated)' (Table1) -- a direct provenance/source-trust mechanism -> FIDELIDAD in F. Table3: in the realistic BLIND regime, learned multi-factor value retains 0.770+-0.011 of gold evidence across 479 usable cases vs 0.657(uniform)/0.518(best single factor, self-relevance)/0.368(recency)/0.286(goal-only, near the 0.30 chance floor) -- every per-case bootstrap gap's 95% CI excludes zero -> BENCHMARK-E2E. Section4.1 synthetic confound study (planted value-alignment/self-relevance confounds) shows the gradient-free learner recovers 1.00 retention vs uniform-weighting's 0.62 and all single-factor baselines' 0.00 -> ABLATION; Section4.2's linear-vs-MLP nonlinear-value ablation shows a statistical TIE (+0.003, 55% of splits) -> further ABLATION. NEGATIVO in F: the near-chance-floor collapse of similarity/recency-only policies under realistic (blind) conditions is direct P5-style negative evidence that today's dominant single-factor production memory policies are fundamentally MIS-SPECIFIED for the forgetting decision. F_screening was CONSOLIDACION;COSTO; full text does NOT support either (no true multi-item merge/consolidation operation is tested, and no $/token cost is measured -- CPU-only/no-API-calls is a qualitative design property, not a measured cost outcome) so BOTH are DROPPED, and WRITE, FIDELIDAD, NEGATIVO are added.

title: G-Long: Graph-Enhanced Memory Management for Efficient Long-Term Dialogue Agents
benchmarks: MSC, CC, LoCoMo, LongMemEval (LME)
fallos_mitigaciones: 2-hop subgraph traversal through high-degree hub nodes (e.g. 'User') introduces 'Semantic Drift' noise into retrieval; mitigated by restricting expansion to L=1 hop (Table 7, sensitivity analysis, §4.7.1).
cita: Choi et al. (2026). G-Long: Graph-Enhanced Memory Management for Efficient Long-Term Dialogue Agents.
notes: mem_tipos EPISODICA;SEMANTICA: persona-driven triplets from dialogue events+persona attributes via PersonaExt (§3.2). representacion GRAFO;VECTOR: 'dual-storage strategy...dense vector indexing for entity nodes and attribute-rich edge storage' (§3.3). operaciones=WRITE only (triplet extraction per utterance, §3.2); trigger EVENTO-DETERMINISTA (extraction runs for each utterance). retrieval EMBEDDINGS;GRAFO;RANKING: anchor-node cosine similarity + 1-hop subgraph expansion + two-stage hybrid rerank Sfinal (§3.4, Eq.4). mide_lectura=SI: Recall@3/5, Accuracy@3/5 on LME (Table 4/5, +40.8% recall vs LD-Agent). benchmarks MSC/CC/LoCoMo/LME (§4.1.1). metricas OTRA (BLEU/ROUGE/G-Eval/Recall/MRR) + COSTO-TOKENS ($1.56 vs $7.61 = 4.9x cheaper, 63.0% token reduction vs Long-Context, Table 6). handoff=CONTENIDO: graph triplets persist across dialogue sessions and are injected as context (MLong) into future-session prompts (§3.5). alcance=SESION (multi-session MSC/CC/LoCoMo).

title: CoreMem: Riemannian Retrieval and Fisher-Guided Distillation for Long-Term Memory in Dialogue Agents
benchmarks: LOCOMO, LongMemEval-S, LongMemEval-M
fallos_mitigaciones: Isotropic cosine retrieval suffers hubness (a few 'hub' memories dominate nearest-neighbor lists, drowning peripheral facts), mitigated by a locally adaptive Fisher-Rao/Mahalanobis metric (§3.2). Naive global token-dropping shatters syntax; mitigated by hierarchical sentence-level distillation + structural protection masks (§3.3-3.4, ablated in Table 5).
cita: Chen et al. (2026). CoreMem: Riemannian Retrieval and Fisher-Guided Distillation for Long-Term Memory in Dialogue Agents.
notes: mem_tipos EPISODICA: 'historical memory set M' of past dialogue turns in an edge-cloud pipeline (§3.1). representacion VECTOR: dense embeddings in a local vector store memory bank (Fig.1, 'Knowledge and Memory'). operaciones=WRITE (embeddings added to bank, no explicit consolidation/eviction of the store itself); trigger EVENTO-DETERMINISTA (implicit per-turn embedding, no explicit admission gate). retrieval EMBEDDINGS;RANKING: Riemannian Fisher-Rao/Mahalanobis retrieval + residual cosine-Riemannian fusion score (§3.2, Eq.2, alpha=0.5). mide_lectura=SI: Hit@k retrieval accuracy (Table 2, H@10 0.532) and structural ablation H@1/H@10 (Table 5). metricas OTRA (ROUGE-L, LLM-Judge accuracy, Hit@k) + COSTO-TOKENS (PTok prompt-token counts Table 2/3; FDTD compresses prompts 20-30%, abstract) + LATENCIA (Time(s) wall-clock, Table 2/3). evidencia_tipo ABLATION (Table 5 structural ablation; embedding-model ablation §5.1) + BENCHMARK-E2E (Table 2/3) + MEDICION-COSTO (8GB VRAM ceiling profiling §5.6; ~20% API cost reduction, Fig.1 caption). handoff=CONTENIDO: the compressed distilled context X-tilde transmitted to the cloud LLM carries facts forward across the ongoing multi-session history. alcance=SESION (multi-session dialogue, 'dozens of sessions').

title: Learning What Not to Forget: Long-Horizon Agent Memory from a Few Kilobytes of Learning
benchmarks: AppWorld, LoCoMo, LongMemEvalS
fallos_mitigaciones: Naive FIFO/recency eviction drops load-bearing state (e.g. an auth token or a path a later step needs), causing agents to loop or fail (Fig.1-2). LLM-based compression (ACON) paraphrases and loses exact identifiers, also causing loops. Both mitigated by LRE's verbatim, query-blind, learned-relevance retention (§5.1-5.2: 14 tasks solved only by LRE, Table 10/11).
cita: Lia and Mazumder (2026). Learning What Not to Forget: Long-Horizon Agent Memory from a Few Kilobytes of Learning.
notes: mem_tipos TRABAJO;EPISODICA: in-context history units are dialogue turns or agent action-observation steps managed under a token/unit budget (§3.1), i.e. working-memory/context eviction over episodic content, not a persisted long-term store. representacion DOCS-ARCHIVOS: units are kept 'verbatim' as plain text (§3.1, 'nothing is summarized or rewritten'); the feature vector phi(ui) is only a scoring signal, not the stored representation. operaciones=OLVIDO: the paper's entire contribution is a proactive eviction policy (title: 'Learning What Not to Forget'; §1,§3). trigger=PRESUPUESTO: eviction is bound by an explicit token/unit budget B (Eq.1, Table 1: 2048 tokens for agents, unit-count cap for conversation). retrieval=NA: the paper explicitly contrasts eviction from retrieval ('Eviction is different from retrieval...it must decide what to keep before the query...exists', §1) -- LRE is query-blind and does not perform query-time search over stored memory. mide_lectura=SI (correction vs F_screening 'CONSOLIDACION;COSTO': adding RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO to F per rule 3, since the paper explicitly measures read/selection quality): macro-AUC ranking of gold-evidence turns (Table 3, 0.829 LoCoMo, 'A query-blind scorer that rivals dense retrievers') and gold-recall-vs-retention-budget curves (Fig.6, §5.4). alcance=TAREA;SESION (AppWorld agent task-level; LoCoMo/LongMemEvalS conversational session-level). multiagente=NO (explicit limitation: 'not on...collaborative multi-agent systems', §7 Limitations). fidelidad_procedencia=NO: the paper's own use of 'fidelity' (abstract: 'eviction...is a fidelity problem') refers to verbatim-extraction exactness of load-bearing content, not provenance/staleness verification of sources. metricas EXITO (Task Goal Completion %, Table 2) + ITERACION (mean trajectory steps Stp, Table 2) + COSTO-TOKENS (peak tokens Pk; 68% fewer tokens on LoCoMo, §5.4) + OTRA (macro-AUC, gold recall). evidencia_tipo ABLATION (Table 4: self-supervised vs supervised label recovery) + BENCHMARK-E2E (Table 2/3: AppWorld, LoCoMo, LongMemEvalS) + MEDICION-COSTO (Table 13: scores 1,181 units/s vs 103/36 for dense-encoder/LLM-pruner baselines, 11.5x/32.8x faster, CPU-only, ~1.7KB scorer). handoff=CONTENIDO: the verbatim-retained units are precisely what persists/carries forward across the growing multi-session/multi-step history (Fig.2).

title: Are We Ready For An Agent-Native Memory System?
benchmarks: LoCoMo, LongMemEval (via MemoryAgentBench), DB-Bench (via LifelongAgentBench)
fallos_mitigaciones: Append-only memory stores show catastrophic degradation as evidence grows more distant, and systems lacking lifecycle management return stale facts under conflicting updates ('hallucinations of the past', O3/O4, §1). Own finding/mitigation: 'conservative memory consolidation serves as the best default maintenance strategy, whereas delayed flushing creates a deceptive trade-off between surface-level coverage and actual answerability' (O6).
cita: Zhou et al. (2026). Are We Ready For An Agent-Native Memory System?
notes: Paper de MEDICION/benchmark puro (evalua 12 sistemas de memoria representativos + 2 baselines, sin proponer mecanismo propio) => mem_tipos=NA por regla 5; mide en su lugar una taxonomia de 4 modulos (R representacion/storage, S extraccion, Q retrieval/routing, U maintenance, §2) aplicada a sistemas EXISTENTES (Mem0, Zep, MemGPT/Letta, A-MEM, MemTree, Cognee, LightMem, SimpleMem, MemOS, MemoryOS, MemoChat, MEM1, MemAgent -- Table 1, §3), evaluados end-to-end sobre 5 research questions (§4). representacion/operaciones/trigger/retrieval=NA por la misma razon: no hay sistema propio (Table 1 documenta que las 12 systems abarcan Token-Sequence/Graph-Tree/Heterogeneous-Composite representation x extraction schema-free/constrained x retrieval attention/semantic/subgraph/agentic/hybrid x maintenance versioning/eviction/consolidation, sin que el paper adopte ninguna combinacion como propia). mide_lectura=SI: RQ2 'retrieval fidelity' medido explicitamente por sistema (§4, O2: 'retrieval accuracy degrades significantly as the temporal distance...increases'). fidelidad_procedencia=SI: RQ3 'dynamic update robustness under conflicting knowledge' -- sistemas sin gestion de ciclo de vida 'return stale facts, leading to hallucinations of the past' (O3, abstract). alcance=NA: meta-estudio, no define un scope propio (evalua sistemas de alcance heterogeneo: TAREA en DB-Bench, SESION en LoCoMo/LongMemEval). benchmarks: LoCoMo, LongMemEval (accedido via MemoryAgentBench), DB-Bench (via LifelongAgentBench) -- ver lineas 1466-1476 (5 workloads/11 datasets en total, solo 3 nombrados explicitamente en el extracto leido). metricas EXITO (task success F1/EM, explicitamente llamado 'task success metrics' en el Abstract) + OTRA (ROUGE-L, LLM-Judge Accuracy, retrieval precision) + LATENCIA (RQ5: 'index construction time and query latency', O5). evidencia_tipo ABLATION (§5: experimentos controlados variando un modulo a la vez) + BENCHMARK-E2E (§4: 12 sistemas x 5 workloads/11 datasets) + MEDICION-COSTO (RQ5 dedicado a costo operacional). handoff=NO: no se estudia un protocolo explicito de traspaso entre sesiones/agentes, solo representacion/retrieval/maintenance.

title: Routing Memory A Tiered, Vector-Quantized Memory System for Long-Lived Language-Model Agents
benchmarks: MS-MARCO
fallos_mitigaciones: Domain/distribution drift of the embedding stream degrades routing quality; mitigated via rolling quantization-error monitoring (alarm at 1.3x baseline) triggering codebook refit (§2.5, H5: recall recovers to 0.92 from a 5K-item domain shift, pre-shift 0.952). Hierarchical routing trades recall for bounded latency; the residual recall gap (up to -9pp at N=1M) is localized to fine-bucket assignment (Table 5) and left unresolved as future work (§5).
cita: Sertel (2026). Routing Memory: A Tiered, Vector-Quantized Memory System for Long-Lived Language-Model Agents.
notes: Sistema de indexado agnostico al contenido: opera sobre 'items' de texto embebidos genericos via K-means codebook/IVF (§2.1), sin distinguir tipo de memoria episodica/semantica/etc. => mem_tipos=NA. representacion=VECTOR: embeddings densos indexados via IVF (§2.1-2.3). operaciones/trigger=NA: el paper asume un corpus D ya dado (Let D={(ti,ei)}) y no describe mecanismo propio de escritura/admision/consolidacion/olvido de contenido; 'drift detection' (§2.5) es shift estadistico de la distribucion de embeddings/queries, no staleness de contenido. retrieval EMBEDDINGS;RANKING: multi-probe IVF sobre centroides + rerank por dot-product (§2.2) + score-based filtering por umbral tau (§2.4). mide_lectura=SI: R@5/recall@10/purity medidos extensamente (Tabla 1-3, H1-H2, Table 2 MS-MARCO). alcance=NA: infraestructura generica para 'long-lived agents' sin delimitar explicitamente tarea/sesion/proyecto/organizacion (§4.4). fidelidad_procedencia=NO: el 'drift detection' es deteccion de shift de distribucion estadistica, no verificacion de procedencia/staleness de contenido (distincion explicita de rule 7). benchmarks MS-MARCO (§3.3, validacion con encoder real all-MiniLM-L6-v2). metricas OTRA (R@5, recall@10, purity) + LATENCIA (p50/p95/p99 extensivamente reportado, Tablas 1-4) + COSTO-TOKENS (H3: tau=0.6 descarta 31.8% de tokens perdiendo solo 0.9% de recall, §3.1). evidencia_tipo ABLATION (K-sweep, umbral de filtrado, flat-vs-jerarquico, SQLite-vs-mmap: Tablas 3-5) + BENCHMARK-E2E (MS-MARCO con encoder real, Tabla 2) + MEDICION-COSTO (RAM RSS medido, latencia, Tablas 1-4). handoff=NO: arquitectura de indice de recuperacion; no describe un protocolo explicito de traspaso de memoria entre sesiones o agentes (aunque menciona agentes 'long-lived' que acumulan memoria, §4.4).

title: EMA: An Episodic Memory Agent for Efficient and Selective Memory
benchmarks: Locomo, Long-MT-Bench+
fallos_mitigaciones: 'Unfiltered memory degrades performance': naive RAG / long-context methods that feed full histories without filtering suffer redundancy and performance drops under edge-device constraints (§4.2). Mitigated by MemDecider, an importance-based admission filter (ablation Table 3: 'All-Accept'/'Random' both degrade performance vs EMA).
cita: Lan et al. (2026). EMA: An Episodic Memory Agent for Efficient and Selective Memory.
notes: mem_tipos=EPISODICA: EMUs (Episodic Memory Units) explicitly modeled on human episodic memory (Tulving, §2), fields id/tau/P/phi/C/s/c/L/x. representacion=HIBRIDA: EMU = structured record (metadata+summary+original content) + semantic embeddings + a link-graph across EMUs ('Memory Linking...forms a structured memory network', §3.3, Fig.2). operaciones=WRITE;ADMISION;CONSOLIDACION;ACTUALIZACION: MemDecider is explicitly an admission gate ('filters memory admission based on information importance', contribution bullet, §3.2); Memory Manager writes/constructs EMUs (WRITE); Self-Update revises stale EMUs (ACTUALIZACION, explicit example: a canceled plan updates the corresponding EMU, §3.3); EMUs Reorganization runs periodic 'global re-embedding and consolidation' (CONSOLIDACION, §3.3). trigger=EVENTO-DETERMINISTA;CHECKPOINT: MemDecider scores every incoming dialogue turn (event-based); reorganization fires 'once the frequency of Memory Linking and Self-Update operations reaches a predefined threshold' (count-based checkpoint, §3.3). retrieval=EMBEDDINGS;RANKING: Caller does NER-augmented query encoding then embedding top-k match against EMU label+summary+links (§3.4). mide_lectura=SI (matches F_screening). fidelidad_procedencia=SI: Self-Update explicitly handles staleness (example: a plan mentioned then canceled triggers an EMU update, §3.3). F changed vs F_screening ('RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO;COSTO'): added WRITE because MemDecider (the admission/write-gate module) is central and directly ablated (Table 3). benchmarks Locomo, Long-MT-Bench+ (§4.1, §4.3). metricas OTRA (F1, BLEU, EM) + COSTO-TOKENS (Token Cost columns, Tables 1-2; MemDecider reduces token consumption by 11.48% on average, §4.2). evidencia_tipo ABLATION (Table 3: MemDecider All-Accept/Random, Caller w/o NER/w/o Link) + BENCHMARK-E2E (Tables 1-2, Locomo/Long-MT-Bench+) + MEDICION-COSTO (token-consumption reduction, Tables 1-3). handoff=CONTENIDO: Fig.1's worked example shows a fact mentioned 'on Monday' explicitly retrieved and referenced in a later turn ('Considering what we discussed on Monday...').

title: Experience Graphs: The Data Foundation for Self-Improving Agents
benchmarks: KernelEvolve (production accelerator-kernel optimizer, Meta, internal controlled study)
fallos_mitigaciones: Buggy nodes trigger expensive debug-retry loops; cross-session memory reuse cuts the buggy-node fraction from 55% to 34% (p=0.1) / 21% (p=0.5), driving the 52% token-cost saving (§6). But higher injection anchors the search (p=0.5 collapses to 8 strategy combinations vs 20 cold-start, and the single best solution comes from no-memory, 1.49x vs 1.36x) -- an open exploration-anchoring tradeoff (§7).
cita: Liao et al. (2026). Experience Graphs: The Data Foundation for Self-Improving Agents.
notes: mem_tipos: the paper unifies 3 existing knowledge tiers (declarative=SEMANTICA via CLAUDE.md/MEMORY.md, procedural=PROCEDIMENTAL via skills, episodic=EPISODICA via session transcripts, §3) plus an orthogonal 4th tier, the 'experience graph' (causal tree of attempts with rewards, Table 1) which does not map 1:1 to the closed vocabulary; annotated as additional EPISODICA (records of past attempts with timestamps/lineage). representacion=GRAFO;VECTOR: 'tree/DAG: nodes with parent links, rewards, siblings' (Table 1) + task-description embeddings for cross-session vector similarity (§4, under a 4-table relational schema with Cypher over foreign keys). operaciones=WRITE;ACTUALIZACION: 'Writes are a mix of appends (new nodes) and localized path updates (MCTS backpropagation walks the ancestor chain to update visit counts and cumulative rewards)' (§3). trigger=EVENTO-DETERMINISTA: each outer-loop step persists its result after each inner-loop invocation (§2). retrieval=GRAFO;EMBEDDINGS;RANKING: 'Reuse: Find similar prior tasks via vector search, then retrieve their high-fitness subtrees via graph traversal' (Table 2) + frontier selection ordered by fitness/UCB. mide_lectura=SI: §6 measures the effect of injecting prior memory (cross-session reuse probability p) on convergence speed/cost/failures (Fig.3). alcance=PROYECTO;ORGANIZACION: 'Collectivity' is an explicit substrate requirement -- 'a proven playbook should be reusable organization-wide'; 'governed cloud store, cross-user, cross-session' (Table 1). multiagente=SI: contribution 1 explicitly extends to 'multi-agent scientific societies' + a dedicated 'Concurrent multi-agent search' subsection (atomic backprop across workers, §5). fidelidad_procedencia=SI: 'Time travel: CDC changelog -> AS-OF reconstruction at any step' + 'Audit: Trace which prior attempts...influenced a given decision' (Table 1/2); governance inherits access policy from source episodes (§3). F=RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO;COSTO;MULTIAGENTE (MULTIAGENTE added vs F_screening for the dedicated architectural treatment, though not empirically benchmarked in the KernelEvolve controlled study). handoff=PUNTEROS;CONTENIDO;CONTRATO: 'a child node either inherit its parent's session as a cheap resume [PUNTEROS via session_id/parent_id] or reconstruct context from the graph' [CONTENIDO]; Tasks define 'specification, target environment, and success metric' [CONTRATO] received by each session (§4). plan_estado=SI: 'Sessions record who is searching, with which algorithm, and how far they have gotten' (§4, search progress as memory content).

title: SWE-MeM: Learning Adaptive Memory Management for Long-Horizon Coding Agents
benchmarks: SWE-Bench Verified, SWE-Bench Multilingual, SWE-Bench Pro
fallos_mitigaciones: Fixed compression rules cannot adapt to the heterogeneous value of information (code inspected early may remain essential later; verbose logs can be compressed anytime), Fig.1(a)(b); mitigated by proactive, flexible, agent-decided compression based on trajectory state (§1-2.1). Training-data quality filters guard against defects: inappropriate reduction ratio (>80% or <20%), overly short compression ranges, range misalignment (§2.2.2).
cita: Gao et al. (2026). SWE-MeM: Learning Adaptive Memory Management for Long-Horizon Coding Agents.
notes: mem_tipos=TRABAJO: manages the interaction-history/context of a single repair trajectory under a token budget (§2.1, Eq.1), not memory persisted across tasks. representacion=DOCS-ARCHIVOS: memory entries {c}(summary) and {f}(remaining_work) are plain text inserted into the trajectory (Eq.2), no vector/graph. operaciones=WRITE;CONSOLIDACION: the compress() tool replaces a raw span with a higher-level summary (§2.1, analogous to Semantic Consolidation). trigger=DISCRECIONAL-LLM;PRESUPUESTO: the agent proactively decides when/what/how to compress based on trajectory state (central contribution) + a probabilistic scheduler activated when context budget drops below 20%, reaching 1 at 5% remaining (§2.2.1). retrieval=NA: no external-store retrieval mechanism; compressed content stays inline in context. mide_lectura=NO (matches F_screening, no RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO). alcance=TAREA: memory management scoped to a single repository-repair task (SWE-Bench). fidelidad_procedencia=NO. benchmarks=SWE-Bench Verified, SWE-Bench Multilingual, SWE-Bench Pro (§3.1, §4.3). metricas=EXITO(resolve rate, Table1/3)+COSTO-TOKENS(Token Usage, Table2)+ITERACION(Average Step, Table2). evidencia_tipo=ABLATION(Fig.4: proactive-vs-threshold, selective-vs-full-summarization, curriculum SFT, memory-aware GRPO, memory-tool removal)+BENCHMARK-E2E(Table1/3)+MEDICION-COSTO(Table2: relative token/step usage). F=CONSOLIDACION;COSTO (matches F_screening, confirmed). handoff=NO: intra-trajectory/intra-task memory management, does not cross sessions or agents (remaining_work propagates WITHIN the same trajectory, §2.1). plan_estado=SI: 'remaining_work f records the remaining subtasks and is appended to the end of the trajectory to maintain task continuity' (§2.1) -- exactly plan/progress state as memory content.

title: Mandol: An Agglomerative Agent Memory System for Long-Term Conversations
benchmarks: LoCoMo, LongMemEval
fallos_mitigaciones: Intra-source noise (long-tail relevance-score distribution) mitigated via a dynamic MAD-based threshold (Eq.1, §3.3.2). Cross-source conflicts/staleness (an outdated preference like 'likes coffee' vs. fresher evidence) mitigated by an arbitration score weighing relevance+temporal freshness+source confidence (Eq.2, Beijing-trip example, §3.3.2).
cita: Zhang et al. (2026). Mandol: An Agglomerative Agent Memory System for Long-Term Conversations.
notes: mem_tipos=EPISODICA;SEMANTICA: the abstract layer agglomerates 'episodic memory (event chains), semantic memory (entity graphs), and emotional memory (user preferences)' (§3.1.2); 'emotional memory' (preferences) has no dedicated token in the closed vocabulary and is mapped to SEMANTICA (abstracted user facts) for lack of a better fit. representacion=HIBRIDA: 'SemanticMap and SemanticGraph, which natively fuses key-value, vector, and graph structures' (§3.2, Fig.2) -- unifies KV+vector+graph in one in-memory structure. operaciones=WRITE;CONSOLIDACION;ACTUALIZACION: memory-unit creation (CRUD API, §3.2); the abstract layer agglomerates basic memories via LLM (CONSOLIDACION, §3.1.2); state-update edges track preference evolution (e.g. 'Wangfujing Hotel' -> 'hutong homestay', ACTUALIZACION, §3.1.2). trigger=DISCRECIONAL-LLM;EVENTO-DETERMINISTA: the abstract layer 'leverages an LLM to agglomerate compact abstract memories' (§3.1.2); the basic layer writes each dialogue turn (event). retrieval=GREP-ARCHIVOS;EMBEDDINGS;GRAFO;RANKING: hybrid recall runs BM25+SPLADE+dense vector in parallel, fused via reciprocal rank fusion, subgraph expansion for multi-hop, cross-encoder rerank (§3.3.1). mide_lectura=SI (matches F_screening): retrieval accuracy reported in Table3/4 (LoCoMo 92.21%, LongMemEval 88.40%). alcance=SESION: cross-session memory is explicitly central ('cross-session, multi-typed information', Abstract). fidelidad_procedencia=SI: conflict resolution weighs 'temporal freshness' and 'source confidence', discards 'stale or redundant alternatives' (Eq.2, §3.3.2); traceable links 'source_unit_uids...allows the system to verify abstract evidence' (§3.1.2). F=RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO;COSTO;FIDELIDAD (FIDELIDAD added vs F_screening for the dedicated staleness/conflict-resolution design pillar, §3.3.2). benchmarks=LoCoMo, LongMemEval (§5.1, Table3/4). metricas=OTRA(accuracy Table3/4)+COSTO-TOKENS('Avg. Tok.' column, Table3/4)+LATENCIA(5.4x retrieval speedup, 4.8x insertion speedup at 10 QPS, §1/§5.3). evidencia_tipo=BENCHMARK-E2E(Table3/4)+MEDICION-COSTO(latency and RAM/GPU utilization, §5.3-5.4) -- no explicit ablation section was found in the reviewed text. handoff=CONTENIDO: linked events/facts persist and are retrieved across sessions (Mike's Beijing-trip example linking sessions, §3.1.2). plan_estado=NO.

title: ContextSniper: AntTrail's Token-Efficient Code Memory for Repository-Level Program Repair
benchmarks: SWE-bench Lite (matched 50-task-per-condition comparison); a separate unnamed 5-task comparison
fallos_mitigaciones: The 'read-try-fail-reread' loop: a failed patch attempt triggers another whole-file read or broad search, spending tokens without necessarily finding the missing evidence (§1.1); mitigated by 'retrieve broadly, expose narrowly' plus two-phase synchronization that prevents stale reads after edits (§3.1, §3.3).
cita: Luk et al. (2026). ContextSniper: AntTrail's Token-Efficient Code Memory for Repository-Level Program Repair.
notes: mem_tipos=TRABAJO;EPISODICA: local memory scoped to the current repair task ('task-time local code memory...built from the current repository snapshot, queried during the current repair run', §2.2), explicitly NOT cross-task memory ('leaving room for future integration with cross-task experience memory'). representacion=HIBRIDA: AGFS hierarchy L0(abstract text)/L1(structured metadata: paths, symbols, graph relations, BM25 docs)/L2(source chunks with embeddings) -- fuses DOCS-ARCHIVOS+GRAFO+VECTOR (§3.2, Fig.3). operaciones=WRITE;ADMISION;ACTUALIZACION: memory-node creation (WRITE); an 'intention-aware context gate' filters what enters the prompt (ADMISION, §3.5); two-phase memory-repository synchronization after each agent action keeps code memory aligned with edits (ACTUALIZACION, §3.3). trigger=EVENTO-DETERMINISTA: 'The first phase runs after agent actions through runtime hooks' (§3.3, each action triggers recording). retrieval=EMBEDDINGS;GREP-ARCHIVOS;GRAFO;RANKING: 'adaptive top-k retrieval that fuses semantic embeddings, BM25 lexical scoring, ctags-style symbolic metadata...and graph relations through weighted reciprocal rank fusion (RRF), with a ripgrep-based text-search fallback' (Contributions, §1.3). mide_lectura=SI (matches F_screening): retrieved-evidence quality validated indirectly via resolution rates 'essentially unchanged' despite -51.5%/-38.9% tokens (Abstract, Fig.1C). alcance=TAREA: local memory for a single repair run, explicitly not cross-task. fidelidad_procedencia=SI: 'preserve provenance so the host agent can inspect and edit the source'; synchronization treats memory freshness as part of source grounding ('If retrieval returns an old version of a function after an edit, the compact context becomes actively harmful', §3.3). F=RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO;COSTO;FIDELIDAD (FIDELIDAD added vs F_screening for the dedicated synchronization/staleness mechanism, §3.3). metricas=COSTO-TOKENS(-51.5%/-38.9% total token use, -36.4%/-27.3% logged cost, Abstract)+EXITO(resolution rates 'essentially unchanged'). evidencia_tipo=BENCHMARK-E2E(matched SWE-bench Lite comparison, Fig.1C)+MEDICION-COSTO(token/cost reduction) -- no explicit ablation section found. handoff=NO: local memory for a single task run, no explicit cross-session/cross-agent handoff protocol. plan_estado=NO.

title: Egress-Bounded Retrieval: A Privacy-Preserving Enterprise Memory Architecture with No External Model in the Retrieval Path
benchmarks: NINGUNO
fallos_mitigaciones: (1) Corpus content egress to a third-party model provider on every query = GDPR compliance risk, mitigated by the egress-bounded invariant (100% local retrieval, §3-4). (2) Aggressive key-sentence-extraction compression destroys 37.8% of tagged facts across the 41 test passages (41/41 lose >=1 fact), 'disqualifying' for enterprise use; mitigated by SEETR (only 1/41 passages loses a fact, §6.2). (3) Honest, unmitigated limitation: the paper's own retrieval-quality benchmark uses hash-based embeddings and therefore proves nothing about semantic-retrieval quality under the egress bound (§6.3, §7 item 1).
cita: Biancheri (2026). Egress-Bounded Retrieval: A Privacy-Preserving Enterprise Memory Architecture with No External Model in the Retrieval Path.
notes: mem_tipos=SEMANTICA: declarative enterprise knowledge -- organisation documents, people and decisions, organized via standard ontologies (Org/schema.org/ArchiMate, §4.1), no per-session episodic dialogue component. representacion=HIBRIDA: 'Text, vectors and the relationship graph share a single PostgreSQL instance' (Abstract, §4.2) -- fuses DOCS-ARCHIVOS+VECTOR+GRAFO. operaciones=WRITE;CONSOLIDACION;ACTUALIZACION: ingestion/chunking/embedding (WRITE, §4.2); self-tuning Tier1-3 detects 'near-duplicates...candidate cross-team links, likely mis-filings' and applies reversible 'merges, re-classification' (CONSOLIDACION, §4.4); trust score decays over time without deletion (soft ACTUALIZACION, §4.2: 'stale material recedes without being deleted'). trigger=EVENTO-DETERMINISTA: ingestion triggered by file arrival; self-tuning Tier2 triggered by real usage patterns (§4.4). retrieval=GREP-ARCHIVOS;EMBEDDINGS;GRAFO;RANKING: 5 parallel strategies -- structured lookup, multilingual full-text, dense semantic, people-to-artifact graph traversal, thematic summaries -- merged and re-ranked by a local cross-encoder (§4.3). mide_lectura=SI (correction vs F_screening 'COSTO' alone; RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO added to F per rule 3): NDCG@10/Recall@5/Recall@10/MRR table in §6.3, though the paper itself honestly discloses the harness uses hash embeddings (not a real encoder) and therefore does NOT establish semantic-retrieval quality -- 'This benchmark does not evaluate semantic retrieval' (§6.3), it only verifies the fusion pipeline is wired correctly. alcance=ORGANIZACION: 'One customer, one tenant; every query scoped and access-controlled' (§4.1), multi-tenant enterprise-wide system with RBAC. fidelidad_procedencia=SI: explicit time-decaying trust score per content type (§4.2, §4.4); source attribution as a scoring criterion in the planned agentic-baseline comparison (§6.4). F=COSTO;RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO;FIDELIDAD (two additions vs F_screening='COSTO': RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO for §6.3, FIDELIDAD for trust-decay/provenance as a first-class design pillar). benchmarks=NINGUNO: no established academic benchmark used (BEIR is mentioned but dismissed as unsuitable, §2); the paper builds its own ad-hoc corpora (511 production documents; 41 passages/627 facts for SEETR §6.2; 54 documents/25 queries for the retrieval harness §6.3). metricas=LATENCIA(p50/p95/p99 tables §6.1, HNSW 430x faster than JSONB fallback at 10K)+COSTO-TOKENS(SEETR: 12.8% savings retaining 99.8% of facts vs. 39.6% savings destroying 37.8% of facts with key-sentence, §6.2)+OTRA(NDCG@10, Recall@5/10, MRR, §6.3). evidencia_tipo=BENCHMARK-E2E(§6.3 retrieval harness, with explicit validity caveats)+MEDICION-COSTO(latency §6.1, compression/tokens §6.2) -- the paper itself states in Limitations that there is NO measured ablation ('Re-ranking is the quality bottleneck...This is an observation, not a measured ablation', §7 item 3). handoff=NO: enterprise memory for human users via an assistant, not context handoff between LLM-agent sessions/agents. plan_estado=NO.

title: Memory Management and Contextual Consistency for Long-Running Low-Code Agents
benchmarks: NINGUNO
fallos_mitigaciones: 'Memory Inflation' and 'Contextual Degradation' (older critical info pushed out of the context window, 'stateless'/incoherent behavior, contradicting prior decisions) and 'self-degradation' of the naive 'All-Add' strategy due to 'catastrophic interference' (§1.2, §2.3, Fig.2); mitigated by the 'Intelligent Decay' mechanism (utility-based selective pruning/consolidation) plus HITL user pin/forget intervention (§3.2-4).
cita: Xu (2025). Memory Management and Contextual Consistency for Long-Running Low-Code Agents.
notes: RECONSIDERAR: Appendix A reveals that the Figure 2 data (the 'All-Add' vs 'Hybrid System' comparison over 500 turns) is generated by a Python script with HAND-CODED exponential-decay/logistic-drift formulas, with ranges explicitly 'clamped...for realistic visualization' -- NOT derived from real LLM-agent executions. §5.1 itself admits 'Through simulated long-running task experiments' and 'We conducted a series of simulated experiments', without specifying which LLM (if any) actually produced Table 1. Given the appendix evidence, the paper's empirical rigor is doubtful (possibly post-hoc invented data to illustrate the narrative); values are extracted AS THE PAPER PRESENTS THEM but flagged for human review. mem_tipos=TRABAJO;EPISODICA;SEMANTICA: explicit 3-component architecture -- 'Working Memory (WM)' (TRABAJO), 'Episodic Memory (EM)' a vector-DB of timestamped MemoryEntry (EPISODICA), 'Semantic Memory (SM)' of distilled abstract concepts/summaries (SEMANTICA) (§3.1). representacion=VECTOR: Episodic Memory is concretely implemented as a vector database with dense embeddings (§3.1); Semantic Memory is described with hedged/non-committal language ('potentially implemented as a fact collection or knowledge graph') and is therefore not confidently labeled. operaciones=WRITE;CONSOLIDACION;OLVIDO: MemoryEntry creation (WRITE); Algorithm 1 'ConsolidateToSemanticMemory(Mi)' via LLM summary (CONSOLIDACION, §3.3); explicit 'EpisodicMemory.Delete(Mi)' for low-utility entries (OLVIDO, Algorithm 1). trigger=PRESUPUESTO: decay decision by utility-score threshold S(Mi) < theta_decay (Algorithm 1, §3.2.1-3.2.2). retrieval=EMBEDDINGS;RANKING: cosine similarity Ei between memory vector and current-task vector, selection by composite Utility Score (§3.2.1). mide_lectura=NO (matches F_screening, no RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO; §5.2 promises 'retrieval latency' as a Memory Metric but Table 1 does not actually report it). alcance=TAREA: a single long-running task (a multi-week software-project plan, 500 turns, §5.1), no explicit cross-session framing. fidelidad_procedencia=SI: a dedicated 'Contradiction Rate' metric measures when the agent's output conflicts with previously stated facts/instructions (§5.2) -- consistency between recalled and previously stated content, central to the paper's title. F=WRITE;CONSOLIDACION;COSTO;NEGATIVO (NEGATIVO added vs F_screening: the paper explicitly documents the 'self-degradation' failure of the naive 'All-Add' strategy as a central finding, Fig.2, §5.3 -- negative evidence about naive memory management, though the evidence's rigor is doubtful, see RECONSIDERAR). benchmarks=NINGUNO: a self-built simulated task, no standard academic benchmark (§5.1). metricas=EXITO(Task Completion Rate)+COSTO-TOKENS(Average Token Cost per turn)+LATENCIA(Average Latency per turn)+OTRA(Consistency Score, Contradiction Rate) -- Table 1. evidencia_tipo=CUALITATIVA: since Appendix A shows at least Figure 2 was generated with hardcoded formulas (not measured from a real system), and the text itself calls its experiments 'simulated', it does not meet the real ABLATION/BENCHMARK-E2E bar (gate rule 2: 'demos and examples = CUALITATIVA'); see RECONSIDERAR. handoff=NO: memory for a single continuous task/agent, no explicit handoff protocol between distinct sessions or agents. plan_estado=NO: MemoryEntry objects are atomic interactions (message/tool-call/observation), not a dedicated plan/progress object.

title: Zep: A Temporal Knowledge Graph Architecture for Agent Memory
benchmarks: Deep Memory Retrieval (DMR, from MemGPT), LongMemEval
fallos_mitigaciones: Temporally overlapping contradictions between new and existing edges (stale/superseded facts) mitigated by LLM-driven edge invalidation prioritizing the transactional timeline T' (new info wins), §2.2.3. The paper also self-critiques the DMR benchmark's own limitations (ambiguous questions, small scale, poor enterprise representativeness, §4.2), motivating the harder LongMemEval evaluation.
cita: Rasmussen et al. (2025). Zep: A Temporal Knowledge Graph Architecture for Agent Memory.
notes: mem_tipos EPISODICA;SEMANTICA: explicit dual episode-subgraph (raw messages, non-lossy) + semantic-entity-subgraph (resolved entities/facts), directly mirrors 'psychological models of human memory... episodic memory... semantic memory' (§2). representacion=GRAFO;VECTOR: temporal knowledge graph G=(N,E,phi) with 3 tiers (episode/semantic/community subgraphs, §2) + entity/fact/community names embedded for cosine search (§2.2.1, §2.3). operaciones=WRITE;CONSOLIDACION;ACTUALIZACION: episode ingestion + entity/fact extraction (WRITE, §2.1-2.2); community subgraph built via community detection + iterative map-reduce summarization (CONSOLIDACION, §2.3); temporal extraction and EDGE INVALIDATION -- 'the system employs an LLM to compare new edges against semantically related existing edges to identify potential contradictions...invalidates the affected edges' (ACTUALIZACION, §2.2.3). trigger=EVENTO-DETERMINISTA;CHECKPOINT: ingestion per episode/message; 'periodic community refreshes remain necessary' (CHECKPOINT, §2.3). retrieval=EMBEDDINGS;GREP-ARCHIVOS;GRAFO;RANKING: cosine semantic similarity, Okapi BM25 full-text, breadth-first graph search (§3.1); rerankers RRF/MMR/cross-encoder/episode-mentions/node-distance (§3.2). mide_lectura=SI (matches F_screening): DMR and LongMemEval accuracy explicitly measured (Table1-3). alcance=SESION: DMR is 5-session conversations; LongMemEval has an explicit 'cross-session information synthesis' category. fidelidad_procedencia=SI: bi-temporal model with tvalid/tinvalid/t'created/t'expired tracking fact validity over time, LLM-driven contradiction detection and edge invalidation (§2.2.3). F=RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO;FIDELIDAD;COSTO (matches F_screening, confirmed). evidencia_tipo=BENCHMARK-E2E(Table1-3)+MEDICION-COSTO(latency/tokens, Table2) -- no explicit internal component ablation of Zep's own modules was found in the reviewed text. handoff=CONTENIDO: facts/entities persist and are retrieved across sessions ('cross-session information synthesis', Abstract).

title: Cogito, ergo sum: A Neurobiologically-Inspired Cognition-Memory-Growth System for Code Generation
benchmarks: HumanEval, HumanEval-ET, EvalPlus, MBPP, MBPP-ET, APPS, xCodeEval, CodeContest
fallos_mitigaciones: Prior external-storage approaches 'either store the complete responses directly...or summarize all the content before storing...requir[ing] excessive storage space or result[ing] in content loss due to summarization' (§1); mitigated by Cogito's region-specific hippocampus-inspired storage (different content types retained per CA region, tokenizer-compression only at CA4).
cita: Li et al. (2025). Cogito, ergo sum: A Neurobiologically-Inspired Cognition-Memory-Growth System for Code Generation.
notes: mem_tipos=EPISODICA;PROCEDIMENTAL: CA1/CA3 store per-attempt responses and code-version+error-traceback history (episodic records of past attempts, §3.3); the Super-Role's accumulated cross-role 'knowledge and cognitive skills' constitute reusable problem-solving strategy (procedural). representacion=DOCS-ARCHIVOS: plain-text/code stored in named hippocampus-inspired regions (CA1/CA2/CA3/CA4) with numeric importance-score/weight metadata (Fig.2); no concrete vector-embedding-based or graph-based retrieval mechanism is described despite the paper's qualitative claim of 'quick retrieval in similar tasks' -- hence retrieval is marked NA. operaciones=WRITE;ADMISION;CONSOLIDACION: responses stored per CA region (WRITE); Fig.2 shows candidate content filtered by importance-score x weight against a MIN threshold before being retained (ADMISION); CA4 'utilize a tokenizer to reduce the size of the stored content, optimizing memory space' (CONSOLIDACION, §3.3). trigger=PRESUPUESTO: importance-score x weight vs MIN threshold gates retention (Fig.2, §3.4). retrieval=NA: no concrete IR mechanism (embeddings/grep/graph/ranking) is described. mide_lectura=SI (matches F_screening): Table3 ablation 'Cogito w/o Super-Role' (without carrying accumulated memory forward) shows the largest performance drop (69.33% vs 90.24% full), demonstrating the utility of reused memory. alcance=TAREA: the hippocampus-like memory operates within a SINGLE question's Debugger->Coder->Planner->Super-Role pipeline (Algorithm1). multiagente=SI: explicit multi-agent system where memory 'acts as a communication bridge across different groups, facilitating the transfer of knowledge and strategies' (§3.2). F=RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO;CONSOLIDACION;COSTO (matches F_screening, confirmed). handoff=CONTENIDO: the Super-Role's accumulated experience is explicitly a 'communication bridge across different groups' (§3.2) between the Debugger/Coder/Planner role-agents. plan_estado=NO: the Planner's output ('Plan') is stored as one type of role-experience content, not a meta-level task-progress tracker.

title: Multi-LLM Orchestration for High-Quality Code Generation: Exploiting Complementary Model Strengths
benchmarks: HumanEval-X, EffiBench-X, HumanEval-Pack
fallos_mitigaciones: 'No single LLM dominates across all programming languages, all problem categories, or all stages' (a model strong at Python generation may be weak at Rust or at debugging, Table1); mitigated by per-stage, per-category memory-informed routing (Table3, Observation1-2). Brute-force multi-model search is computationally prohibitive; mitigated by capping the candidate pool to top-k=5 ranked LLMs per the memory ranking (§3.2, sensitivity analysis §6.2).
cita: Chen et al. (2025). Multi-LLM Orchestration for High-Quality Code Generation: Exploiting Complementary Model Strengths.
notes: mem_tipos=PROCEDIMENTAL: the 'Memory module' is a ranking matrix of which LLM performs best per (language, category) -- reusable strategic know-how for task routing, not conversational/episodic content (§3.2-3.6). representacion=DOCS-ARCHIVOS: a structured offline-profiled ranking table/matrix indexed by language x category (Fig.3); the closest closed-vocab fit though not literally free text -- the vocabulary has no dedicated 'table/matrix' token. operaciones=WRITE;ACTUALIZACION: initial construction 'from offline profiling data' (WRITE) that is explicitly 'updatable as new models/versions become available' (ACTUALIZACION, Abstract, §1). trigger=CHECKPOINT: memory is built via a distinct OFFLINE profiling phase before deployment, not during live task execution (Abstract) -- closest to a periodic/scheduled batch process. retrieval=RANKING: 'each agent consults its Memory to select the most suitable LLMs' via the profiled ranking lookup, §3.2. mide_lectura=SI (matches F_screening): Table3 compares per-stage/per-category memory-informed routing against majority-voting and single-model baselines, measuring the improvement from consulting the memory (Observation1-2, §3.1). alcance=TAREA: the memory is consulted per individual coding problem/task at inference time. multiagente=SI: explicit 4-agent orchestration system (Categorization/Generation/Debugging/Refinement) where the Memory module is 'Used by Agent B/C/D' (Fig.3). F=WRITE;RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO;COSTO;MULTIAGENTE (MULTIAGENTE added vs F_screening for the dedicated multi-agent architecture where Memory is explicitly shared across the 4 agents, Fig.3). handoff=CONTENIDO: the profiled ranking memory (content) is consulted/shared by the Generation, Debugging, and Refinement agents within the same pipeline execution (Fig.3). plan_estado=NO.

title: Improving LLM-Based Fault Localization with External Memory and Project Context
benchmarks: Defects4J
fallos_mitigaciones: Existing LLM-based FL methods (SoapFL, AutoFL) 'depend on complex multi-agent systems or intricate LLM tool usage' and their effectiveness significantly declines on complex projects lacking project-specific context (e.g. Closure, Fig.1, §III); mitigated by MemFL's static+dynamic external memory injecting project-specific knowledge directly into a simplified 3-step pipeline (§III-IV).
